Title: Metaheuristic-driven optimization of ensemble deep learning model for image manipulation classification
Abstract: Detecting image manipulations, particularly in double Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG)-compressed images, remains a critical challenge in digital forensics due to the repetitive compression chain introduced by social media platforms. These processes obscure manipulation traces, complicating detection tasks. This study addresses these challenges by proposing a metaheuristic-optimized ensemble deep learning (DL) model that combines Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Network (SE-ResNet50; fine-grained spatial detail extraction), Squeeze-and-Excitation Dense Convolutional Network (SE-DenseNet121; efficient feature reuse), Squeeze-and-Excitation Inception architecture (SE-InceptionV3; multi-scale feature extraction), and Vision Transformer (ViT-Base/32; long-range dependency and global relationship analysis). Ensemble weights were optimized using five metaheuristic techniques: Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Bayesian Optimization (BO), Differential Evolution (DE), and Genetic Algorithm (GA), with GA achieving the best optimization results. Experiments on three benchmark datasets—Break Our Steganographic System Base (BOSSBase), 10-class Mini-ImageNet (ImageNet-Mini10K), Uncompressed Colour Image Database (UCID)—across multiple JPEG quality factors (75, 85, 95) showed that the proposed ensemble model significantly outperformed individual DL models and traditional equal-weighted ensembles in terms of accuracy and F1-scores, while exhibiting strong cross-dataset generalization under domain shifts. The results highlight the effectiveness of metaheuristic-optimized ensemble learning for robust and scalable manipulation classification, making the proposed framework particularly suitable for offline forensic analysis scenarios involving realistic JPEG compression chains.

Title: A CNN-RNN Dual-Stage Assamese Speech Synthesis and Recognition Framework Using Common Voice Corpus
Abstract: Speech processing for low-resource languages remains a important challenge in the field of artificial intelligence due to limited datasets, linguistic diversity and model generalization limitations. This study includes Text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-text (STT) transformation in unified process. With a short-time objective intelligibility (STOI) score of 0.82, the TTS component uses a hybrid CNN-RNN model for feature extraction and temporal modelling with waveform reconstruction using the Griffin-Lim algorithm. A CNN-RNN architecture optimized with CTCs loss is incorporated into the STT module which results in a word error rate (WER) of 0.20. The proposed system shows the high transcription accuracy while attaining good alignment between source and synthesised speech. This study offers a method to enhance speech technologies for underrepresented languages that can be easily replicated and scaled. The results shows that CNN-RNN architectures have considerable potential for efficient, end-to-end speech synthesis and recognition which will paved the way towards universally accessible digital communication and multilingual systems for AI.

Title: MHDMC-Net: Multi-Head Dynamic Multi-Scale Convolutional Network with Adaptive Gated Mechanism for Crop Disease and Pest Detection
Abstract: Accurate and timely detection of crop diseases and pests is crucial for ensuring global food security and reducing agricultural losses. However, current deep learning approaches for crop disease detection face three critical limitations: (1) insufficient extraction of multi-scale discriminative features for disease symptoms of varying sizes, (2) ineffective feature fusion mechanisms that fail to capture complementary information across different receptive fields, and (3) limited attention to subtle pathological regions in complex agricultural environments. To address these challenges, we propose MHDMC-Net, a novel framework integrating three key innovations matching these limitations: (1) a Multi-Head Dynamic Multi-scale Convolutional (MHDMC) module that employs parallel multi-scale depth-wise convolutions with dynamic weight generation for adaptive feature extraction, (2) an Adaptive Multi-scale Gated Linear Unit (AM-GLU) that leverages gating mechanisms to selectively fuse multi-scale features, and (3) a Lightweight Attention mechanism that efficiently highlights disease-relevant regions with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on a large-scale agricultural dataset containing 22 disease and pest categories demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of our integrated framework.

Title: Real-Time Emergency Detection via Multimodal Fusion of Acoustic and Emotional Features
Abstract: This paper presents a new real-time emergency detection system that recognises emergency signals from noise using speech enhancement, automatic speech recognition (ASR) representations, and emotion modelling. The emergency detection system relied on time domain speech enhancement methods to improve the intelligibility of the audio signal for ASR. The intermediate representations produced by the ASR models (Wav2Vec2 and Whisper) take advantage of the richness of speech to encode connectivity and meaning. Emotion detection is performed using transformer-based models to predict urgency and emotion. Experimental results show improvements in performance over baseline systems developed using traditional methods that processed the raw audio with or without processing the text in noise. Additionally, the use of multimodal features allows this system to detect emergencies at low signal-to-noise ratios. We also explore keyword-based least impactful emergency detection as a quick response capability that can be used alongside the machine learning model. The designed pipelines can also produce low-latency and near-realtime systems that will favourably support emergency responses on mobile and edge devices. Future work includes expanding the system to detect more types of emergencies and potentially support multilingual speech recognition.

Title: A Spatiotemporal CNN-LSTM Framework for Forecasting Crop Disease Progression
Abstract: The majority of deep learning methods used in plant pathology are based on the classification of the static images and do not consider the way diseases change with time. This limitation impairs premature diagnosis and accurate severity determination, in particular in the field, dynamic farm conditions. To overcome this, we suggest a spatiotemporal deep learning model that brings together a convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for image extraction with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network on temporal sequence modeling. This hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture studies the consecutive images in order to capture the progression of disease symptoms. Real time crop data are available only in small datasets, and time-varying datasets do not involve real-time. With scarcity, we present a synthetic sequence generation approach that simulates the disease development out of still pictures with alpha blending. The individual frames are run in a pre-trained inceptionV3 model to generate strong feature vectors, which the LSTM then use to learn the temporal patterns. The proposed approach is demonstrated to work with the publicly available rice leaf disease dataset constantly achieves higher performance than a state-of-the-art static CNN baseline in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. By incorporating temporal information, this framework offers a more credible and informative instrument of predictive disease surveillance in precision agriculture.

Title: Enhancing ASR Performance in Noisy Environments Via Bridging Approach
Abstract: In this research work, we propose a method for noise-robust automatic speech recognition systems in the presence of non-stationary noise, specifically background speaker noise. This proposed technique will be extremely useful for any ASR system/application that needs to be accessed in an outdoor environment. Technically, we focus on the integration of speech enhancement (SE) and automatic speech recognition (ASR) to improve the performance of a pre-trained ASR model in noisy conditions. We employ a technique called observation addition (OA) where the original noisy signal is added to the SE version of itself using a weighting approach and then subsequently passed through the ASR model. We tested this approach using the Google FLEURS dataset. In this dataset, each speech sample is evaluated at five different SNR levels. Using an attention-based deep learning network, we estimate the SNR from the noisy samples. The SNR is then mapped to the best OA coefficient, which is then used for assigning weights to noisy and enhanced signal. Our proposed approach improves ASR performance across all SNR levels. At lower SNRs, it gives a 3.1% absolute gain at 3 dB when using a fixed OA coefficient for all utterances from a general domain.

Title: Early Stage Parkinsonian Disorder Detection Using Machine Learning Classifiers and Neuro Motor Feature Analysis
Abstract: Parkinson disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease whose diagnosis is not an easy task because of subjective clinical examination and late onset of motor symptoms. Immediate and correct diagnosis is imperative in the prompt intervention and better patient outcomes. This paper introduces a machine learning-based system of earlystage Parkinsonian disorder detection with neuro-motor voice features. There was a publicly available biomedical voice dataset (22 acoustic features, 195 samples) in which each sample was classified as either Parkinson disease or healthy control. Some of the supervised machine learning classifier such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, Extra Trees and XGBoost were tested. In order to further improve classification performance and minimize falsenegative predictions, a hybrid stacking ensemble model was set forward that uses XGBoost and Extra Trees as base learners and Logistic Regression as a meta-learner. Adequate preprocessing methods like stratified data splitting and feature standardization were used. The results of the experiment show that the proposed hybrid stacking model is better than single classifiers; with an accuracy of 98.31 percent and is able to remove false negative cases of the Parkinson disease. The results suggest the usefulness of ensemble learning in addressing the issue of class imbalance and enhancing diagnostic accuracy, which means voice-based machine learning models might be proposed as a useful decision-supporting instrument to detect Parkinson disease at an early stage. Further research will be conducted on subject-independent validation and multimodal neuro-motor data integration to improve on its generalizability.

Title: Enhancing Pre-Eclampsia Screening Through Machine Learning and Multi-Source Data Integration
Abstract: Pre-eclampsia remains one of the most severe pregnancy complications, tormenting the maternal and neonatal outcomes all over the world. In order to mitigate this risk, clinicians need risk-stratification instruments that are not only rapid but also evidence-based. This paper presents a predictive framework in modules that would combine clinical, biochemical, and biosensor data into a single and clear risk estimate. It consists of five modules which are inter-relational as follows: (1) acquisition and harmonization of multi-source data, (2) preprocessing and feature construction, (3) supervised machine-learning modelling, (4) clinical risk stratification and decision support, and (5) independent validation and performance monitoring. The Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting (XG Boost) models are crossvalidated and hyper-optimized to ensure strong discrimination and calibration. Individual risk type categories are thus created and incorporated to the clinician dashboards effortlessly and the patients are given brief educational information. The proven system helps to detect high-risk pregnancies at early stages and implement timely interventions, including low-dose aspirin and enhanced monitoring. Demonstrating that machine learning can be directly introduced into obstetric practice, the framework shows that a data-driven approach can offer a practical mechanism to improve maternal safety and the initial diagnosis of pre-eclampsia through the synthesis of clinical records, laboratory data, and biosensor inputs.

Title: Postpartum Depression Detection Using Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Postpartum Depression (PPD) is an important issue in mental health among new mothers in the world at a rate of {1 0 - 2 0} percent. Timely intervention in PPD is the best option to live with good health outcomes as mother and child. The paper introduces an all-inclusive machine learning strategy to detect PPD based on 5,000 simulated maternal health records. In this paper, we apply and compare five single machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, and XGBoost and three ensemble learning strategies: Hard Voting, Soft Voting, and Stacking. The samples were trained considering {1 4} characteristics such as demographic data, pregnancy complications, delivery type, sleep patterns, and psychological symptoms. Outcomes show that the use of ensemble techniques and specifically Stacking has a better performance with a high accuracy of over 92%. XGBoost and random forest also performed well with minimum accuracy of 91% on an individual basis. The researchers find such major predictive characteristics as frequent sadness, loss of interest, sudden crying, and sleep deprivation. This study can help in the creation of automated PPD screening instruments that will help healthcare professionals to early detect and intervene with at-risk mothers.

Title: Prosody Disruptor for Voice Protection Against Unauthorized Speech Synthesis
Abstract: Recent advances in neural speech synthesis enable highly realistic speech generation, raising concerns about unauthorized voice impersonation. To prevent this, proactive voice protection introduces imperceptible perturbations into speech signals that hinder synthesis models from learning a target speaker's identity. However, many existing approaches rely on complex optimization procedures and multiple auxiliary models, resulting in high computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight prosody-driven voice protection method that disrupts prosodic cues used for speaker adaptation during neural speech synthesis training. The method simply perturbs pitch confidence and energy contours of the original waveform using a fixed pitch tracking model, enabling efficient and lightweight protection. Since prosodic features play a role in representing speaker identity, corrupting these cues reduces speaker similarity in synthesized speech while preserving perceptual quality. Experiments across multiple neural speech synthesis architectures demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves comparable protection performance while enabling a fourfold reduction in processing time.

Title: A Multi-stage Deep Learning and Clustering Framework for Early Parkinson’s Disease Risk Identification from Voice Biomarkers
Abstract: Early and accurate identification of Parkinson’s Disease (PD) risk seems to be an unmet challenge, particularly for diagnosing persons with sub clinical symptoms or those in early stages. Most of the existing frameworks for PD diagnosis rely on binary classification or predicting the severity of the disease by using Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) score, omitting nuanced risk gradation and failing to discover PD-like healthy subgroups essential for preventive medicine. The present work proposes a multi-stage framework, combining autoencoder-based latent feature extraction, 2-tier GMM-based hierarchical clustering and adaptive model fusion to differentiate between PD, healthy, and PD-like healthy groups using voice biomarkers based on Parkinson’s Disease Similarity Index (PDSI). The proposed framework is validated using 5-fold stratified cross validation on a clinically annotated dataset of 756 voice samples, significantly skewed towards PD-positive cases. Paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistical analysis are carried out against standard Random Forest and SVM baselines to investigate their selection correctly and reliably. The proposed model achieves a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.957, PR-AUC of 0.986 and F1-score of 0.945 with statistically significant improvements over ensemble and margin-based classifiers (). The hierarchical approach uniquely enables detection of “PD-like healthy” individuals, thus supporting graded risk scores that can drive personalized early intervention strategies. The findings highlight PDSI as a valuable, scalable and clinically pertinent instrument for early diagnosis of PD and risk assessment and hence it creates new avenues for population wide preventative screening and incorporation into telemedicine systems.

Title: Promises/Manual Labor Paradox: The Accountability Style of On-Site Validation in Microbiology Laboratory Automation
Abstract: This study investigates the role of validation reports in legitimizing laboratory automation through artificial intelligence and robotic systems in clinical microbiology. Based on a qualitative analysis of thirty reports authored by expert microbiologists between 2016 and 2023 across eight countries—Australia, Belgium, China, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom—we examine how technological promises are made accountable. Building on Science and Technology Studies (STS) and the sociology of expectations, we approach these reports not as mere sources of “objective” information, but as instruments of accountability that link future-oriented promises with conventional laboratory practices—particularly manual labor. We argue that they embody a distinct accountability style, diverging from an ethics-driven approach often found in influential STS contributions. Automation promises—largely framed through managerial values—actualize their contractual character when articulated through metrics designed to assess satisfactory performance. Yet numerical results alone are insufficient to legitimize devices that mostly match the performance of manual labor. A paradox emerges: while manual labor serves as the gold standard against which automation is assessed, for automation to be validated, manual labor must be discursively problematized as an “entrenched habit”—a hindrance to addressing contemporary healthcare challenges. We argue this constitutes an essential feature of the validation accountability style.

Title: A Reliable Bayesian Deep Learning Framework With Rectified Flow for Fault Diagnosis Under Limited Data
Abstract: Despite advancements in intelligent fault diagnosis, the lack of sufficient training data remains a critical barrier in real-world industrial scenarios. To tackle this issue, numerous deep generative models have been proposed. However, existing methods often exhibit suboptimal generation quality, slow speed, and resource inefficiency when generating multi-class samples. Moreover, although the generated data can enhance the robustness of diagnostic models, it cannot ensure well-calibrated confidence estimates, and the reliability of predictions remains a persistent concern. To address these challenges in a unified manner, we propose a Bayesian Deep Learning Framework with a Rectified Flow-based Model (BDRF). Rectified Flow is introduced as the backbone for high-quality and efficient data augmentation by transforming Gaussian noise into industrial data distributions via optimized ordinary differential equations. We further incorporate classifier-free guidance algorithm to enable conditional multi-class generation within a single model. To bridge the gap between data-driven generation and domain-specific knowledge, large language models and text embeddings are leveraged to extract semantic information from fault descriptions as conditions, enhancing generation realism and interpretability. Finally, to remedy the issue of misaligned confidence, BDRF employs a Bayesian diagnostic classifier using the last-layer Laplace Approximation. Comprehensive experiments conducted on a benchmark simulation dataset and a real-world industrial dataset demonstrate that BDRF integrates data augmentation and calibrated confidence, effectively advancing the automation of fault diagnosis processes by improving both prediction performance and reliability under limited data. Note to Practitioners - In industries where automation is increasingly crucial, intelligent fault diagnosis methods are vital to maintaining the efficiency, productivity, and reliability of operations. However, these methods often struggle due to limited data, leading to inaccurate predictions and uncalibrated confidence in diagnostic results. This research proposes a unified framework, BDRF, that tackles these two critical issues simultaneously. BDRF introduces a Rectified Flow-based generation module and leverages large language models to incorporate domain-specific knowledge from fault descriptions, improving both the quality and efficiency of data generation for training diagnostic models. Additionally, a Bayesian diagnostic classifier is employed to enhance the reliability of predictions, thereby mitigating the risk of overconfidence or underconfidence in fault detection. Based on our experiments, BDRF demonstrates strong applicability in sectors with limited industrial fault data, such as condition monitoring for complex machinery including chemical processes and multi-phase flow systems. Furthermore, BDRF's ability to generate high-quality data and enhance classification reliability in resource-constrained environments makes it an effective instrument for improving automation in other domains like maintenance, healthcare, and finance.

Title: Machine Learning for Bearing Health Monitoring: A Controlled Experimental Benchmark Using Vibration-Based Statistical Features
Abstract: Reliable condition monitoring of rolling element bearings is essential for improving machinery availability and reducing unplanned downtime. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been widely applied for vibration-based bearing fault diagnosis; however, reported performance is often difficult to interpret due to variations in datasets, operating conditions, and validation protocols. This study presents a controlled experimental benchmark evaluating three classical ML algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)—for vibration-based fault classification of cylindrical roller bearings. Experiments were conducted on SKF N204 bearings using a machinery fault simulator under three bearing conditions (healthy, outer race defect, and roller defect) at four rotational speeds (100–400 RPM). Artificial defects were introduced using electrical discharge machining (EDM), and vibration signals were acquired using a National Instruments data acquisition system. Root mean square (RMS), kurtosis, and crest factor were extracted as interpretable statistical features, resulting in a dataset of 119 feature samples. Model performance was evaluated using stratified train–validation–test splits, with k-fold cross-validation applied uniformly across all classifiers, including the ANN, to ensure fair comparison. Under the present laboratory conditions, the ANN exhibited the most consistent performance across validation and testing, while SVM and k-NN showed slightly lower validation accuracy but comparable testing behavior. The results demonstrate that high classification accuracy can be achieved using simple statistical features and classical ML models in a controlled setting. However, the findings should be interpreted as upper-bound diagnostic performance under laboratory conditions, rather than direct indicators of industrial-scale generalization. The study provides a transparent benchmarking reference and highlights the trade-off between interpretability, data efficiency, and classification performance in bearing health monitoring applications.

Title: Cross-Domain Detection of AI-Generated Songs: Benchmarking Encoder Models on Bahasa Indonesia
Abstract: In recent years, advances in deep learning have significantly improved our ability to detect highly realistic AIgenerated song content. This progress has raised concerns about copyright protection, cultural authenticity, and the spread of misleading content. Despite growing global attention, there are still very few research studies related to this domain, especially in low-resource languages such as Bahasa Indonesia, due to the lack of appropriate datasets. To address this gap, we compiled and gathered a dataset of Indonesian songs collected from publicly available sources on social media, consisting of both real performances and AI-generated modifications, reflecting real situations in which AI-generated content is usually shared. We investigate our detection strategies by comparing several detection techniques using established audio encoders such as AST, Wave2Vec2, and WavLM. These models are then evaluated on unseen and different domain datasets. This is a crucial challenge given the rapid growth of AI music generation technologies. This experiment highlights both techniques and offers new insights into cross-generator detection, as well as dataset design and model robustness, which are important for protecting musical integrity in the era of generative AI.

Title: Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition for Indonesian Speech Using CNN and GoogLeNet
Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems often experience significant performance degradation in noisy real-world environments, particularly for resource-constrained languages such as Indonesian where training data is still relatively scarce. This study aims to develop a noise-robust end-to-end ASR system by quantitatively comparing two different encoder architectures: a standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a complex multi-scale GoogLeNet-Attention architecture. Both models are trained end-to-end using Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss on the Indonesian Common Voice dataset, which is rigorously enriched with non-stationary environmental noise from the ESC-50 dataset at various Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs). Experimental results show that the standard CNN architecture significantly outperforms the GoogLeNet-Attention model, achieving a Word Error Rate (WER) of 45.45% compared to 51.21%. Furthermore, the CNN model proved to be significantly more computationally efficient, requiring approximately 35% less training time per epoch. These findings suggest that for low-resource tasks characterized by high acoustic variability, welltuned deep CNNs with increased capacity offer a superior balance between robustness and efficiency compared to complex multi-scale architectures.

Title: Age Estimation from Speech Using Whisper-based Speaker Representations
Abstract: Automatic age estimation from speech is a challenging paralinguistic task due to subtle age-related acoustic cues and variability in recording conditions across corpora. In this work, we investigate age estimation using speaker representations. Our approach employs an automatic speaker verification (ASV)adapted Whisper-small encoder as a fixed feature extractor and trains a regression head on top of the resulting embeddings. Experiments on multiple corpora demonstrate that ASV-oriented Whisper representations consistently achieve superior performance and outperform open-source self-supervised learning (SSL)-based baselines when evaluated across heterogeneous datasets recorded under diverse acoustic conditions, including TIMIT, AgeVoxCeleb, NIST SRE10, and RusIVR. We further validate the results using a balanced evaluation protocol on AgeVoxCeleb and RusIVR, where the proposed system achieves an MAE of 6.35 years and 81% accuracy within a 10 year tolerance, outperforming both open-source baselines and an anonymized commercial system. To analyze potential speaker-identity leakage, we introduce VoiceBiometricAge, a new dataset, and conduct both qualitative and quantitative representation analyses. The results indicate that the learned age projection substantially reduces speaker separability. Finally, duration-based experiments confirm that the proposed method remains effective for short utterances, achieving strong accuracy with only 5-7 seconds of speech.

Title: Composite Algorithm for Autism Spectrum Disorder Early Identification
Abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that requires early diagnosis to facilitate timely intervention and care. Herein, we present an analysis of a publicly accessible dataset accessed through the ASD Tests app created by the Nelson Marlborough Institute of Technology. The dataset is comprised of self-reported answers of every age group adolescent and adults gathered using standardized screening instruments like Q-CHAT-10 and AQ10, however the experiments were performed on adolescent and adult's dataset. Preprocessing steps involved the removal of duplicates, missing value handling, and normalization of data to achieve the best model performance. A wide range of machine learning models was used, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), AdaBoostM1, Logit Boost, and ensemble models like Voting, Stacking, and Boosting. The performance metrics used for evaluation were accuracy, precision, recall, F-measure, and ROC-AUC, supplemented with 5-fold cross-validation. SVM acquired high accuracy of 98%. This research provides robustness and cross validation model confirms the model stability, and highlights the potential for remote and accessible screening. This research open the pathway for early and scalable intervention.

Title: IoT-Driven Intelligent Water Fountain Controlled by MHRISCNN Algorithm for Music Therapy
Abstract: As per ancient age water fountains have been used for multipurpose entertainment events like laser shows at statue of unity Ahmadabad, Vradavan garden, Mysore and Akshardham etc. Design such fountains becomes the best opportunity for interdisciplinary learners. It's difficult to design the physical structure and control system of a fountain with water jet dancing effects with light which change the mood swing of a psychological patient. This paper gives ideas about indoor fountains in educational institutions and hospitals to target psychological patients to heal the mind and for students to concentrate on specific mind states for study. Proposed model work on IoT and modified machine learning algorithms. It captures emotions and facial expressions of patients(Fountain Viewer) and detects mood. Accordingly it will select musical instruments from the playlist as per mood. It converts the signals to create patterns which are input for solenoid valves and light systems. Solenoid activity and light systems will generate different water jet dancing patterns and light glowing patterns for different mood based scenarios. For the healing process, body and mind response with music therapy is a new area. The challenging issues here are which ragas to listen to, when to listen and how much time to listen. Feature extraction techniques from digital signal processing are adopted to address the particular raga with notes and swaras. Machine learning algorithms are used to classify the type of raga for a particular disease. Performance of classification of ragas is done using various classifier algorithms. MHRISCNN Algorithm (Mind Healing Raga Instrument Selection Convolution Neural Network) is being proposed which will select a particular Raga and instrument based on the person's mood at that time. This will help any person to reduce his or her stress who is near a fountain which in turn improves his health.

Title: Leveraging Text and Image Information for Ovarian Tumors Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
Abstract: Accurate segmentation of ovarian tumors in ultrasound images is essential for early diagnosis and treatment planning. However, this task remains challenging due to the inherent limitations of ultrasound imaging, such as noise, shadowing, low contrast, and blurred tumor boundaries. Furthermore, the large variability in tumor shape, size, and position across patients further complicates traditional segmentation methods. Most existing deep learning approaches rely solely on visual features, overlooking the potential benefits of incorporating semantic information. In this study, we propose a novel multimodal segmentation framework that explicitly integrates both visual and textual information. Our architecture is based on a UNet-style backbone enhanced with a pretrained VGG16 encoder and a Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast (SPPF) block for improved multi-scale feature learning. The key contribution lies in the integration of Image-Text Matching (ITM) modules into the segmentation pipeline, enabling deep cross-modal interaction between image features and semantic tumor descriptions. Additionally, we introduce a lightweight captioning module that automatically generates textual descriptions from ultrasound images, allowing the model to be trained even when manual annotations are unavailable. To further enhance performance, we employ a combination of loss functions including Tversky, Weighted Binary Cross Entropy (WBCE), and Structure Similarity (SSIM), aiming to balance precision, recall, and structural similarity. Experimental results on the OTU_2d dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving 90.16% Dice, 82.05% IoU, 90.23% Recall, 91.12% Precision.

Title: Robust and Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Early Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease with XGBoost
Abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a progressive and frequently asymptomatic condition that impacts millions globally, resulting in significant health issues if not identified promptly. Timely and precise prediction is essential for facilitating prompt clinical intervention and alleviating the burden of renal failure. This paper presents a robust and clinically interpretable machine learning system for chronic kidney disease prediction, incorporating advanced data preparation, ensemble learning, and explainable AI methodologies. Missing values in clinical data are managed with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to produce realistic synthetic samples while maintaining feature distributions. Class imbalance, prevalent in chronic kidney disease datasets, is addressed by the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), facilitating impartial model training. The ensemble classifier, XGBoost, is refined by hyperparameter tuning and assessed using stringent 5-fold cross-validation on a merged dataset of internal (UCI CKD) and external clinical records, attaining 100 percent accuracy internally and 99 percent accuracy overall. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is utilized for model interpretability, pinpointing significant predictors such as hemoglobin, serum creatinine, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which correspond with clinically acknowledged risk factors. The findings indicate that the suggested paradigm offers both superior predictive accuracy and transparent, reliable insights for doctors. This methodology enhances cutting-edge CKD prediction by integrating high precision, generalizability, and interpretability, providing a pragmatic instrument for early illness identification and preventive healthcare administration.

Title: An Explainability-Aware Transformer Framework for Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification Using MRI
Abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging is one of the most commonly used neuro-oncology imaging modalities, which is a non-invasive mode of imaging and helps in detecting brain abnormalities in an effective way. Earlier researchers have demonstrated that brain tumor segmentation and classification can be effectively performed using deep learning techniques. Existing studies are primarily aimed at increasing prediction accuracy and provide insignificant consideration to model interpretability, limiting their practical application in clinical practice. To address this limitation, this research presents a two-stage explainable deep learning model, which combines transformer-based segmentation with an ensemble classification model that is consistent in explanations. The first stage introduces Swin-DS-HAFUNetv2, an enhanced transformer-based segmentation architecture that integrates hierarchical Swin Transformer encoders, refined hierarchical attention fusion, a contextual bottleneck transformer, and multi-scale deep supervision to improve tumor localization in T1-weighted MRI, particularly under low-contrast and irregular morphological conditions. The second stage includes the ECWMEv2 ensemble classifier, which integrates a perturbation analysis based on Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) to systematically assess the consistency and clinical significance of visual explanations for candidate models. Only those architectures that exhibit stable and pathology-consistent explanations, such as ConvNeXt, Swin Transformer, and EVA02, are stored and merged by means of explanation-weighted soft voting with XGBoost-based meta-learning. Experimental evaluation on the BRISC2025 benchmark dataset indicates that Swin-DS-HAFUNetv2 has a mean Dice coefficient of 0.9782 and Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8656, with ECWMEv2 having a classification accuracy of 0.9917 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9867. The mean Grad-CAM IoU of 0.692 reflects uniform and anatomically significant consistency of attention to tumor regions. These results demonstrate that the integration of explanation stability as a fundamental design principle significantly improves model robustness and interpretability to provide a methodologically validated and benchmark-level framework for future studies of multimodal and clinically oriented brain tumor analysis systems.

Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Enhanced SVM Model
Abstract: This paper has introduced a Hybrid Machine Learning architecture on which the Enhanced SVM model predicts cardiovascular diseases with high accuracy. The proposed system combines both hybrid feature selection and kernel optimization methods to obtain high diagnostic accuracy and strength. Based on the Cleveland Heart Disease data, the model has high performance in terms of accuracy of 96.4, precision of 96.0 and AUC of 97.8 when compared to traditional classifiers, which include: Logistic Regression, KNN, and Random Forest. The methodology focuses on preprocessing of data, balanced sampling and hybrid feature optimization to minimize noise and bias that improves stability of predictivity. The model is tested experimentally to be able to separate healthy and diseased patients with misclassification occurring at a minimum level. The suggested hybrid design is a scalable and valid diagnostic instrument that can be used in smart health systems. The study forms groundwork on future advances in predictive cardiology and data-driven healthcare intelligence based on AI.

Title: Detecting Sugarcane Leaf Diseases using InceptionV3 Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: Sugarcane is an essential commercial crop whose productivity and quality are profoundly influenced by foliar diseases, including red rot, smut, and yellow leaf disease. Timely and precise identification of these diseases is essential to mitigate economic losses and promote sustainable farming practices. This research presents an automated method for detecting sugarcane leaf diseases using the InceptionV3 convolutional neural network (CNN). A total of 6,748 high-resolution leaf images including 11 categories of healthy and sick leaves were gathered, resized to 299 × 299 pixels, and normalized to optimize model performance. Transfer learning using the pre-trained InceptionV3 model was used for effective feature extraction and precise classification. The proposed technique attained an overall accuracy of 99.92%, with precision, recall, and F1-score at 99.55%, indicating robustness across disease groups. The model's resilience was also confirmed in actual field situations, encompassing occlusion, various soil backgrounds, and varied lighting and weather influences. Statistical significance tests showed that performance enhancements were not attributable to chance (p < 0.05). The findings demonstrate that the InceptionV3-based model is a dependable, scalable, and efficient instrument for automated sugarcane disease identification, facilitating prompt intervention and enhancing precision agriculture.

Title: Speech Emotion Recognition Using Deep CNN-Bilstm with Attention Mechanism on EMO-DB Dataset
Abstract: This paper proposes a CNN-BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism for speech emotion recognition on the German EMO-DB corpus. The model classifies seven emotion categories and achieves a validation accuracy of 98.13%. Melspectrogram features are extracted using two convolutional blocks with 64 and 128 filters, followed by two bidirectional LSTM layers with 128 units to capture forward and backward temporal dependencies. An attention-based pooling strategy aggregates information across time instead of relying only on the final LSTM state, resulting in a 3.2% performance improvement over final-state pooling. To address the limited size of EMODB (535 utterances), eight-fold data augmentation is applied and validated through Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, a three-annotator perceptual study (κ=0.82,92 % agreement), and ablation experiments showing a 13 % improvement over non-augmented training. The model maintains over 84 % accuracy under white and babble noise at 10 dB SNR, achieves F1-scores above 0.97 for all emotion classes, and uses only 4.6 million parameters, making it computationally efficient compared to large transfer-learning models.

Title: Real-time marker-less needle tracking for CT-guided interventions using multiple RGB cameras
Abstract: Purpose: In CT-guided interventions, instrument tracking reduces patient risk while improving the overall outcome. Though useful, marker-based tracking systems suffer from occlusion, are complex to set up, and fail when needles deflect. A marker-less tracking system could overcome these challenges, enabling streamlined integration. Methods: We developed and evaluated a proof-of-concept system combining standard RGB cameras with a U-Net-ConvNeXt architecture for needle detection and tracking. We compiled a fully annotated dataset of 35,000 frames, spanning multiple needle types and scenarios. We evaluated tracking accuracy against state-of-the-art marker-based systems, utilizing an IR-based and an image-based system on static positioning, dynamic movement, and needle-deflection scenarios. Moreover, our marker-less system was evaluated using both known and unknown needle types. Results: Our proof-of-concept system demonstrated a 3D tracking error of 2.70±1.07 mm at 25 FPS with 3 cameras, outperforming ArUco marker-based tracking (5.29±1.85 mm). Tracking accuracy remained consistent for unknown needle types not included in the training data, suggesting strong generalization. The system maintained a 99.4 % needle-tip detection rate across all frames with robust performance during needle deflection, while marker-based systems failed under identical conditions. With only 2 cameras, the tracking error of our system increased modestly (4.81±2.38 mm). Conclusion: Our proof-of-concept demonstrates the feasibility of marker-less needle tracking, suggesting potential for clinically relevant accuracy, reliability, and reduced complexity while exhibiting robustness to needle deflection and varying needle appearances. These preliminary results indicate promising directions for future clinical development.

Title: PRAD-Hybrid CNN (PRADHC): A Deep Learning Model for Assisted Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer on MRI
Abstract: Background: Prostate cancer is a prevalent malignancy in males, with prostate MRI imaging as the primary diagnostic method. However, this method is subjective and can miss early-stage cancers, necessitating more efficient diagnostic techniques. Method: In this study, we introduced the PRAD-Hybrid CNN (Prostate Adenocarcinoma Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network, PRADHC) model, a novel amalgamation of EfficientNet and Residual Blocks, which was developed and validated on 1,528 MRI images from 64 patients. By strategically increasing the number of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layers in the EfficientNet architecture, our model improved the diagnostic accuracy inherent to the original EfficientNet. Additionally, the integration of Residual Networks (ResNet) successfully mitigated the gradient vanishing issue often encountered during the training of deeper models, thereby significantly enhancing training accuracy. This innovative model, thus, offers clinicians an efficacious tool for assisted diagnosis. Result: The PRADHC model, upon validation, achieved an accuracy of 99.34% and an AUC of 99.34%, a 4% improvement over the conventional EfficientNet. The baseline elementary CNN model achieved 95.72% accuracy and 96.74% AUC, which are still lower than the PRADHC model. Discussion: The superior performance of PRADHC can be attributed to the synergistic integration of EfficientNet’s multi-scale feature extraction and residual learning, which facilitates deeper network optimization without degradation. Compared with single-architecture CNN models, the hybrid design enhances robustness to MRI appearance variability and improves discrimination between malignant and non-significant prostate tissue. Conclusion: This study introduces a novel deep learning model specifically designed for automated prostate cancer diagnosis. This model aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, especially in the early stages of the disease. Such advancements have the potential to enhance the diagnostic proficiency of both radiologists and urologists, enabling more informed treatment planning. However, it is imperative to acknowledge that false-positive lesion detections remain a limitation of AI-assisted diagnostic tools. Nevertheless, this system can serve as a valuable supplementary instrument for radiologists in their diagnostic endeavors.

Title: Early Breast Cancer Detection Using an Advanced Deep Learning Neural Network Framework
Abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy afflicting American women; fortunately, mortality rates can be drastically reduced with early detection and prompt treatment. The high expense and radiation exposure of digital mammography with CE prevent its widespread usage, despite the fact that it outperforms ultrasound and conventional mammography in thick breast tissue in terms of accuracy. Early Breast Cancer Detection uses data pretreatment with Weiner Filtering and a region growth picture segmentation technique based on GSO. GSO ideally creates initial seed spots and threshold values. A hybrid strategy is used to increase feature extraction and forecast performance by combining traditional and deep learning methods. Introducing HitNet, a Hybrid Ternary RNN that uses ternary weights and activations, with a slope component in the activation functions to further improve accuracy and close the accuracy gap between full precision and quantised models. The suggested model is effective, as it obtains a precision of 94.06% when tested using a conventional RNN architecture. By merging state-of-the-art imaging analysis with hybrid neural network modelling, this method supplies a powerful instrument for early diagnosis of breast cancer, which has the ability to decrease breast cancer death rates and enhance diagnostic accuracy.

Title: Developing a Sinhala Speech Recognition System Using Whisper
Abstract: The demand for accurate and robust speech recognition in low-resource languages has increased significantly in recent years. Sinhala, despite being spoken by over 17 million people, remains underrepresented in Automatic Speech Recognition research due to the limited availability of annotated datasets and its linguistic complexity. This study presents the development of a Sinhala Automatic Speech Recognition system by fine-tuning OpenAI’s Whisper model on a curated and augmented Sinhala speech dataset. A combined dataset of 3078 clips (5.83 hours) was expanded to 12312 clips (23.32 hours) using multiple augmentation techniques. Fine-tuning was performed on individual datasets and their combinations, both with and without augmentation, to evaluate the impact of dataset diversity. Experimental results show that the zero-shot Whisper models performed very poorly on Sinhala. However, fine-tuning significantly improved performance. The Whisper medium model, trained on an augmented news-style custom dataset, achieved a Word Error Rate of 5%. These results confirm the importance of dataset quality, augmentation, and multi-source training for improving ASR in low-resource languages. Furthermore, a lightweight web interface was developed to enable real-time Sinhala speech-to-text transcription. This work demonstrates that fine-tuned multilingual ASR models can bridge the resource gap for Sinhala Language.

Title: FEMBA on the Edge: Physiologically-Aware Pre-Training, Quantization, and Deployment of a Bidirectional Mamba EEG Foundation Model on an Ultra-Low Power Microcontroller
Abstract: Objective: To enable continuous, long-term neuro-monitoring on wearable devices by overcoming the computational bottlenecks of Transformer-based Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models and the quantization challenges inherent to State-Space Models (SSMs). Methods: We present FEMBA, a bidirectional Mamba architecture pre-trained on over 21,000 hours of EEG. We introduce a novel Physiologically-Aware pre-training objective, consisting of a reconstruction with low-pass filtering, to prioritize neural oscillations over high-frequency artifacts. To address the activation outliers common in SSMs, we employ Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) to compress the model to 2-bit weights. The framework is deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power RISC-V microcontroller (GAP9) using a custom double-buffered memory streaming scheme. Results: The proposed low-pass pre-training improves downstream AUROC on TUAB from 0.863 to 0.893 and AUPR from 0.862 to 0.898 compared to the best contrastive baseline. QAT successfully compresses weights with negligible performance loss, whereas standard post-training quantization degrades accuracy by approximately 30%. The embedded implementation achieves deterministic real-time inference (1.70 s per 5 s window) and reduces the memory footprint by 74% (to ≈2 MB), achieving competitive accuracy with up to 27× fewer FLOPs than Transformer benchmarks. Conclusion: FEMBA demonstrates that Mamba-based foundation models can be effectively quantized and deployed on extreme-edge hardware without sacrificing the representation quality required for robust clinical analysis. Significance: This work establishes the first full-stack framework for deploying large-scale EEG foundation models on ultra-low-power wearables, facilitating continuous, SSM based monitoring for epilepsy and sleep disorders.

Title: A Novel Preprocessing Approach Applying Pairwise Differences of Opposite Samples for Improved Interpretability in Binary Medical Classification
Abstract: Interpretability is crucial for the clinical adoption of machine learning, as healthcare providers require transparent decision-making processes to trust predictive tools effectively. Traditional feature selection methods often struggle to capture subtle distinctions between patient subgroups, particularly in datasets with overlapping classes. To address this limitation, we propose the Pairwise Difference Filter (PDF) and its enhanced version, the directional Pairwise Difference Filter (dPDF). These preprocessing methods use margin-based instance selection to isolate 'hard examples' - patients from distinct clinical cohorts who share highly similar global phenotypic profiles. By anchoring feature extraction on these clinically ambiguous cases near the decision boundary, dPDF successfully identifies the subtle biomarkers responsible for true class separation. Evaluation across four medical datasets demonstrates that dPDF achieves competitive global performance (average accuracy: 74.63%, average rank: 2.00/6) among six established methods, while attaining leading accuracy (90.47%) on the primary MUSIC Med clinical dataset - outperforming techniques such as LASSO and Random Forest on complex clinical data. Furthermore, dPDF-generated feature rankings consistently align with clinical knowledge, isolating biologically plausible biomarkers rather than spurious variables associated with broad data divergence. This combination of competitive accuracy, intrinsic directional interpretability, and transparent methodology makes dPDF particularly valuable for real-world clinical implementation, effectively bridging the gap between model performance and practitioner trust.

Title: Application of Hierarchical Architecture Technology in Edge Devices
Abstract: With the deepening exploration of intelligent audio and the increasing demand for low latency, deploying deep learning models at the edge can not only effectively reduce latency, but also better protect user privacy. However, the high degree of hardware coupling of algorithms in traditional development models seriously restricts the portability and scalability of the system. With in-depth exploration of this issue, we propose a collaborative layered audio processing software architecture for multi-edge devices, which logically divides the various parts of the system into five relatively independent levels: hardware, drivers, data, algorithms, and applications. This eliminates the tight dependence of software and hardware and improves the flexibility and scalability of the system. At the same time, designing a heartbeat monitoring and asynchronous communication mechanism based on TCP/IP can achieve a stable and complete processing pipeline for VAD, streaming ASR, and punctuation recovery on a single edge node, which can also improve the reliability and synchronization efficiency of multi-device collaboration. In-depth experimental practice on Huawei Ascend Atlas 200I DK A2 has shown that it not only meets real-time performance requirements, but also has good system robustness and good scalability.

Title: Enhanced Deepfake Speech Classification With Ensemble Learning
Abstract: The advancement of speech synthesis technology has made detecting synthesized recordings a critical challenge in security and audio analysis. This study addresses the core challenge of cross-generator generalization under varying data availability by investigating the detection of synthesized speech using various machine learning architectures: Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers. To evaluate model robustness, we introduce a tiered dataset framework comprising three variants, which simulate different levels of data scarcity and generator diversity. To improve robustness, Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) was applied as the primary ensemble aggregation method, allowing for uncertainty-aware integration of the individual model outputs. Our experimental results, evaluated using Equal Error Rate (EER) and ROC-AUC, demonstrate that the BMA ensemble significantly outperforms individual architectures, particularly in data-constrained and temporally varied scenarios. The models were intentionally trained on impoverished and imbalanced datasets to evaluate their resilience under adverse conditions, with the reduced variant being the most demanding due to its severe data constraints. In the challenging variant, the BMA approach achieved an EER of 1.02% and an AUC of 0.99, effectively mitigating the performance drop-off seen in standalone models, which reached EERs as high as 5.82%. Furthermore, on the complete dataset, the proposed system attained an exceptional EER of 0.22% and an accuracy of 99.82%. These findings offer valuable insights for researchers in cybersecurity and multimedia forensics, highlighting that model uncertainty-aware aggregation can compensate for limited training data and provide reliable detection of synthesized audio even across diverse temporal variations and augmentation-heavy environments.

Title: A GAN-Augmented Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework for Explainable Crop Disease Detection
Abstract: The identification of crop diseases plays a crucial role in safeguarding agricultural productivity and ensuring global food security by enabling timely intervention and minimizing yield losses. Early diagnosis mitigates economic repercussions, optimizes pesticide application, and promotes sustainable agricultural practices. Automated detection systems enhance effective crop management and facilitate informed decision-making through increased accuracy and scalability. This research introduces a GAN-augmented multi-scale feature fusion network as an innovative methodology for crop disease detection and interpretability. To address class imbalance and improve generalization in real-world agricultural contexts, we employ generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enrich training datasets with diverse, high-quality synthetic crop images. The proposed framework utilizes a deep convolutional architecture with multi-scale feature fusion to extract hierarchical disease characteristics from leaf images, thereby enhancing recognition of subtle symptomatology across varying conditions. Our solution achieves cutting-edge detection accuracy (99.95% validation accuracy, AUC = 1.0), robust performance with limited data, and enhanced explainability through SHAP and LIME techniques. Comprehensive experiments conducted on publicly available crop disease datasets demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional methods including VGG16, ResNet50, and conventional augmentation approaches. This research advances precision agriculture and supports informed strategies for crop disease management by offering a scalable, interpretable deep learning instrument.

Title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Diabetes Risk
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is one of the most serious and emerging global public health issues requiring sophisticated instruments for early prediction to enable early interventions. This work introduces a machine learning framework for predicting diabetes risk with good accuracy. Methodologies include extensive preprocessing of data involving normalization and correction of class imbalance by using SMOTE followed by feature selection methodologies such as SHAP on the PIMA Indian Diabetes dataset. A suggested ensemble model incorporating multiple base learners was trained and tested. Experimental results confirm the better performance of the suggested ensemble model achieving an accuracy of 96.5%, AUC = 0.95, and F1-Score = 0.94 outperforming single classifiers such as Logistic Regression, SVM, and Random Forest. Title: DeepTexBoost OSCC: A Three-Stage Hybrid Classifier Combining GLCM, CNN, and XGBoost for Reliable Oral Cancer Detection
Abstract: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) is the most common oral cancer and continues to be a major health problem worldwide associated with late-stage diagnosis due to tissue complexity and diagnostic inconsistency among pathologists. To overcome these issues and enable early, trustworthy detection, in this work we propose DeepTexBoost OSCC, a unique three-level hybrid classification framework incorporating handcrafted texture descriptors, deep features and gradient-boosted learning. The presented methodology combines GLCM-based texture features to encompass crucial micro-patterns such as contrast, correlation, homogeneity, and energy, all of which are tightly associated with malignant changes in the epithelia layers. At the same time, a refined CNN is designed to learn high-level morphological representations directly from the histopathological images to fully capture OSCC-related structural variations. The GLCM and CNN features that are extracted are concatenated to construct a more descriptive feature vector that could represent both textured and spatial information. This fused representation is subjected to classification via XGBoost, a recently proposed scalable and robust optimized gradient boosting algorithm which has exhibited superior performance with heterogeneous feature spaces. The model is tested on a preprocessed OSCC histopathology dataset on 80-20 train-test split. DeepTexBoost OSCC attained a precision of 9 8 %, recall of 9 7 %-1 0 0 %, and F1-score of 0. 9 8 - 0. 9 9 in both Cancer and Normal classes under the overall accuracy of 99. The result of confusion matrix confirms the high ability of discrimination and the stability of the proposed framework, that is 79 out of 80 samples were successfully classified. he proposed hybrid structure significantly outperforms traditional CNN-only or texture-only approaches by integrating complementary feature and boosting-based classification. DeepTexBoost OSCC serves a strong, fast, and accurate computer-aided diagnostic instrument with great promise for clinical translation, enabling pathologists for rapid and objective screening of OSCC. In future work, the generalization will be evaluated as a multi-center retrospective study and a prospective study, and XAI-module which not only maintains the clinical image but also HINM will be developed.

Title: A Multi Module Deep Learning Framework for User Preferences and Behaviour in FM Radio
Abstract: The Speech Processing Project is a broad process of giving meaning to the audio with the help of state-of-the-art machine learning and deep learning. This project brings together a number of key modules in order to reach some very important goals, which include preparing audio, speech transcription, inappropriate content detection, identifying song preferences, and estimating the age of speakers. Taking advantage of state-of-the-art models like OpenAI's Whisper for converting speech to text, Facebook's Wav2Vec2 for classifying audio, and Cardiff NLP for detecting offensive material, the following project offers a powerful yet flexible means to analyze a wide variety of audio information. The preprocessing pipeline employs tools such as Librosa and Noisereduce for noise reduction, normalization, and dynamic range compression to make sure that high-quality audio goes into the models. Besides, in-house machine learning models with Scikit-learn-trained algorithms attained a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.35 for speaker age estimation and more than 95% accuracy for transcription analysis. The module for song preference analysis was seen to be able to classify songs by era with 90% confidence and map preferences to age groups successfully. Through automating music and conversation audio analysis, the project provides outputs as accurate transcripts, confidently detected inappropriate content, song tastes by time ranges and age groups, and results of age estimation. Provided through interactive visualizations and reports in details, the project outputs indicate that it can handle real-world tasks for audio analysis and promoting precision and scalability across applications.

Title: Predicting PHQ-9-Derived Depressive Symptom Screening Proxy Labels in NHANES
Abstract: Depression is a leading contributor to global disability, and population surveys such as the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) include validated symptom instruments (e.g., PHQ-9) for large-scale monitoring. This work presents a reproducible machine-learning baseline to predict a PHQ-9-derived screening proxy (PHQ-9 ≥q 10) using a compact set of demographic and socioeconomic NHANES covariates (with optional sleep information), intended for benchmarking and epidemiological analyses rather than clinical diagnosis. Using NHANES 2017-2018 (N=5,533; test N=1,107; prevalence=0.0488), we compare CatBoost, logistic regression, and random forest under deterministic stratified splits with strict leakage prevention. CatBoost achieves the best overall performance with ROC-AUC 0.7607 (unweighted bootstrap 95% CI [0.6951, 0.8233]), PR-AUC 0.1441, and balanced accuracy 0.7248 at a tuned threshold. We additionally report survey-weighted evaluation, subgroup and fairness auditing, decision curve analysis, robustness checks (sleep ablation and threshold sensitivity), and cross-cycle transfer across NHANES 2005-2018. Finally, calibration transport experiments show that Platt scaling improves expected calibration error for logistic regression under temporal shift without changing discrimination.

Title: A Framework for Stroke Prediction Using CDA-ResNet with Adaptive Feature Selection and Evaluation of Ensemble ML Methods
Abstract: This study provides a stroke prediction framework with CDA-ResNet with adaptive feature selection and a comparison of the performance of different ensemble machine learning (ML) approaches. The CDA-ResNet model is the second model that can improve the accuracy of the prediction process by using the dense convolutional blocks and attention to extract meaningful features out of the brain MRI images. Adaptive feature selection is the best approach to optimization of the model as it picks the most relevant features and minimizes overfitting and efficiency. Ensemble such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM are compared and evaluated on the framework to determine its performance. Based on the results obtained, the proposed CDA-ResNet model, with adaptive feature selection, has an accuracy of 94.5 % and F1-score of 0.93 and AUC of 0.97, which compares with the traditional models. The ensemble techniques also enhance the performance and XGBoost has the best precision and recall. This framework has a great potential of detecting early strokes which is a reliable instrument of clinical decision making and intervention planning.

Title: An Improved Wireless Sensor Network for Secure and Real-Time Violin Performance Assessment in the Domain of 6G-IoT
Abstract: Currently, the music industry is the main focus of many researchers, scholars, and experts. However, there is limited research on real-time assessment and feedback mechanisms in the mentioned industry. Therefore, there is a pressing need for innovative solutions in the context of advancing musical education and performance that facilitate real-time assessment and feedback for musicians, particularly violinists. The conventional evaluation methods often lack the adaptability and immediacy required for effective skill enhancement. Keeping these in mind, this research paper proposes the Violin Real-Time Response to Data Collection Model (VRRTDCM) for real-time violin performance assessment within the framework of 6G Internet of Things (6G-IoT). In order to facilitate real-time performance for violinists, this research work presents a comprehensive system architecture that integrates a robust Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) by highlighting modular components for independent development and elevations. To capture critical performance metrics like bow speed, pressure, and angle, this research deploys low-power and lightweight sensors attached to the violin and its bow. The proposed framework uses WSNs and LSTM-CNN models to provide accurate evaluation while also ensuring secure, scalable, and reliable data transmission, making it an excellent choice for real-time performance assessment. Upon collecting data from the violin, the deployed sensors wirelessly transmit the same to a centralized Data Collection Hub utilizing secure communication protocols such as LoRa or Zigbee. By compiling the sensor data into a unified dataset that supports high temporal resolution for real-time analysis the centralized hub performs data aggregation and synchronization, which then passes to the Processing and Analysis Unit. This unit applies advanced algorithms, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to evaluate performance metrics and provide immediate feedback by enabling musicians to make real-time adjustments. To ensure secure storage of all processed data, the data is handed over to the Data Storage and Feedback Unit by providing a sequential log of performance metrics while enabling a real-time feedback interface that visualizes key metrics. Experimental evaluations of the proposed VRRTDCM are compared with existing models, showing that our proposed model has highly superior performance by achieving an accuracy of 81.69% and an AUCROC of 0.89. from these results, it is clear that our suggested approach allows musicians to improve their techniques more efficiently by developing a deeper connection to their skill and elevating the quality of musical performance in educational settings.

Title: Flexible IMU Sensor Array For 3D Colonoscope Shape Reconstruction and AI-Based Loop Detection
Abstract: Looping during colonoscopy procedures is a major cause of patient discomfort and increases the risk of complications. With the rising incidence of colorectal cancer, there is an urgent need for safer and more efficient colonoscopy techniques. We developed a proof-of-concept platform for 3D visualization of the colonoscope combined with artificial intelligence (AI)-based loop detection. The system consists of an array of 15 inertial measurement units (IMUs) mounted on a flexible printed circuit board that can be retrofitted into the instrument channel of conventional colonoscopes. Using sensor fusion algorithms, the position and orientation of individual IMUs are estimated to reconstruct the 3D shape of the colonoscope in real time. The system successfully reconstructed the colonoscope shape in a silicone colon phantom, and the AI model achieved high loop-detection performance with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.95 on test data. These results demonstrate feasibility in an artificial environment, while further validation in clinical settings is required.

Title: Gaussian Process Regression of Steering Vectors With Physics-Aware Deep Composite Kernels for Augmented Listening
Abstract: Thispaper investigates continuous representations of steering vectors over frequency and microphone/source positions for augmented listening (e.g., spatial filtering and binaural rendering), enabling user-parameterized control of the reproduced sound field. Steering vectors have typically been used for representing the spatial response of a microphone array as a function of the look-up direction. The basic algebraic representation of these quantities assuming an idealized environment cannot deal with the scattering effect of the sound field. One may thus collect a discrete set of real steering vectors measured in dedicated facilities and super-resolve (i.e., upsample) them. Recently, physics-aware deep learning methods have been effectively used for this purpose. Such deterministic super-resolution, however, suffers from the overfitting problem due to the non-uniform uncertainty over the measurement space. To solve this problem, we integrate an expressive representation based on the neural field (NF) into the principled probabilistic framework based on the Gaussian process (GP). Specifically, we propose a physics-aware composite kernel that models the directional incoming waves and the subsequent scattering effect. Our comprehensive comparative experiment showed the effectiveness of the proposed method under data insufficiency conditions. In downstream tasks such as speech enhancement and binaural rendering using the simulated data of the SPEAR challenge, the oracle performances were attained with less than ten times fewer measurements.

Title: Multi Learning on Discriminative Embedding Vector and Masking for Cocktail Party Effect
Abstract: Nowadays, the incorporation of cutting-edge deep learning techniques into speech processing is regarded as groundbreaking, exerting a significant influence on various domains such as speech recognition, speech separation, audio-visual content creation, telecommunication, and hearing aid technologies. This study delves into the exploration of both deep learning models and learning methods for speech separation. Two distinct approaches are considered as the first involves end-to-end networks that directly estimate masks or utterances. In contrast, the second employs deep clustering, a time-frequency-based voice separation framework. Deep clustering, functioning as a deep embedding approach, has demonstrated remarkable performance by training embedding vectors during learning and isolating them during inference. The end-to-end networks capitalize on a direct approximation of utterances or masks. This study presents an innovative multi-learning strategy that harnesses the advantages of both techniques for utterance separation. Moreover, we suggest discriminative embedding vector learning to improve separation performance within the deep clustering framework. Experimental findings demonstrate that our approach surpasses individual component networks across multiple datasets on standard metrics.

Title: Facial Emotion-Driven Music Recommendation Systems: Innovations and Applications in Personalized Music Therapy
Abstract: The rapid advancement of facial recognition technology opens new frontiers for the development of music recommendation systems. The new approaches toward recommending music fail to bring in the effective integration of the emotional dimensions of music with the user’s personality and mood, this research paper presents a novel framework of a facial recognition-based music recommendation system that converges toward this objective. It enhances the musical experience for users through their suggestions because of higher resonance with emotional needs and preferences. This groundbreaking innovation includes facial recognition technology in the music recommendation systems. Subsequently, these emotional cues in combination with the analysis of musical features determine songs to be communicated to the listener for maximum resonance with his/her emotional state. Considering the dynamic emotive preferences from the user side, the system may decide to recommend songs to the user that is not only aligned with their past listening history but also cater to the user’s fluctuating emotional needs. This approach is quite different from traditional music recommendation systems that rely heavily on collaborative filtering or popularity-based algorithms. The system might change the face of how humans would interact and find music. It harnesses the power of deep learning and integrates multiple forms of data, it begins by collecting and extracting facial data using the FER dataset. Meanwhile, Song data is extracted from Spotify’s Web API, which allows facial and emotional data to be matched to specific song characteristics. Data cleaning and preprocessing are important steps in refining datasets and organizing them for efficient access. It leverages CNN’s unique ability to recognize and categorize emotional states expressed in facial images to guarantee ideal performance. The research has shown the possibility of computationally modeling the latent constructs underlying music listening and emotion regulation as well as identifying the relationship between user emotions musical mood and personality characteristics of each individual.

Title: Multi-Layer Security for Wireless BCIs via Adversarial Chaos Synergy
Abstract: While we benefit from the capabilities of Denoising Auto-Encoders (DAEs), some security risks also arise with the widespread adoption of these systems. Conventional chaos masking and jamming defenses do not protect against DAE-equipped eavesdroppers. Chaotic masking adds randomness to signals and helps with security, but it cannot stop detection by a DAE. To tackle this problem, we design a secure Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) using Long Short-Term Memories (LSTMs) that combines adversarial training and chaotic signals. We formulate an optimization problem to model the proposed BCI and generate a low-power perturbation vector. The results indicate that when the noise variance is equal to 0.2, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of an illegal DAE exceeds 1.2. At the same time, the non-adversarial performance is approximately 0.5. Moreover, the performances of different Neural Networks are evaluated under the same computational complexity conditions. The best result is provided by the LSTM, with a complexity of about 3104 Real Multiplications per Symbol (RMpS). The proposed Adversarial Chaos Synergy (ACS) framework is compatible with cloud/edge infrastructure. With these features, the ACS approach is suitable for applications such as mobile medical services, lightweight bio-medical instruments, brain-to-brain networks, and smart hospitals.
