Title: Colloquial-Aware Multimodal Fusion Network for Contextual Speech Formalization
Abstract: The increasing use of informal and colloquial language in user-created content on social media presents a significant challenge for automated comprehension systems. Such study demonstrates that we have to consider multi-modal information (text, audio and Video) to enhance the robust multimodal comprehension for colloquial expressions. The proposed model uses the pretrained Wav2Vec2.0 encoder, and a multi-head fusion transformer for aggregating semantic information across modalities. One of the main contributions is the proposed Colloquial-Aware Cross-Attention Module (CAXA) that dynamically correlates the slang-rich audio transcriptions with the visual or textual context for improved interpretability. CAXA-Net combines a Wav2Vec2.0 encoder for speech processing, a ViT (Vision Transformer) for frame-level image understanding, and a CNN-based visual feature extractor for scene image inputs. These streams are fused using a Cross-Attention Fusion Transformer (CAFT) which enables semantic alignment across modalities. Finally, a T5-based transformer decoder translates the fused colloquial text into its formal equivalent Experimental evaluation was conducted using the MELD (Multimodal EmotionLines Dataset), which contains real-world colloquial dialogues across modalities. The proposed CAXA-Net achieves 92.8% accuracy, 82.7 BLEU score, and 89.1 F1-score on the MELD dataset, demonstrating strong improvements over text-only and multimodal baselines.

Title: Task Assignment AI Assistant: Enhancing Administrative Staff and Fieldworker Efficiency with Reasoning LLMs and Speech Interaction
Abstract: Fieldworkers and administrative staff in grid maintenance face inefficiencies when retrieving task-related information, relying on manual searches through PDFs and databases. This paper presents a Task Assignment AI Assistant that streamlines information access via text and speech interaction. Using Text-to-SQL and a vector database, the assistant delivers factually accurate, context-aware responses while leveraging iterative reasoning for multi-step queries. To enhance accessibility, the solution supports multimodal inputs, integrating Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) models. The ASR model, fine-tuned on IMDA's National Speech Corpus (NSC), improves comprehension of Singlish and local accents, achieving a 3 times reduction in word error rate (WER) compared to the base model. Designed for on-premises deployment, it runs efficiently using Small Language Models (SLMs), improving inference speed by 6 times compared to using a 4-bit quantised LLM, enabling the entire solution to run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. This enhances real-time usability while maintaining comparable performance.

Title: Enhanced Voice Pathology Classification Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
Abstract: Early identification is crucial for successful treatment of voice disorders since they can have a substantial impact on communication and general quality of life. This study investigates the use of Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) methods to categorize speech recordings as either problematic or healthy. Key acoustic properties are extracted from a collection of WAV audio recordings and used to train different machine learning and deep learning models. Advanced DL architectures like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are used in conjunction with more conventional ML methods like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest (RF). To ascertain how well these models detect irregularities in voice, their performance is systematically assessed using important measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. In order to shed light on the advantages and disadvantages of each strategy, the study compares them, offering insights into the best methods for classifying voice pathologies. DL algorithms learn intricate patterns straight from unprocessed audio data, potentially providing greater accuracy and resilience than ML models, which use feature engineering for categorization. In order to improve early diagnosis and discover the best classification algorithms, this research adds to the expanding field of automated voice disorder detection. The results provide useful direction for the creation of sophisticated diagnostic instruments in clinical settings, which could help medical practitioners evaluate voice health more quickly. For better results in practical applications, future research might concentrate on improving model generalization, extending datasets, and honing feature extraction methods.

Title: PURE Codec: Progressive Unfolding of Residual Entropy for Speech Codec Learning
Abstract: Neural speech codecs have achieved strong performance in low-bitrate compression, but residual vector quantization (RVQ) often suffers from unstable training and ineffective decomposition, limiting reconstruction quality and efficiency. We propose PURE Codec (Progressive Unfolding of Residual Entropy), a novel framework that guides multi-stage quantization using a pre-trained speech enhancement model. The first quantization stage reconstructs low-entropy, denoised speech embeddings, while subsequent stages encode residual high-entropy components. This design improves training stability significantly. Experiments demonstrate that PURE consistently outperforms conventional RVQ-based codecs in reconstruction and downstream speech language model-based text-to-speech, particularly under noisy training conditions.

Title: A Self-Refining Framework for Enhancing ASR Using TTS-Synthesized Data
Abstract: We propose a self-refining framework that enhances ASR performance with only unlabeled datasets. The process starts with an existing ASR model generating pseudo-labels on unannotated speech, which are then used to train a highfidelity text-to-speech (TTS) system. Then, synthesized speech text pairs are bootstrapped into the original ASR system, completing the closed-loop self-improvement cycle. We demonstrated the effectiveness of the framework on Taiwanese-Mandarin speech. Leveraging 6,000 hours of unlabeled speech, a moderate amount of text data, and synthetic content from the AI models, we adapt Whisper-large-v2 into a specialized model, Twister. Twister reduces error rates by up to 20 % on Mandarin and 50 % on Mandarin-English code-switching benchmarks compared to Whisper. Results highlight the framework as a compelling alternative to pseudo-labeling self-distillation approaches and provides a practical pathway for improving ASR performance in lowresource or domain-specific settings.

Title: PrediscanNetV2: Early Risk Classification of Coronary Artery Disease via Gated Cross-Attention on Retinal Fundus Images
Abstract: Preventive medicine presently faces challenges in identifying the risk of Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) prior to the occurrence of symptoms. We employ PrediscanNetV2, a method that simply uses basic demographic data and non-invasive fundus photography to estimate Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT), which is an important sign of atherosclerosis. Most current approaches just integrate tabular and visual information. Our method is different because it uses a Gated Cross-Attention mechanism on top of a Siamese EfficientNet-B3 backbone. This architecture makes it possible to change the weights of visual features based on the patient's age and gender, which is a good way to simulate a clinical setting. We examined the model with the China-Fundus-CIMT dataset (n=2,903) using a strict 5-fold cross-validation procedure. The results showed that the average accuracy was 84.52% and the Area Under the Curve (AUC) was 0.9104. PrediscanNetV2 demonstrates its efficacy as an automated, scalable instrument for assessing cardiovascular risk by statistically surpassing conventional performance benchmarks.

Title: Skin Cancer Detection and Classification Using Dermoscopic Imaging with Deep Learning Analysis
Abstract: Early detection and correct classification are the most effective methods for improving patient outcomes in cutaneous cancers such as melanoma. This study introduces a deep learning system capable of autonomously analysing dermoscopy images. It integrates cutting-edge Deep Learning (DL) architectures with comprehensive data pre-processing and augmentation methods. We assembled a curated dataset from public sources including high-resolution dermoscopy images of Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) and benign melanomas. Colour normalisation was used to standardise the photos. To improve the model's generalisability, it was augmented by rotation, flipping, and intensity shifting. This work used stratified five-fold cross-validation to evaluate three fine-tuned deep learning models: VGG19, DenseNet-121, and MobileNet. The MobileNet model achieved a total accuracy of 0.994, surpassing its competitors to detect healthy and abnormal tissues. This strategy far surpasses typical machine-learning techniques. The results indicate that DL-enhanced dermoscopic analysis may assist dermatologists in skin cancer screening. The technique has promise as a decision-support instrument in clinical processes.

Title: A Multi-Modal AI Framework for Real-Time Stress and Sleep Monitoring with Intelligent Interventions
Abstract: Growing instances of stress and sleep disorders in both students and remote workers demand smart and user-friendly mental health tools. This article suggests creating an AI-driven solution that will implement speech analysis, recognition of emotional facial expressions, and behavior patterns to determine the level of stress and propose proper interventions. The assistant uses Whisper in speech-to-text transcription, Deep Face in facial expression recognition, as well as TextBlob in determining the polarity of sentiments. When the stress is high, the system provides real-time warnings based on the Twilio SMS and plays some soothing music or message based on text-to-speech and Pygame. It also shows the long-term stress trend visualization at matplotlib on a Streamlit application. Neither cloud-based heavy APIs nor extensive hardware is required to use the tool that runs in real-time and uses only a microphone and webcam. The simulations of using the system experimentally reveal that it can respond to indicators of stress timely manner and without compromising the privacy of the user. The given solution is inexpensive, scalable, and efficient regarding the promotion of sleep hygiene and psychological well-being.

Title: VaaniVerse: Low-Latency Speech Translation Using Universal Earphones
Abstract: In multilingual societies like India, language barriers are a major obstacle to effective communication. Due to their reliance on internet connectivity, high cost, poor performance in noisy environments and high latency, existing solutions frequently fail. This paper introduces VaaniVerse, a real-time, multilingual speech translation system with low latency that can be operated with smartphones and standard earphones. The system also integrates an efficient pipeline for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis noise cancellation and context-free translation. VaaniVerse provides accurate and adaptable translations between Hindi, English and Kannada even in noisy environment using lightweight edge AI models like Whisper, Coqui TTS and IndicTrans2. Given that the architecture is optimized for offline use, accessibility and affordability are ensured. The system also futher incorporates several GUI-based novelties that enhances usability and distinguishes it from existing translation applications.

Title: Transfer Learning Based Deep Learning Framework For Multiclass Brain Tumor Classification
Abstract: Brain tumors are detrimental to health as they generate uncontrolled cellular proliferation. This can disrupt critical cognitive functioning and lead to significant problems, particularly in adults. Early and accurate detection of brain tumors (BT) is crucial as it enhances treatment efficacy and prolongs patient survival. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) remains the superior method for detecting BT, as it provides superior visualization of soft tissue compared to other imaging modalities. However, manually sorting and analyzing MRI data is time consuming and labor-intensive, and varying interpretations may arise among various individuals. Deep learning (DL) has advanced significantly recently particularly via transfer learning (TL). This demonstrates that deep learning may be significantly beneficial for automating complex tasks in medical imaging. This research presents a TL-based framework for the categorization of BTC utilizing pre-trained convolutional neural networks. Following extensive pre-processing, including cropping of the region of interest, enhancement and augmentation, we evaluate the performance of EfficientNetB4 and MobileNetV2 on MRI data. We evaluated EfficientNetB4 and MobileNetV2 on an accessible Kaggle MRI dataset. EfficientNetB4 has a training accuracy of 97.51% and a test accuracy of 98.56%. MobileNetV2 achieved an accuracy of 99.79% during training and 96.67% during testing. These findings indicate that advanced TL structures can enhance our ability to classify brain cancers. This enhances the efficacy and reliability of diagnostic instruments in practical situations.

Title: Integrating Physiological Signals into Music Machine Learning: An HRV-Based Framework
Abstract: Music is widely being recognized as a non-pharmacological intervention for anxiety, yet its physiological mechanisms remain unexplored. This study examines the effect of Kaapi raga (a south Indian classical music) and weightless ambient music on cardiovascular regulation and anxiety reduction using heart rate variability (HRV) and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Twenty participants with high anxiety (HAM-A >25) completed a protocol involving rest, music listening, and attention tasks while ECG and MAP were continuously recorded.HRV features were extracted across time, frequency, and nonlinear domains and analysed using machine learning classifiers. Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest performance (70.8% accuracy; AUC up to 0.89), outperforming linear models. Feature ablation revealed non-linear SD2, pNN50, HR mean, and high-frequency power percentage as key predictors of music-induced physiological changes.The findings here demonstrate that ensemble machine learning methods can robustly model music's impact on anxiety, while domain-specific HRV features provide actionable biomarkers for developing personalized, evidence-based music therapy interventions.

Title: Detection of Parkinson's Disease by Analysis of Vocal Signals Using Genetic Algorithm & KNN Classifier
Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) represents a slowly advancing neurological disorder often associated with aging. Its progression results in significant motor impairments and a marked decline in daily functioning. Since conventional diagnosis mainly depends on identifying motor abnormalities that arise at later stages, early recognition remains a challenge. To mitigate this, a hybrid diagnostic strategy combining Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based feature refinement and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classification is presented. The GA process also aids in the selection of important acoustic features and the tuning of the neighborhood parameter of KNN to reduce data dimensions and increase model efficiency. Experimental testing using a freely available Parkinson's speech dataset revealed that the performance of the GA-KNN model surpassed that of the standard classifiers SVM, ANN, and individual KNN with 94.56% mean cross-validation accuracy and 96.61% test accuracy.

Title: Time-Frequency Conformer and Kalman Filter-Based Speech Enhancement Method
Abstract: The performance of Kalman filters (KF) in speech enhancement is highly dependent on the estimation accuracy of linear predictive coefficients (LPCs). To address the significant estimation bias of LPCs in complex noisy environments, this paper proposes a time-frequency dual-domain Conformer-based Kalman filter speech enhancement method - CAKFNet. The model adopts an encoder-decoder architecture: during the encoding phase, a Dilated DenseNet module is introduced to exponentially expand the receptive field and enhance local feature continuity, thereby achieving multi-scale feature aggregation. Subsequently, dual Conformer modules in both time and frequency domains jointly model the long-term dependencies of speech signals and local convolutional features, fully capturing spatio-temporal correlations. The decoding stage employs a decoupled dual-branch architecture to separately regress the LPC power spectrum (LPC-PS) of clean speech and noise. Building upon this, an autocorrelation matrix is generated via inverse Fourier transform. The Levinson-Durbin recursive algorithm is then employed to compute the clean speech and noise LPC coefficients required for the Augmented Kalman Filter (AKF), along with their prediction error variance, ultimately achieving speech enhancement. The proposed method undergoes systematic experimental evaluation on the publicly available VoiceBank + DEMAND dataset. Results demonstrate that CAKFNet effectively reduces spectral distortion in LPC estimation. Objective metrics, including PESQ and STOI, show significant improvements over baseline methods, while subjective listening tests confirm substantial enhancements in speech quality and intelligibility.

Title: Integrating Generative AI into Challenge-Based Learning: A Case Study in Preventive Medicine and Public Health Education
Abstract: This study explores the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into a challenge-based learning (CBL) course on preventive medicine and public health for first-year health students. Implemented at Tecnologico de Monterrey, the course aimed to enhance students' ability to design community based strategies for preventing non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Starting in 2024, students used AI tools to generate and refine proposals aligned with national health guidelines. Academic performance data from 2021 to 2025 showed stable overall grades, but there was a notable improvement in the quality of AI-assisted preventive proposals. Additionally, student motivation-measured using the MUSIC model-was higher in 2025, particularly in terms of empowerment and perceived success. These findings suggest that AI can enhance engagement and support the development of critical and digital skills in health education. Further research is needed to assess long-term impacts and guide the ethical and effective integration of AI in medical training.

Title: Swara-Net: A Deep Learning Baseline and Curated Dataset for Five Under-Represented Carnatic Ragas
Abstract: This paper addresses a critical gap in computational musicology: the lack of robust datasets and baselines for specific, under-represented Carnatic ragas. We introduce a new, manually-curated dataset of 638 audio snippets for five prominent ragas: Shankarabharanam, Revathi, Abheri, Brindavanasaranga, and Mayamalavagowla. This collection, sourced from public recordings, is designed to be timbrally diverse. To establish a strong performance benchmark, we compare a standard Support Vector Machine (SVM) against a 3-layer Deep Neural Network (DNN). The results are striking: the SVM achieves only 57.03% accuracy, while our proposed DNN (Swara-Net) achieves 99.0% accuracy. This demonstrates the superior ability of deep learning to navigate the complex, high-dimensional feature space of raga. We further provide a musicological analysis of the model's single misclassification. This work contributes both a valuable, open-source dataset and a reproducible, high-performance baseline, paving the way for more nuanced research on these specific ragas.

Title: Executional Error Detection in Robotic Surgery using a Hybrid Dual Pathway Architecture
Abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery, enabled by systems like the da Vinci Surgical System, enhances minimally invasive procedures through high-definition 3D visualization and precise instrument control. However, executional errors, such as improper needle orientation or loss of instrument visibility, pose significant risks to patient safety. This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework for detecting executional errors in surgical videos using the JHU-ISI Gesture and Skill Assessment Working Set (JIGSAWS) dataset, focusing on suturing and needle-passing tasks. The model integrates a ResNet-50 backbone for spatial feature extraction with a temporal modeling pipeline comprising 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (1D CNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), and self-attention mechanisms. A dualpathway architecture, combining gesture-aware and gesture-agnostic branches, employs dynamic fusion to adapt predictions based on contextual reliability. Evaluated through Group K-Fold cross-validation, the model achieves robust performance with metrics including F1-score (87.2%), Jaccard index (77.2%), accuracy (87.4%), AUC (89.6%), and recall (87.0%). These results highlight its potential for real-time surgical feedback, skill assessment, and enhanced training systems, advancing safer surgical practices.

Title: Optimization of Temporal Convolutional Networks Using Harris Hawks Algorithm for Efficient Embedded Speech Recognition
Abstract: Recent advances in embedded speech recognition require models that balance accuracy, efficiency, and low resource consumption. This paper presents a novel approach using Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) optimized by Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) to enhance speech recognition performance on Raspberry Pi devices. The HHO algorithm dynamically tunes key hyperparameters of the TCN models such as convolutional filter sizes, dilation rates, and learning rates - in order to achieve high accuracy while reducing computational overhead. Experiments on benchmark speech datasets demonstrate that the proposed HHO-optimized TCN achieves higher recognition accuracy and faster inference compared to baseline models (e.g., standard LSTM, GRU). The work illustrates the potential of combining bio-inspired optimization with efficient convolutional sequence models to enable real-time speech recognition on resource-constrained edge devices.

Title: Deepfake Audio Detection: Differentiating Modulated and Deepfake Audio
Abstract: The rise in deepfake audio and AI-generated speech has become a very real and serious security issue. The voices that are generated using deepfakes are becoming so realistic that it is difficult to differentiate between a real speech and a deepfake speech. Traditional detection techniques that rely only on audio features will fail in such cases. The paper introduced a hybrid approach to deepfake audio detection that combines modern deep learning with classic audio analysis. The paper uses a Wav2Vec2 embedding to capture speech features and MFCC features to highlight fine details in the sound. It shows that using Wav2Vec2 alone achieves about 81% accuracy, while adding MFCCs boosts performance to 85%, with noticeable improvements in detecting modulated speech. It demonstrates that combining deep embeddings, traditional features, and realistic data augmentations leads to a more reliable detection system.

Title: A TabNet-Based Deep Learning Framework for Predicting Uric Acid Elevation and Kidney Health Risks
Abstract: The rising popularity of high-protein diets, while advantageous in some situations, has been increasingly linked to heightened uric acid levels and renal impairment. These illnesses often go untreated until significant consequences develop, highlighting the need for predictive and preventive healthcare instruments. This paper introduces a TabNet-based deep learning framework for the early identification of hyperuricemia and renal health issues using structured health data. The model utilizes the NHANES dataset, a comprehensive repository of publicly accessible data including biochemical markers, nutritional consumption, demographic characteristics, and comorbidity indicators. Proposed Model Works in 3 stages. Initially, data preparation includes the cleansing, imputation, and modification of pertinent parameters like blood uric acid, creatinine, BUN, protein intake levels, age, and BMI. Secondly, the TabNet architecture is trained, which uses attentive feature selection to comprehend intricate, non-linear interactions while maintaining model interpretability. In the third phase, the model is assessed and contrasted with leading classifiers such as XGBoost, Random Forest, and MLP, while feature significance is shown using TabNet's attention masks. The suggested model had an accuracy of 94.2%, exceeding baseline techniques across all principal performance criteria. Findings indicate that consumption of animal protein, salt, inadequate hydration, and compromised filtration are significant factors in increased uric acid levels. This approach exhibits exceptional prediction accuracy and provides valuable insights for personalized dietary planning. Our technique has potential in enhancing AI-driven preventive healthcare and facilitating scalable, personalized dietary risk assessment systems.

Title: Effect of Anxiety Reduction Interventions on Exam Anxiety for Engineering Students Using Physiological Signals
Abstract: Acute test anxiety negatively affects both academic performance and mental well-being in engineering students. Although earlier studies have examined the long-term impact of culturally relevant methods like breathing techniques and Indian classical music, they mostly rely on self-reports, lack real-time physiological data, and seldom offer direct quantitative comparisons. This research investigates the short-term efficacy of guided deep breathing and Indian classical music Raga Bhairavi using wearable biosensors, statistical analysis, and machine learning. The paper randomly assigns sixty undergraduate engineering students with moderate to high anxiety to intervention and control groups. The research measures Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) and Heart Rate Variability (HRV) during the Montreal Imaging Stress Task (MIST), which induces exam-related stress. Non-parametric statistical tests confirm a significant increase in stress for the control group, while both interventions effectively reduce physiological arousal. This paper also implements various Machine learning models (Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost) to classify stress states with high accuracy (>98%), F1 scores (>0.98), and ROC AUC values (>0.96). Integrating culturally grounded interventions with real-time physiological monitoring and AI-based stress classification can offer a scalable, intelligent framework to support student mental health.

Title: Research on Pulmonary Nodule Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8: Attention Mechanism and Multi- scale Feature Fusion
Abstract: Early and precise detection of pulmonary nodules is crucial for improving the diagnosis and treatment outcomes of lung cancer. However, manual reading of traditional CT images has limitations such as low efficiency and the tendency to miss small lesions (<3mm), especially when dealing with the weak features of small nodules and their susceptibility to background noise interference. As a mainstream object detection algorithm, YOLOv8, although it has the advantage of real-time performance, has bottlenecks in the detection of small objects in medical images, such as insufficient feature fusion and high missed detection rate of pulmonary micronodules. To this end, this paper proposes a pulmonary nodule detection system based on the improved YOLOv8, which specifically addresses the above-mentioned pain points by integrating the CBAM attention mechanism and multi- scale feature fusion strategy. Specifically, the improved model embeds CBAM modules in the backbone network (CSPDarknet) and the neck network (PANet), using channel attention (CAM) to learn channel weights and spatial attention (SAM) to generate spatial masks, thereby enhancing feature focusing on nodule regions. Meanwhile, the PANet structure is improved by adding a direct path from the shallow high-resolution feature map (such as 80 × 80) to the detection head, and an adaptive weight fusion mechanism (ASFF) is introduced to optimize the fusion effect of deep and shallow features. Furthermore, by adjusting the weights of the CIoU Loss to balance the positive and negative samples, the Focal Loss is added to alleviate the imbalance problem of the categories of large and small nodules. Experiments on the LUNA16 dataset show that the model achieves 92.5% SOTA performance on the mAP@0.5 metric, significantly outperforming benchmark models such as the original YOLOv8 and Faster R-CNN. Moreover, the lightweight design (only increasing by 0.8G FLOPs) achieves a balance between detection accuracy and speed. The ablation experiment verified the effectiveness of the CBAM module and the multi-scale fusion strategy. This study provides radiologists with an efficient auxiliary tool, which is conducive to improving the efficiency of pulmonary nodule screening and promoting the clinical application of AI-assisted early diagnosis of lung cancer.

Title: Application of the Cascade Method in the Integration of Whisper and Ensemble NLP for Speech Summarization
Abstract: In the era of information overload and due to declined human cognitive skill, efficient comprehension of spoken content has become increasingly important. This study propose a cascade-based speech summarization framework that integrates OpenAI’s Whisper-small model for speech recognition and Ensemble Model that combine T5, Pegasus, and BART for abstractive text summarization process. The CNN/DailyMail News dataset is used for the training and evaluation process. The system aims to transform spoken input into concise, semantically coherent summaries while minimizing transcription and summarizations errors. The methodology consists of two sequential stages, which are Whisper-based ASR for transcription and ensemble model summarization using reranking method. Experimental results demonstrate that Whisper-small achieved an exceptional transcription accuracy with WER of 3.3% and CER of 1.7%. Among individual models, BART obtained the highest summarization performance with ROUGE-L of 0.7498, while the ensemble model achieved balanced performance across all metrics.

Title: A Weighted Ensemble of Multi-Scale Fusion CNNs for Melanoma Classification
Abstract: The early and accurate diagnosis of malignant melanoma remains a significant challenge in dermatology, largely due to the high visual similarity between malignant and benign skin lesions. This paper introduces a novel classification methodology tested on the challenging and highly imbalanced ISIC 2017 dataset. A custom multi-scale feature fusion head was designed to improve the feature extraction capabilities of standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) backbones. Through systematic evaluation, an EfficientNetB6 model equipped with this fusion head was identified as the most effective single-model architecture. To further boost the performance, a weighted ensemble was developed that combines the outputs of our two best fusion models: EfficientNetB6 and DenseNet201. The final proposed model, utilizing a 90/10 weighting scheme, achieved an F1-score of 0.5517, an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.8174, and a clinically significant recall of 75.2%. The experimental results demonstrated that this weighted ensemble of multi-scale fusion models offers a superior balance between precision and recall, establishing an effective strategy for this complex classification task.

Title: Speech Enhancement using Sub Convolutional based STCM Model
Abstract: Speech enhancement improves the quality and intelligibility of speech in noisy environments. An effective speech Enhancement model depends on precisely modeling the long range dependencies of noisy speech. Although several recent studies have been performed to enhance speech by capturing long-term contextual information, in this paper we propose that speech enhancement through multistage learning is an effective method for improving various deep learning modules. The proposed model utilizes a multi-stage structure where Sub-convolutional blocks are followed by stacks of Squeezed Temporal Convolutional Network Modules (STCMs) featuring exponentially increasing dilation rates, and improves the parameters. The STCM blocks handle temporal sequence modeling tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed model improves performance over existing baselines with objective metrics being PESQ and STOI.

Title: Performance Evaluation of Lyric-Based Music Recommendation Model: Comparison of TF-IDF, Word2Vec, BERT, and Hybrid Model
Abstract: Music recommendation systems play a vital role in enhancing user experience on streaming platforms like Spotify by providing accurate and personalized song suggestions. This study explores and compares different text-based recommendation approaches, including TFIDF, Word2Vec, BERT, and a Hybrid Model, to analyze song lyrics and improve recommendation accuracy. Using a dataset of song lyrics, TF-IDF identifies word frequency similarities, Word2Vec captures semantic relationships between words, and BERT understands lyrical context using deep language modeling. A Hybrid Model combining these approaches is also developed to enhance recommendation performance. The models are evaluated using Precision@5, Recall@5, and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) to determine their effectiveness. The results indicate that TF-IDF has the lowest performance, as it relies only on direct word matching. Word2Vec improves accuracy by recognizing word associations, while BERT significantly enhances recommendation quality by understanding contextual meaning. The Hybrid Model achieves the best performance across all metrics, demonstrating that integrating multiple techniques leads to more precise recommendations. These findings suggest that combining deep learning and NLP methods improves recommendation systems, making them more effective for platforms like Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube Music. Future research can further optimize these models by incorporating user listening behavior and song metadata for even better personalization.

Title: Improving Sentiment Classification Accuracy using Engagement and Temporal Features from Social Media Data
Abstract: Sentiment analysis has become an important instrument to gain insight on user attitudes, brands and trends in online behavior and digital platforms. This paper addresses this aspect by conducting a recognizable study of an approach encompassing all the available methodologies on classifying sentiment in three categories, i.e. positive, negative and neutral as well as traditional Machine Learning (ML) models, ensemble approaches and a stacking-based combination approach. Different independent classifier models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB) mode have been tested with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) features on a sentiment dataset that has undergone preprocessing. Hard voting and extended voting using multiple learners are applied to make a more significant improvement in performance. It shows the biggest benefit in a stacking ensemble model, where LR, NB and SVM are implemented as base learners, and Random Forest (RF) serves as a meta-learner. The findings confirm the usefulness of using hybrid ensemble models in sentiment classification particularly when sparse and moderate sized data sets are involved.

Title: Deep Learning Based Multimodal Biometric Authentication using Iris and Speech
Abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital era, securing identity verification systems is critical, particularly with the rise in sophisticated cyber threats. This study presents an innovative biometric authentication system based on deep learning, which combines iris recognition with speaker identification. The iris features are extracted using pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as ResNet101, while speech features Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), energy, pitch, and frequency are derived using digital signal processing techniques. These features are concatenated and passed to a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for final classification. The system is trained using a synthesized dataset formed from the Iris of the Eye dataset and the CMU ARCTIC speech corpus. It achieves an outstanding 98.5% identification accuracy, outperforming several unimodal and state-of-the-art methods. Robustness is further analyzed under speech noise injection and modality mismatch scenarios. The integration of CNN and LSTM architectures demonstrates superior learning of both spatial and sequential biometric traits, paving the way for more secure and intelligent for significantly strengthen authentication reliability and accuracy.

Title: Early Detection of Knee Osteoporosis Using Fine-Tuned VGG19 Model on X-ray Images
Abstract: Usually resulting in major mobility problems and pain, knee osteoporosis (KO) is a common disorder compromising bone strength and raising the risk of fractures. Effective therapy depends on early diagnosis; but conventional techniques include clinical examination and bone mineral density tests can ignore early-stage bone abnormalities. This work uses a customized VGG19 deep learning model to predict knee osteoporosis from X-ray pictures. Leveraging transfer learning, the VGG19 model known for its great performance in image classification was modified for binary classification (healthy against osteoporotic). With both Healthy and Osteoporosis categories, the model was trained and validated on a dataset of knee X-rays including 1,258 training images, 315 validation images, and 472 testing images. With great accuracy of 97.5%, high precision, recall, and F1-scores of 0.97 for both classes, the model performed really remarkably. With just 12 false negatives and low misclassification no false positives the confusion matrix exposed Although sporadic variations in validation loss indicated minor overfitting, the general training and validation accuracy curves showed consistent learning and good generalization. This work validates the ability of deep learning models especially VGG19 in automating knee osteoporosis detection and thereby enhancing diagnosis accuracy. Title: A GeneSwarm-Enhanced Hybrid Ensemble Model for Predicting Cardiac Outcomes in Kawasaki Disease
Abstract: Kawasaki Disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis that may cause coronary artery lesions (CAL) in case it is not diagnosed and treated early. The problem of complicated clinical data and nonspecific markers has complicated proper forecasting of the long-term KD outcomes. This paper suggests a hybrid ensemble machine learning model to use XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers and soft voting in order to have robust and interpretable predictions. The GeneSwarm Feature Selector was used to select the features based on the Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization which can optimally identify the most informative and non-redundant clinical and laboratory features. The Babysitting algorithm was used to optimize hyperparameters dynamically and Interquartile Range (IQR) to eliminate outliers and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to deal with class imbalance were used during preprocessing. Assessed on 1,850 paediatric KD cases, the proposed model demonstrated a 97.10% accuracy, 96.50% precision, 96.80% recall, 96.60% F1-score, and a macro-AUC of 97.40% and is better than the current ML methods. Best predictive variables were Complications, Clinical Outcomes, Treatment Approach, Echocardiography, Laboratory Tests, Fever Duration, and Symptoms. These findings indicate that the framework is a reliable, interpretable, and clinically applicable instrument of early KD prognosis, which helps to plan personalized treatment and stratify risks. Through the incorporation of superior feature selection, ensemble learning, and a solid preprocessing, the research will add to an empirical and pragmatic method of enhancing cardiac care in pediatrics.

Title: Multimodal NLP-Audio Approach for Early Alzheimer's Detection Using BERT and Acoustic Embeddings
Abstract: Alzheimer's disease, or AD, requires early diagnosis to intervene and reverse the progression of the condition. In this paper, a strong multimodal scheme is proposed by incorporating Natural Language Processing (NLP) and signal processing of the acoustic signal to detect early indications of AD. The postulated system will use Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) to capture semantic and syntactic information of transcribed speech and acoustic information through Melfrequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) and pretrained sound models like VGGish. The methodology comprises broad preprocessing of the datasets of clinical interviews, extraction of linguistics and acoustic embeddings, and combination of these features through a late-fusion-based design in a deep neural network framework. The pipeline includes the modular sets of steps, such as pre-processing, training, evaluation, and realtime inference using a web interface. Performance was found to be an overall accuracy of 92% on labelled clinical data. Its system allows effortless interaction with the users through uploading audio or inputting text and produces results interpretable with clinical suggestions. In the future, we will extend the dataset with multilingual and nonhomogeneous speech samples, adopt methods of explainable AI, e.g., SHAP and LIME, and also support longitudinal monitoring of cognitive dynamics and the optimization of the framework to run on edge hardware that would allow us to screen people remotely in resource-limited areas.

Title: Identifying Fake Audio Using Social Media Metadata and Audio Features
Abstract: With a rise in AI generated audio, more commonly referred to as audio deepfakes, it has become increasingly important to detect fake audio content especially as it spreads across social media. While most detection methods rely only on analyzing the sound itself, they often miss important clues found in social media engagement data. In this work, we introduce a new approach that combines both audio features (such as, spectrograms, energy levels, tempo, and pitch-related measurements) and social media metadata (such as likes, dislikes, and comment counts) to determine whether an audio clip is real, or AI generated. We developed an ensemble model that brings together five different machine learning methods being, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and a Neural Network which uses a stacking approach to improve overall prediction. We compared the results acquired from this model to the results of well known papers, including CFAD, Singfake, and ASVspoof 2019. Our model achieved an AUC of 0.847, accuracy of 84.6%, and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 20.4%, showing that it performs similarly, if not better, than existing methods that use only audio. These results suggest that combining sound with social context offers a promising and practical way to detect deepfake audio, especially in a real world social media setting. While our model achieved moderate performance (AUC of 0.847), it highlights the potential and limitations of combining social and audio features in deepfake audio detection, and opens avenues for future tuning and dataset expansion.

Title: SOBi-Net: A Soft Ordinal and Bidirectional Fusion Network for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
Abstract: Automated Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) grading is crucial for preventing blindness; however, existing methods face two primary challenges:'Ordinal Blindness' and 'Scale Insensitivity'. To address these issues, a soft ordinal and bidirectional fusion network (SOBi-Net) is proposed. To tackle 'Ordinal Blindness,' a Soft Ordinal learning paradigm is introduced, which explicitly embeds clinical ordinal relationships into the loss function by optimizing a smoothed target probability distribution. For 'Scale Insensitivity,' a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network is designed to efficiently fuse multi-scale features from the backbone network, enabling the robust identification of lesions ranging from microaneurysms to neovascularization. Experiments conducted on the public APTOS2019 dataset show that the proposed model achieves excellent performance on key ordinal metrics, with a Quadratic Weighted Kappa of 0.9288 and an accuracy of 85.06%. This performance demonstrates its significant potential as an efficient, accurate, and clinicallyaware solution for automated DR grading.

Title: Emotion Detection in Indonesian Music Comments Using BERT, Traditional Machine Learning and Their Hybrid Model
Abstract: In the era of digital communication, social media comes as a platform to express honest feelings and opinions, especially in Indonesia where user engagement continues to increase. Music, often related to emotions, gives various reactions in comments on social platforms. However, detecting emotions from Indonesian-language comments is still a challenge due to the use of informal language, emoticons, etc. This research proposes and evaluates three approaches: traditional machine learning employs TF-IDF and SVD for feature extraction, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, and a hybrid model that combines both. The results show that BERT achieves the highest accuracy (79%). The hybrid model achieves an accuracy of 77% with the training time (0.97 s). Meanwhile, logistic Regression alone offers the fastest performance (0.35 s) with the lowest memory usage but lower accuracy (64%). This study highlights the potential of hybrid approaches to balance accuracy and computational efficiency, contributing to a better understanding of musicrelated emotional expression in Indonesian online communities.

Title: Research on the Technical Principles and Performance Verification of SoVITS Speech Synthesis Model
Abstract: In recent years, the naturalness and quality of speech generated by text-to-speech (TTS) framework based on deep learning have been greatly improved. The purpose of synthesizing understandable and natural audio from text has long been the research topic of artificial intelligence, natural language and speech processing. Aiming at the problems existing in traditional text-to-speech (TTS) technology, such as weak training ability with few samples, low naturalness of cross-language synthesis, poor controllability of emotional expression, lack of emotional expression and large amount of target speaker corpus, this paper systematically analyzes the technical framework and operating mechanism of SoVITS speech synthesis model, and focuses on the principle of its acoustic generation part. It aims to transform the emotional state of speech from one to another, while retaining the language information and the identity of the speaker. By designing multi-dimensional experiments involving few samples training and emotion control, the performance of the model is finally verified on LibriSpeech and AISHELL standard data sets, and the joint optimization goal is constructed by introducing reconstruction loss, confrontation loss and semantic alignment loss. The experimental results show that when the training sample duration is only 5 minutes, the naturalness (MOS) of SoVITS synthesized speech is 4.63, and the similarity (COS) of the embedded cosine of the speaker is 0.835. This model provides an efficient solution for the generation of speech synthesis content with low resources and few samples.

Title: Randomized Neural Network with Multiple Output Layers for Multi-label Classification
Abstract: Multi-label classification (MLC) applications span numerous real-world domains, including music annotation, medical diagnosis, and biological analysis, where instances may be associated with multiple categories simultaneously. However, MLC is a challenging problem due to imbalanced label distributions that exist in multi-label data, making accurate prediction more complicated. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Label ensemble deep Random Vector Functional Link (ML-edRVFL) framework that extends the edRVFL architecture with multiple output layers to multi-label setting by integrating three adaptive thresholding techniques and two ensemble aggregation rules. The framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets from diverse domains. The experimental results show that the proposed ML-edRVFL models achieve competitive performance in comparison to the baseline methods.

Title: Thyroid Disease Identification via EfficientNetB2: Leveraging Deep Neural Networks for Early Detection
Abstract: Hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism are thyroid diseases that can harm human health by influencing the brain, heart and ability to have children. Correctly identifying these disorders in the early stages allows patients to recover faster and gets treatment underway more efficiently. Typically, doctors order imaging and blood tests for diagnosis and each can be time-consuming and costly. It is suggested that using a modified version of EfficientNetB2 for deep learning will improve and simplify how thyroid disorders are diagnosed. The model was set up with two divisions - 0 for healthy and 1 for thyroid illness - using photos of more than 7,200 different thyroid conditions. Making some changes to the data, transforming the images, keeping them the same size and enriching it resulted in a robust model. On the assessment of thyroid illness and healthy groups, the EfficientNet B2 model performed extremely well and was accurate 90% of the time. Using a confusion matrix, loss curves and classification criteria, the performance of the model was evaluated, leading to a well-balanced strategy that helps avoid many unneeded positive or negative results. This work supports the healthcare sector by providing easy access to early detection, encouraging health care and encouraging the development of sustainable medical methods. The findings prove the instrument can detect thyroid illnesses early, as EfficientNetB2 is an automation method that runs fast and is capable of scaling up.

Title: The Synergy of Consumer Perception and AI Success in Driving Business Optimization
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of information and communication technology marked by the era of digitalization in various sectors, businesses are increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to improve operational efficiency and strategic decision-making. Although many studies have explored the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on business performance and consumer behavior separately, there is still limited understanding of how consumer perceptions and AI implementation interactively affect businesses. Most existing studies tend to focus on the technical success of AI devices or on consumer trust and acceptance separately, without examining how these dimensions collectively contribute to measured business outcomes. This study investigates the influence of consumer perceptions and AI implementation on business quality, with a particular focus on the moderating role of AI implementation success. The research method used is a survey with the main instrument in the form of a questionnaire distributed to 120 employees from various companies that utilize AI technology in their companies. Consumer perceptions play a significant role in determining how innovations such as AI are accepted and trusted, which directly affects customer engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty. The implementation of AI devices - such as predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and customer service chatbots - can contribute significantly to internal communication processes and external service delivery. Of the three variables tested against Business Process Optimization, only AI Implementation Success did not show a significant effect, while AI Implementation and Employee Perception of AI were shown to have a positive and significant effect. Thus, AI Implementation does not moderate the relationship between Consumer Perception and AI Implementation on Business Optimization.

Title: A Multifaceted Approach Based on Deep Learning Architectures for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
Abstract: Dysarthric speech presents significant challenges to effective communication and overall quality of life. Traditional diagnostic methods are often subjective and time-consuming, limiting both the accuracy and efficiency of detecting this condition. In response, this study proposes a novel automated system for dysarthric speech recognition, designed to improve diagnostic precision and timeliness. The proposed system adopts a comprehensive framework that integrates advanced signal processing techniques, robust feature extraction methods, and cutting-edge deep learning architectures. Multiple acoustic features, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients 'MFCCs' and Power-Normalized Cepstral Coefficients 'PNCCs', are extracted to capture detailed characteristics of the speech signal. Additionally, speech enhancement algorithms such as Minimum Mean Square Error 'MMSE' based noise reduction are applied to improve input quality, especially under noisy conditions. At the core of the system lies a deep learning model combining Convolutional Neural Networks 'CNNs' with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory 'BiLSTM' networks. This architecture effectively captures both local and temporal dependencies within speech signals. To further enhance performance, the Connectionist Temporal Classification 'CTC' approach is incorporated for word level recognition in dysarthric speech. CTC is particularly beneficial in speech recognition tasks as it enables training sequence to sequence models without requiring strict alignment between input features and output labels. The system's performance has been thoroughly evaluated on the UASpeech dataset, showing notable effectiveness in handling speech with low intelligibility.

Title: Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Spoken Language Understanding for Resource-Constrained Microcontroller Unit
Abstract: Speech input is increasingly adopted as an intuitive interface for various embedded mobile devices. Cloud-based solutions provide powerful speech language understanding (SLU) capabilities but introduce privacy risks, as sensitive information may be processed remotely. To address these concerns, disentanglement-based encoders have been developed to strip sensitive data from audio signals, allowing SLU without compromising privacy. However, such encoders are often memory-intensive and computationally demanding, limiting their practicality on resource-constrained devices. Based on extensive experiments, this paper observes a key phenomenon: SLU relies on global information from the entire sentence, whereas the recognition of privacy-sensitive words predominantly depends on local information. We implemented simple encoder designed for efficient privacy-preserving SLU offloading (SILENCE) on an STM32H7 microcontroller and evaluated its performance under various privacy threat scenarios. Results demonstrate that SILENCE provides competitive speech intent classification accuracy and privacy protection compared to more complex encoders. Simultaneously, it achieves a speedup of up to 53.3 times and a reduction in memory footprint by 134.1 times, marking the first time that privacy-preserving SLU services have been realized on a microcontroller with only 1 MB of memory.

Title: Improving ViT Performance for Colon Cancer Histopathological Image Classification Using Transfer Learning
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized medical image analysis, particularly the automatic classification of histopathology images. Vision Transformers (ViTs) now surpass convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in modeling long-range dependencies and capturing global features. However, when initialized with random weights, ViTs often struggle to adapt to the varying scales and morphologies of tumor tissues, resulting in suboptimal performance. Transfer learning addresses this challenge by pretraining the model on large datasets to obtain a stronger weight initialization before fine-tuning on the target domain. This strategy has proven especially effective for histology image classification. In this study, we fine-tuned a ViT-B/16 model pretrained on ImageNet-21k by first training it on 75,000 Renal Cell Carcinoma (RCC) patches and then applying it to classify colon tumor subtypes in the Chaoyang dataset. Our proposed method achieves an accuracy of 87.14 %, a precision of 83.59 %, a recall of 82.08 % and an F1 score of 82.77 %, outperforming both a model trained from scratch and one pretrained only on ImageNet. These results underscore the value of domain-specific pretraining for enhancing ViT performance on diverse tumor morphologies in histopathology classification tasks.

Title: Deep Transfer Learning for Poultry Disease Classification: A Case Study with EfficientNetB3
Abstract: Poultry rearing is a significant food safety and economic stability factor especially among the small to medium sized farmers in the developing nations. However, timeliness and effective diagnosis of chicken illnesses has been the biggest issue because the number of veterinary practitioners and diagnostic centers remains low. The current paper aims at automating the process of detecting the chicken diseases through a deep learning algorithm used on the fecal image image analysis. The data was compiled into an annotated set of 8,067 fecal images (6,453 of which are training images) and 807 validation images and 807 test images. The model applied in this study is the EfficientNetB3 algorithm that has been famous in providing the best balance between performance and computation efficiency. The model was able to achieve the impressive 98% accuracy on test set through extensive training and optimization and had the potential to be a valuable instrument in the diagnosis of disease. This is a technology-driven approach that can be used to provide early diagnosis and prompt treatment, resulting in the improved health of animals, food security and economic growth. Furthermore, sustainable agriculture, responsible consumption and production, and heightened resilience of agricultural systems are other features that such technology promotes - the goal that is consistent with global ambitions to achieve zero hunger, good health and well-being, and industrialization towards innovation.

Title: Maximizing Speech Denoising Effectiveness with CNNs: A Focus on Key Architectural Strategies
Abstract: Audio signal denoising is important in speech enhancement. Most traditional methods cannot remove noises thoroughly and models proposed recently still achieve poor performance in denoising under low SNR conditions. This paper proposed a model whose speech denoising performance is higher than that of most models. The model is based on convolutional neural network and is added several strategies to improve its metrics. The importance of strategies like residual connection, batch normalization, Dropout regularization and "encoder-decoder"processing mode in the model is illustrated in the paper. The metrics used in the paper is MSE, SNR, PESQ and STOI. Studies show that the proposed model performs better in the four metrics and over-high or over-low Dropout ratios can affect the performance negatively.

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Tabnet and Deep Learning Models for Chronic Kidney Disease Diagnosis: Enhancing Interpretability and Predictive Accuracy
Abstract: This study compares TabNet with other deep learning models, including Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), for diagnosing chronic kidney disease (CKD). The work aims to enhance both prediction performance and model interpretability in clinical diagnosis. CKD advances quietly, and hence detection becomes challenging early in the course of the disease using traditional methods such as GFR, creatinine levels, and urinalysis, particularly in wide-ranging patient populations. Machine learning algorithms, implemented across varying datasets - such as clinical, laboratory, and patient data - improve diagnostic specificity. While DNNs and CNNs identify intricate non-linear patterns, interpretability restricts their application in high-risk medical judgments. As opposed to that, TabNet, designed for tabular data, employs sequential attention to mark salient features while deciding, with transparency and accuracy. The data set analysis has shown that Tab Net achieved 94 % which is higher than the existing CNN and DNN algorithms. The research emphasizes TabNet's edge in providing interpretable decision paths, highly important for clinical trust and use. By comparing such models, this paper offers insights into the selection of proper diagnostic instruments, facilitating personalized treatment planning, and the development of explainable AI in nephrology.

Title: Student Depression Prediction: A Multimodal Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: In today's world, Depression among students has been a critical mental health concern that substantially impacts desired outcomes, productivity, and overall human well-being. Traditional diagnostic instruments involve conventional medical tools, classical diagnostic apparatus, or conventional diagnostic equipment such as the PHQ-9 questionnaire provide effective clinical measures but lack of ease of use in digital-first environments. This paper put forward a plan for multimedia machine learning (ML) framework that integrates behavioral features (mobility, smartphone usage, sleeping patterns) and other feature like linguistics features (related to language text contents from essays and posts on social medias) to estimate depression. A dataset of 820 university students was taken and compared with PHQ-9 scores as ground truth labels. Hereby the functioning of models including BERT, RoBERT, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and a Fusion Ensemble was evaluated. Title: A Lightweight CNN-based Explainable Approach for Potato Disease Detection with Deep Evaluation Metrics
Abstract: The potato is a major staple food crop across the globe; it plays an important part in food security and sustaining agricultural economies. Potato disease is very dangerous to yield loss when the potato plant infected with diseases like early blight, late blight, etc., as this could cause huge losses when not detected and identified earlier enough. The assessment of diseases is still a manual process performed by agronomists and this approach is slow, inconsistent, and not practical for assessing disease for commercial scale monitoring. This research describes the development of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for the automatic classification of potato leaf disease into early blight, late blight, or healthy. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 98.38%, and does not suffer from degradation in performance having used a lightweight architecture. The model was assessed beyond accuracy; precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix and ROC-AUC curves were used to assess performance, providing a more comprehensive insight into performance for each class. Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) was used to aid the interpretability of the CNN by highlighting regions of the leaf image relative to disease, reminding us of the role and impact of explainable AI (XAI) in agricultural disease detection. Overall, findings indicated that the CNN was accurate, efficient, and had trust; a good proposition for a real-world precision agriculture harvest technology.

Title: Intelligent expert system fault diagnosis based on PCA-SPE-CNN classifier
Abstract: Centrifugal compressors are widely used in the oil and natural gas industry for gas compression, reinjection, and transportation. To address the challenges of the difficult separation of data anomalies from equipment failures and limited knowledge acquisition from expert knowledge bases, this article proposes a dynamic fault diagnosis method for centrifugal compressor expert systems, combining convolutional neural networks (CNN) and principal component analysis for statistical process monitoring (PCA-SPE). Realize the combination of expert knowledge and instrument data, and break through the weak links in existing petrochemical instrument safety monitoring technology and traditional expert systems. The method has been validated using process data from centrifugal compressors. The results demonstrate that the method achieved 100% classification accuracy for two types of faults: non-starting of the drive machine and excessively low oil pressure. Combined with the expert system, it reached a satisfactory diagnostic performance.

Title: Deep Analysis of MFCC, LPC, MEL Spectrogram, and Weighted Features to Classify Stuttered and Non-Stuttered Speech
Abstract: Speech serves as the verbal tool for expressing thoughts, ideas, and emotions, and is essential for human interaction. Stuttering is a speech disorder that impacts millions of individuals worldwide. The determination of whether an individual stutters or does not stutter is conducted through assessments in Speech Language Pathology (SLP). Traditionally, this evaluation involved manually counting the instances of stuttering within speech to classify individuals as either stutterers or non-stutterers. Therefore, the process is time-consuming and susceptible to mistakes. Stuttering speech recognition has been a well-focused area of study within speech signal processing for researchers in recent decades. The present research focuses on identifying stuttered and fluent speech and highlighting its performance in deep learning methodologies. This study examines an in-depth evaluation of the CNN & Bi-LSTM model utilizing MFCC, LPC, and MEL spectrogram features. Additionally, the weighted features of these have also been evaluated by our deep learning methods for the classification of stuttered and fluent speech. A comparison has been carried out on the efficiency achieved from the CNN & Bi-LSTM models utilizing different types of features. Research indicates that the CNN model achieves an impressive accuracy rate of 92% compared to the Bi-LSTM model when utilizing weighted MFCC.

Title: Ta Ka Di Mi: AI for Konnakkol and Rhythm Training
Abstract: We present Ta Ka Di Mi, an AI-powered mobile application designed to make rhythm training and Konnakkol-the South Indian art of vocal percussion-accessible to learners worldwide. Konnakkol is a centuries-old tradition where rhythmic syllables are recited to convey complex tala (time cycles or rhythmic frameworks), often serving as both a pedagogical tool and a performance art. While deeply rooted in South Indian classical music, rhythm itself is a universal language, integral to music, dance, speech, and movement across cultures. Despite this universality, learning Konnakkol has traditionally required close mentorship, consistent practice, and significant exposure to expert practitioners, making it less accessible outside specialized communities. Our system addresses these challenges by combining modern AI technologies with carefully curated pedagogical content to create an interactive, scalable, and user-friendly learning experience for global audiences. The application integrates automatic speech recognition, audio signal processing, and real-time feedback models to evaluate learners across multiple dimensions: rhythmic accuracy, pronunciation fidelity, and tempo consistency. Through gamified lessons, learners can progress from foundational exercises to advanced rhythmic improvisations, guided by structured modules designed in collaboration with renowned artist B.C. Manjunath. The AI-driven evaluation engine provides instant personalized feedback, enabling learners to refine their skills iteratively and at their own pace. In addition, the app incorporates adaptive learning strategies that track a user's growth over time and dynamically suggest exercises tailored to individual strengths and weaknesses. Our demo highlights the unique intersection of cultural heritage and modern AI, showcasing how domain-specific AI/ML techniques can be applied to music education in a globally meaningful way. Beyond traditional music training, Ta Ka Di Mi supports diverse use cases, including rhythm practice for dancers and instrumentalists, therapeutic interventions for speech and motor coordination, and cross-cultural exploration for learners worldwide who seek rhythm as a bridge across traditions. By blending ancient tradition with contemporary technology, the platform not only preserves and disseminates an important cultural practice but also reimagines how rhythm can be taught, experienced, and shared universally. Ultimately, Ta Ka Di Mi demonstrates how AI can democratize access to art forms, enhance pedagogy through personalized insights, and foster global community-building around rhythm. In bridging the gap between ancient tradition and modern technology, the system illustrates the potential of AI-powered education platforms to enrich cultural learning and inspire new creative possibilities across the world. A short demo video is available at: https://youtu.be/LveumJymJ-M.

Title: A Method for Zebrafish Egg Viability Identification Based on Improved YOLOv8
Abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of zebrafish egg viability is crucial for high-throughput screening in biomedical research. Although deep learning-based object detectors like YOLOv8 offer feasible solutions, their performance in detecting semi-transparent and small zebrafish eggs within complex microscopic images remains suboptimal. To address this, this paper presents a comprehensively enhanced YOLOv8 model. Specifically, we introduce the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) into the backbone network to enhance feature representation by focusing on salient regions; adopt a weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) for more effective multi-scale feature fusion; and replace the original IoU loss with the EIoU loss function to achieve more accurate bounding box regression. Evaluation on a self-constructed dataset containing 8,992 instances shows that the proposed method achieves an mAP@0.5 of 98.2%, representing a 3.1% improvement over the baseline YOLOv8n model.

Title: Noise Suppression using Multi Scale Feature Extractor and Channel and Sequence Attention
Abstract: A highly efficient deep neural network architecture is introduced for real-time speech enhancement and noise suppression on resource-constrained devices. The method utilizes a two-phase processing framework with channel-wise feature reorientation and a Channel and Sequence Attention (CSAtt) module to reduce computational cost while retaining state-of-the-art performance. Modified power law compression further optimizes perceptual quality and robust speech estimation. Extensive testing on established datasets demonstrates that the approach matches or surpasses leading solutions such as DeepFilterNet2 with only 25% computational complexity. These results emphasize the potential for deploying advanced deep learning models in IT and IoT environments, aligning with the conference goal of promoting innovative artificial intelligence solutions for real-world applications.

Title: Fuzzy-Deep Learning Hybrid Model for Voice and Fluency Assessment in English Literary Performance
Abstract: Reading fluency is an essential component of reading teaching, especially for students encountering literacy difficulties. It differentiates competent readers from those who struggle and serves as a robust indicator of reading comprehension challenges. Upon mastering decoding skills, the subsequent essential stage is to enhance fluency, particularly within the realm of English literary performance. This research presents a technique for evaluating Voice and Fluency in English literary performance utilising FuzzyRNN. The methodology underscores the significance of data preparation and feature extraction, since the calibre of input data profoundly affects model efficacy. Utilising fuzzy numbers for data modelling enables the system to encapsulate human-like perceptions and tackle the uncertainties present in voice and fluency evaluation. The recurrent connections of the FuzzyRNN facilitate a streamlined network architecture while improving its capacity to generalise from fuzzy input. Of the four models evaluated, FuzzyRNN exhibited the highest forecasting accuracy at 94.53%, surpassing its competitors. The results indicate that FuzzyRNN can function as an effective instrument for enhancing fluency assessment in educational settings. The adaptive and perceptual modelling features provide a viable solution for real-time, automated assessment systems, enhancing the efficacy of reading instruction and literary performance evaluation.

Title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection and Classification of Ovarian Cancer from Medical Imaging
Abstract: Ovarian cancer remains one of the most lethal types of gynaecological cancer because it advances asymptomatically and is often identified at an advanced stage. Early and precise identification is a critical to maintain health. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning (DL), have shown significant potential for enhancing computer-aided diagnosis and medical picture analysis. This study presents a DL-based system for the automated detection and classification of ovarian cancer utilising medical imaging techniques. The extraction of distinguishing features and categorisation of benign and malignant cases with high precision is achieved through the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning techniques. The proposed approach is evaluated using publicly accessible datasets and clinical datasets, demonstrating superior performance relative to traditional machine learning (ML) methods in accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. DL models possess the capability to serve as valuable, dependable, and scalable instruments that can aid radiologists in the early detection and classification of ovarian cancer. This will ultimately enhance patient outcomes and facilitate tailored treatment planning. The results underscore the potential of deep learning methods.

Title: A Lightweight Attention Convolutional Network for End-to-End Monaural Speech Separation
Abstract: Existing single-channel speech separation methods often rely on complex deep neural network architectures, such as convolutional neural network and recurrent neural network. These approaches suffer from high model complexity and poor real-time performance, especially in resource-constrained scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight attention convolutional network (LAC-Net), centered around a Lightweight Multi-Branch Attention Block (LMBA Block). This module integrates Ghost Module, Channel Split and Channel Shuffle operations, as well as an improved Convolutional Block Attention Module. It significantly reduces model parameters and computational cost while effectively enhancing speech feature modeling and separation performance. Extensive experiments were conducted on WSJ0-2mix, Libri2Mix, and the selfconstructed Chinese datasets NJUST603-2Mix and NJUST6033Mix. The results demonstrate that LAC-Net consistently outperforms several classical baseline models in terms of SDRi and SI-SNRi. While maintaining a compact model size, LACNet exhibits stable performance in multi-speaker scenarios and achieves favorable results in real-time evaluations, highlighting its strong generalization ability.

Title: VisionAid Edge: Design and Technical Feasibility Study of a Multimodal Assistive System for Visually Impaired Individuals
Abstract: Vision impairment affects 2.2 billion people worldwide, while existing assistive technologies face fragmentation through single-modality approaches, privacy concerns from cloud dependency, or cost barriers exceeding Rs. 3 lakh. This paper presents VisionAid Edge, a cyber-physical system integrating multimodal artificial intelligence on low-cost edge hardware while preserving privacy through on-device processing. The architecture combines object detection (YOLO11n via NCNN), Indian currency recognition (ONNX), ultrasonic ranging with haptic feedback, offline voice control, and Global Positioning System (GPS) alerts on Raspberry Pi 4. To address thermal and power constraints, adaptive input resizing, two-frame temporal filtering, and priority-based audio queuing are applied. Technical characterization over five 100-minute trials demonstrates currency recognition accuracy of 87.3 percent on 900 test images, median text-to-speech latency of 275 milliseconds, sustained throughput of about two to three frames per second (FPS), and 3.2-hour battery life on 37 Wh power. Face encodings use PBKDF2-derived AES-256 encryption. Results establish that low-cost edge platforms (Rs. 10,400) can support integrated assistive functionality with acceptable performance. Complete implementation is opensourced to enable user studies and deployment.

Title: LLM-Guided Multimodal Scene Captioning via Prompt-Based Fusion of Visual and Auditory Descriptions
Abstract: Understanding complex scenes in real world environments often demands more than visual analysis alone it requires the integration of both visual and auditory cues. This study investigates whether prompt-based fusion using large language models (LLMs) can effectively combine modality specific outputs for zero-shot scene captioning. We propose a modular framework that leverages BLIP-2 for visual captioning, Whisper for audio transcription, and FLAN-T5 for prompt-driven fusion. To simulate multimodal caption pairs, we augment the COCO image caption dataset with text-to-speech (TTS) generated audio and incorporate filtered real-world audio-image samples. Unlike prior approaches requiring joint training or architectural modification, our pipeline operates entirely in zero-shot mode with no model retraining. Evaluation using BLEU, ROUGE-L, and cosine-based semantic similarity reveals that our fusion strategy, despite its simplicity, achieves semantically coherent captions across modalities. This work demonstrates the feasibility of LLM-guided fusion for assistive AI and offers a reproducible, low-resource solution for applications such as smart narration, AR/VR accessibility, and navigation aids for visually impaired users.
