Title: Bangla Speech to IPA Transcription: A Multi-Stage Transformer-Based Approach
Abstract: The International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) provides an exact way to represent speech sounds across different dialects, making it crucial for tasks like linguistic research and pronunciation-focused applications. Precise IPA transcription plays a significant role in areas such as speech therapy, language education, and the preservation of endangered languages. This paper presents a multistage approach for transcribing Bangla speech into IPA, aiming to improve phonetic accuracy and offer a modular solution tailored for low-resource language contexts. The pipeline consists of two stages: speech-to-text transcription and grapheme-to-phoneme IPA conversion. We used two curated Bangla datasets with diverse phoneme coverage, addressing limitations in existing datasets. The first stage employs a customized automatic speech recognition (ASR) model based on transformer architectures, inspired by recent multilingual ASR advancements. Title: Toward Early Detection of Prediabetes in Children: A Multimodal Analysis of Oral, Cutaneous, and Metabolic Indicators
Abstract: Early detection of pre-diabetes in children and adolescents is essential to prevent its progression to type-2 diabetes. In paediatric settings, conventional diagnostic approaches relying on invasive blood tests often pose practical and psychological challenges. This study investigates the feasibility of using external physiological indicators, specifically tongue and skin features, as non-invasive markers of early metabolic alteration. To support this objective, a tri-modal screening framework integrating clinical parameters with machine-learning-based image analysis is proposed to enable patient-friendly assessment. The dataset comprises 127 synthetically generated clinical image cases, with a mean participant age of 14.13 years. From these images, a total of 152 quantitative features were extracted, including GLCM-based texture metrics, colour-distribution descriptors, and high-dimensional deep-learning representations. These visual features were analysed alongside metabolic indices such as HbA1c and fasting blood glucose. The ensemble model that combined all modalities achieved an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.94, with a sensitivity of 92% and specificity of 88%, demonstrating strong diagnostic potential. Overall, the findings support the use of visual cues as a viable, non-invasive approach for early pre-diabetes screening in paediatric populations. Validation on larger, real-world, and demographically diverse cohorts will be essential for future clinical adoption.

Title: Evaluation of Accuracy, Information Quality, and Readability of Artificial Intelligence Based Chatbots in Pediatric Oral Surgery: A Comparative Analysis Based on the AAPD Clinical Guideline
Abstract: Objectives: Chatbots powered by artificial intelligence are increasingly used as tools for obtaining medical and dental knowledge. This study aimed to assess and compare the performance of four AI chatbots in providing evidence-based information on pediatric oral surgery topics, with reference to the American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry (AAPD) clinical guideline. Materials and Methods: This descriptive observational study evaluated four AI chatbots (ChatGPT-5, Gemini, Copilot, and DeepSeek) by posing 20 questions derived from the AAPD Guideline on Management Considerations for Pediatric Oral Surgery. Responses were assessed for accuracy using the grading system, for quality using the 16-item DISCERN instrument and for readability using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) formula. Non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment were employed for statistical comparisons (p < 0.05). Results: Significant differences were observed among chatbots in all outcome measures. Gemini and ChatGPT-5 achieved the highest accuracy scores (1.30 ± 0.47 and 1.40 ± 0.60, respectively; p = 0.001), whereas DeepSeek and Copilot showed lower accuracy. In terms of information quality, DeepSeek produced the highest DISCERN scores (52.90 ± 3.73; p < 0.001), followed by Copilot. ChatGPT-5 and Gemini yielded more readable outputs (10.73 ± 1.98 and 11.68 ± 1.91, respectively), though readability differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). Conclusions: Of the models evaluated, Gemini and ChatGPT-5 produced the most accurate responses, while DeepSeek generated the highest-quality content. While AI chatbots show promise as supplementary tools for patient education and clinical learning in pediatric oral surgery, their reliability varies considerably across platforms. Continuous validation and guideline-based evaluation are essential prior to clinical integration.

Title: Detection of Apple Mosaic Disease Based on YOLOV5 Model
Abstract: The apple industry occupies an important position in the global agricultural economy, but the yield and quality of apple mosaic disease are seriously threatened, and it is urgent to achieve accurate and efficient detection of the disease. In order to solve the problem of insufficient accuracy of traditional detection methods due to complex shape characteristics (such as irregular patches, twisted leaf veins and scattered punctate lesions) of apple mosaic diseases, an optimization solution based on YOLOv5 deep learning model was proposed. Firstly, a large-scale disease image dataset covering major production areas, multiple climatic conditions and growth stages in the world was constructed, focusing on the collection of leaf characteristic data with different environmental backgrounds and disease levels. Then, by improving the network structure parameters, optimizing the multi-scale feature fusion strategy and adjusting the weight of the loss function, the ability of the model to capture subtle disease features was significantly improved. The experimental results show that the optimized YOLOv5 model has achieved breakthrough detection performance in complex orchard scenes: The detection accuracy of irregular plaque lesions has been improved, the recall rate of twisted leaf vein lesions has been greatly improved, and the key indicators are significantly better than those of the comparison model. This achievement provides high-precision technical support for the intelligent monitoring of orchard diseases, and effectively solves the problem of identifying complex disease spot features.

Title: Music Popularity Prediction Platform
Abstract: Predicting the popularity of songs has long been a challenge in the music industry due to rapidly changing listener preferences and evolving production practices. This is an empirical study with a deployed prototype. It applies machine learning techniques to audio features and temporal metadata spanning six decades of music to predict whether a track will achieve commercial popularity. Four models were developed and evaluated, including a tuned Random Forest with decade encoding, which demonstrated superior performance in terms of F1-score and ROC-AUC. Stratified sampling and per-decade validation ensured robustness against temporal bias, while feature importance analyses revealed danceability, instrumentalness, and acousticness as key predictors. SHAP-based explainability methods provided transparency into model decisions, enhancing trust and interpretability. A Streamlit-based application was also deployed to offer an interactive interface for exploring predictions, enabling threshold tuning and scenario testing. Results suggest that integrating temporal context with acoustic features improves predictive accuracy and provides actionable insights for playlist curation, artist scouting, and trend forecasting. The platform's ranking, calibration, and explainability support practical Artist scouting, repertoire triage and playlist curation, offering measurable screening efficiency and transparent decision support for labels and distributors

Title: Deep Learning for Predicting Drug-Drug Interactions and Patient Safety in Dental Clinical Trials
Abstract: This paper introduces a new model, named Deep Federated Transformer Graph Attention Network (DFT-GAT), to predict drug-drug interaction (DDIs) to improve patient safety in dental clinical trials. The proposed model is based on the PyTorch 2.x and includes multimodal data sources: molecular structures, clinical records, and treatment notes, which are processed with the help of an attention-based fusion mechanism to learn features holistically. With the federated learning paradigm, model training can be done in more than one dental center, and the data privacy and adherence to the clinical rules must be provided. Graph attention module focuses on capturing the inter-drug associations, whereas SHAP-based explainability enables easy understanding of the results of decisions, enhancing clinical trust and interpretability. Experimental analyses showed better performance with accuracy of 93.8% and AUC-ROC of 0.962 and exceeding the current deep learning benchmarks. These findings indicate that the framework can provide scalable, interpretable, and privacy-aware predictions and that DFT-GAT is a powerful AI-based instrument in dental pharmacological analysis to provide safe and efficient predictions.

Title: Academic Confidence in the Age of AI: A Study on Chatbot-Assisted Learning Among Graduate Learners in Hospitality and Tourism Management
Abstract: This study examines the relationship between chatbot-assisted learning and academic confidence among graduate students in Hospitality and Tourism Management programs in Metro Manila. Grounded in Bandura's Self-Efficacy Theory, the research employed a quantitative, descriptive-correlational design involving 350 Master's and PhD students. Data were gathered using adapted Likert-scale instruments and analyzed through Pearson correlation and linear regression. Findings revealed no significant correlation between chatbot usage and academic confidence, suggesting that while students frequently engage with AI tools, such interactions may not meaningfully influence their self-belief in academic performance. These results challenge assumptions about AI's impact on learner psychology and highlight the limitations of current chatbot systems in fostering self-efficacy. The study contributes to the discourse on digital learning by emphasizing the need for emotionally intelligent, feedback-rich AI integration. Future research should explore mediating variables to uncover the nuanced dynamics between technology and learner confidence.

Title: Hear little and Help big - LSTM Enhanced Temporal signal Processor for Infant Vocalization Analysis
Abstract: Hear Little and Help Big' proposes an LSTMbased Temporal Signal Processing pipeline for real-time infant cry analysis, aiming intelligent neonatal monitoring and early detection of distress. The system is based on spectrogrambased preprocessing and extraction of MFCC features to convert cry audio into formatted temporal representations, which are analyzed by a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network involved in classifying the cries into hunger, pain, or discomfort categories. Integrated with a context sensing decision engine, the model translates classifications into prescriptive caregiving actions and sends automatic notifications via an integrated notification module. Built for low-latency systems, the framework exhibits strong performance on noisy datasets and provides a scalable solution for AI-augmented infant care in clinical and home environments. Yet, this model could be constrained by the sample size and demographic makeup of the training dataset, potentially imposing biases on generalization over heterogeneous infant populations. Although early results are encouraging, wider assessment and comparison with current state-of-the-art cry analysis systems would be necessary to establish its full efficacy.

Title: From Noise to Clarity: Emerging Trends in Speech Enhancement for Real-Time Communication
Abstract: Real-time communication demands speech that is both intelligible and natural, even in noisy environments. This paper traces the progression of speech enhancement from traditional DSP techniques-such as spectral subtraction and Wiener filtering-to modern deep learning and diffusion-based models. While classical methods offer low latency and interpretability, they falter in complex, non-stationary noise. Deep neural networks, including CNNs, RNNs, and transformers, brought adaptive, data-driven noise suppression with superior performance. Most recently, diffusion models have redefined the state-of-the-art, enabling high-fidelity speech reconstruction from heavily corrupted inputs. We present a comparative analysis of these approaches in terms of effectiveness, latency, and deployment feasibility, and highlight the promise of hybrid models that unify DSP precision with generative AI power.

Title: Synthetic Speech Detection via Multi-Generator GANs with Anomaly Detection Architectures
Abstract: Advancement in text-to-speech and voice conversion have enabled highly realistic synthetic voices, resulting in threats to cybersecurity, and fraud prevention. Classic classifiers and deep learning models often struggle to generalize across diverse spoofing conditions. In this work, we propose two improved anomaly detection architectures for synthetic speech detection: Enhanced D-AnoGAN (eD-AnoGAN) and Multi-generator RESGANomaly (RES-MGANomaly). eD-AnoGAN removes the bandit prior by directly assigning clusters to generator-encoder branches and incorporates a latent consistency loss during training, while RES-MGANomaly extends RES-GANomaly by introducing multiple residual-attention generators with shared encoders. On WaveFake, eD-AnoGAN with latent consistency achieves the highest performance with an AUC of 0.9211 and F1 of 0.8957, while RES-MGANomaly also performs strongly with an AUC of 0.9030. In cross-dataset evaluation on ASVspoof2019 LA, eD-AnoGAN attains the best generalization with an AUC of 0.8428 and F1 of 0.7956. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-generator anomaly detection in improving robustness against synthetic speech attacks.

Title: Vox2Brief: Summarizing Conversational Medical Narratives
Abstract: This paper provides a thorough analysis and evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) capacities, in this case the performance of the OpenAI Whisper Medium model. We describe the end-to-end system architecture for audio processing and transcribing, and its rigorous assessment using industry-standard jiwer library metrics: Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), and Match Error Rate (MER). Experimental performance on a well-chosen audio sample, we show the model's exceptional ability to translate spoken English into text. We also use a Flan-T5-based summarization module to translate medical accounts into patient-readable accounts. The strong performance obtained indicates the extensive value of large-scale pre-trained models in bridging the gap between human speech and digital text across many applications. In addition, the paper explains the implications of such great accuracy for real-world deployments and specifies directions of future research, such as large-scale evaluation on multiform datasets and investigation of real-time ASR systems. This paper adds to the increasing amount of knowledge about state-of-the-art ASR model performance in real-world cases and their ability to improve human-computer interaction.

Title: Enhancing Digital Strategic Performance in Higher Education through AI-Enabled Strategic Capabilities

Title: A Biochemical Reaction Anomaly Detection System Based on Stage-Awareness and Spatiotemporal Features
Abstract: Biochemical reaction instruments are vital for nucleic acid testing, but anomalies like uneven liquid stratification, bubble interference, or mechanical failures during extraction can cause experimental errors and resource wastage. Traditional sensorbased monitoring faces limitations in coverage, cost, and realtime performance. This study presents a video-based anomaly detection system for nucleic acid extraction, tested on a laboratorydeveloped instrument. The system combines ResNet18 for adaptive video segmentation, CLIP ViT-B/32 for robust visual feature extraction, Bi-LSTM for temporal dependency modeling, and PU learning to address data imbalance, enabling real-time anomaly detection. Evaluated on a self-constructed dataset with simulated anomalies, the model achieves a ROC AUC of {0. 7 7 8 4, } {8 0} percent accuracy, and zero false negatives, ensuring clinical safety. This work's core value lies in developing an integrated stageaware spatiotemporal framework (ResNet18+CLIP+Bi-LSTM) to address sensor-based monitoring limitations, designing a weighted loss and adaptive threshold for clinical safety, and enabling early intervention within the 6 -minute extraction phase-reducing reagent waste by 90-95 percent, saving 45-90 minutes per detection, and offering a scalable solution for high-throughput testing and other biochemical instruments.

Title: Explainable Deep Learning Approach for Automated Classification of Retinal Diseases Using OCT Images and Grad-CAM
Abstract: The retinal conditions cause the most vision loss across the globe, and it is necessary to diagnose the retinal disease properly and in time. Optical Coherence Tomography, also known by the initials OCT, is a non-invasive imaging test of the retina characterized as being in high-resolution, cross-sectional imaging, and through it, the detection of disease is possible. The proposed approach was a deep learning-based solution to automating the classification of retinal OCT images into four classes, including CNV, DME, DRUSEN, and NORMAL. Daily, a huge amount of approximately 85,000 labeled OCT images was used to develop and train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. A massive preprocessing was done on the dataset involving resizing the images, converting the RGB values, and data augmentation to improve model robustness and generalization. The CNN model proposed was trained by Adam optimizer and took 10 epochs to attain 96% accuracy in terms of classification performance, appreciable precision, recall, and F1-score in all categories. Grad-CAM visualization was performed to enhance interpretability; areas relevant to disease were highlighted in OCT images, and the manner in which the model reached its decision provided visual decisions. The findings prove the potential of deep learning techniques, with the help of explainability methods, to be a fruitful and trustworthy instrument in the diagnosis of retinal disease and help ophthalmologists during clinical decision-making.

Title: AFTR-HAR-Net: Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Reasoning Network for Robust Human Activity Recognition
Abstract: In this era, Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has become a crucial component in healthcare monitoring, fitness tracking and smart IoT applications. Specifically, attaining accurate classification still struggles with various challenges where the deep learning approaches have limitations with multimodal fusion and efficient temporal modelling that leads to suboptimal performance on sensor data. Therefore, to resolve these limitations, this research proposes an Adaptive Fusion and Temporal Reasoning Human Activity Recognition Network (AFTR-HAR-Net) which is a lightweight robust framework that combines adaptive sensor fusion, a dilated Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) encoder and an Attention-guided GRU temporal reasoning module. In particular, the adaptive fusion mechanism learns modalityspecific significance weights which assists to improve resilience to sensor imbalance, then the dilated CNN captures multi-scale temporal features with minimal computational cost. Further, the GRU and attention layers helps to refine temporal dependencies which improves the discrimination of overlapping activities. The proposed AFTR-HAR-Net acquired higher results with 98.12% accuracy and 97.89% F1-Score when compared with the existing hybrid model namely CNN with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory.

Title: A Network with High-Frequency Feature Extraction and Feature Recalibration Mechanisms for Chinese Speech Recognition
Abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, speech recognition has become an important form of humancomputer interaction. Chinese speech recognition faces unique challenges due to tones, homophones, and dialect differences. To enhance recognition performance and robustness, a novel network named LCHANet was proposed. A DSCSE module that combines depthwise separable convolution (DSC) and squeeze-andexcitation (SE) networks, along with a lightweight-improved attention mechanism (FECA), is included in this model to achieve efficient feature extraction and channel recalibration. Compared with the baseline model, the LCHANet proposed in this paper has reduced the character error rate (CER) by 13.45% on the THCHS-30 dataset. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each module, demonstrating that both the FECA and DSCSE modules play crucial roles in performance improvement. The proposed method delivers an efficient and precise solution for Chinese speech recognition, showcasing remarkable performance.

Title: Spoken Language Recognition for Indonesian Local Languages Using Deep Learning
Abstract: This paper presents a spoken language identification (LID) system for seven Indonesian local languages: Acehnese, Balinese, Batak Toba, Javanese, Sundanese, Yawa, and Rote. The dataset was constructed from audio.sabda.org, with recordings standardized, normalized, and segmented into 3-second utterances to ensure consistent input. Three deep learning architectures were evaluated: a baseline CNN, ResNet-50, and DenseNet-121, trained on multiple acoustic features including MFCC, log-Mel spectrograms, and shifted delta coefficients (SDC). Hyperparameters were optimized using random search, resulting in nine best-performing configurations. Experimental results show that deeper architectures substantially outperform CNN, with ResNet-50 trained on SDC achieving the highest overall performance (81 % accuracy, FRR 0.19, EER 0.07, C avg 0.11). Per-class analysis reveals that Balinese and Rote are recognized with near-perfect accuracy, while Batak Toba and Javanese exhibit higher error rates due to phonotactic similarities. Compared to prior work, the proposed system achieves competitive performance despite being trained on a relatively small dataset. The findings confirm that residual networks combined with temporal features provide a robust backbone for low-resource spoken language identification, and highlight promising directions for extending research on Indonesian languages.

Title: A General Classification Framework for Detecting AI-Generated Voices
Abstract: The rapid advancement of deepfake voice synthesis technologies has led to increasing misuse cases, including impersonation, misinformation, and fraud. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-generated voices offer legitimate benefits, their misuse poses growing cybersecurity threats. This paper presents a general classification framework for detecting AI-generated voices across Sinhala, Tamil, and English languages. Publicly available datasets for multilingual deepfake voice detection, particularly in low-resource languages such as Sinhala and Tamil, remain limited, with most existing models focused primarily on English. To address this gap, an acoustic dataset covering Sinhala, Tamil, and English was created using real voice samples either recorded or sourced from public datasets and synthetic samples generated through Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC) techniques, including tools such as Google Translate and Resemble AI. A hybrid CNN-LSTM model was developed to classify voices as real or synthetic. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) were extracted and fed into separate CNN-LSTM models trained for each language. The proposed system achieved over 95% test accuracy across all three languages, demonstrating robust cross-linguistic performance. The findings offer a foundation for scalable, AI-driven deepfake voice detection frameworks adaptable to diverse linguistic and regional contexts.

Title: Real-Time Financial Risk Modeling Using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: — Traditional financial risk modelling methodologies frequently fail to capture complicated, nonlinear patterns in real-time data in the age of highfrequency trading and turbulent global markets. In order to improve forecast accuracy and responsiveness, this article investigates the incorporation of deep learning techniques into real-time financial risk modelling. We create models that can interpret large, dynamic financial datasets in real-time by utilising cutting-edge architectures like Transformer models, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Real-time trading signals, sentiment analysis from news and social media, and macroeconomic factors are added to previous market data to train these models. Significant gains in predicting accuracy and risk identification are seen when the study compares the performance of DL models to traditional risk models like Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR). We also discuss issues such managing noisy, non-stationary data, latency limitations, and model interpretability. The findings show that DL techniques can greatly improve the accuracy and promptness of risk forecasts, providing financial organisations with an effective instrument for proactive risk control. Deep learning may revolutionise real-time risk assessment and decision-making, as this study shows, adding to the expanding field of Al-driven finance. A realtime, adaptive deep learning-based financial risk modelling framework proposed in the proposed study has a fundamental contribution to the current state-of-the-art practices. In contrast to classical statistical or batch-trained machine learning models which assume fixed data and require time to inquire about it, this literature uses streaming deep learning models, namely the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to perpetually learn on-the-fly based on real-time data streams in the market.

Title: Bringing Llama-3 to the Edge: End-to-End Quantized Conversational AI on Raspberry Pi 5
Abstract: Deploying conversational AI systems on resource-constrained edge computing devices requires sophisticated optimization techniques to ensure computational efficiency without compromising performance quality. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the optimization and deployment of an end-to-end conversational AI pipeline - comprising Whisper automatic speech recognition (ASR), a 3-billion parameter Llama-3 large language model (LLM) and lightweight text-to-speech (TTS) - running entirely on a Raspberry Pi module. Multiple quantization levels are benchmarked across two inference stacks, Ollama and the lower-overhead llama.cpp. The evaluation is conducted in two phases: first, by analyzing the metrics for individual components and second, by assessing the overall pipeline. The results show that implementing a lower bit quantized version of llama.cpp within the pipeline yields significant improvements in latency and energy consumption compared to the higher bit baseline, with only a marginal reduction in coherence. Similar results are observed for the Ollama deployment. These findings demonstrate that strategic quantization and runtime optimizations facilitate the practical deployment of conversational AI systems on edge devices, maintaining high conversational quality while paving the way for locally executed, privacy-preserving AI applications.

Title: Hybrid Deep Learning with ConvNeXt and Self-Attention for Pulmonary Disease Classification
Abstract: Pulmonary lung detection represents a critical challenge in modern neuroimaging, with significant implications for timely medical intervention. In this study, we use the IQ-OTHNCCD lung cancer classification dataset to introduce a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) with ConvNeXt-inspired convolutional blocks for effective lung disease classification. The proposed model captures both local spatial features and long-range dependencies that are necessary for spotting subtle and scattered problematic patterns. Following a sequence of convolutional layers with Layer Normalization for initial feature encoding, ConvNeXt-style blocks that integrate depth-wise convolution, Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU)-activated multi-layer perceptron's (MLPs), and residual connections are used. Tokenized spatial depictions are moderate to MHSA in order to improve global contextual comprehension. The proposed method shows superior performance in multi-class pulmonary lung classification with 98.4% accuracy, 96.3% precision, 97.0% F1-score, and 97.7% recall without compromising computational efficiency. These findings demonstrate the stability and generalizability of our approach, which makes it an optimistic instrument for automatic clinical pulmonary lung disease identification.

Title: Recording Environment and Microphone Recognition in Cymbal Audios Using Machine Learning
Abstract: Although machine learning techniques are commonly used in audio forensic analysis to identify recording devices and environments, the music industry can also benefit from this type of application, mainly because it is a little-explored approach. In this sense, this work aims to use this type of approach to assess whether different recording conditions - specifically microphones and environments - contribute to increasing the variability of audio signals in a way that simulates similar musical instruments, increasing the number of samples in a limited set of instruments. A dataset of cymbal audio recordings was analyzed using a logistic regression model combined with Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV) to evaluate the classification of microphones and environments. Results indicate that the recording environments significantly impacted signal variability, achieving classification accuracy of 99%, whereas the influence of microphone types was minimal, with classification performance around 52%.

Title: Harnessing Grey Wolf Optimization for Early Thyroid Cancer Prediction
Abstract: Thyroid cancer is an increasing worry for medical professionals, who recognize that early identification is crucial for effective treatment. Machine learning (ML) advancements have generated significant prospects for improving the speed and precision of thyroid cancer detection. The current diagnostic instruments' lack of accuracy and clarity obstructs prompt patient care. Thus, improving clinical decision-making in this domain requires optimizing prediction models. This study assesses a hybrid diagnostic model that incorporates feature selection methods, such as sequential feature selection and recursive feature removal, enhanced by grey wolf optimization (GWO), using the Kaggle Thyroid Cancer Disease Dataset. The objective is to determine the most efficient prediction models for the early and precise identification of thyroid cancer. The suggested hybrid technique demonstrated outstanding performance, with an accuracy of 98.87%, precision of 100%, sensitivity of 94.84%, specificity of 100%, and F-measure of 97.33% across several assessment criteria, setting it apart from the nine hybrid models examined. The results suggest that machine learning models can substantially enhance the accuracy of thyroid cancer detection by GWO-based feature selection and optimization. This technology may improve patient outcomes and reduce strain on healthcare systems by enabling the creation of more efficient and accurate diagnostic tools.

Title: Automated Multi-Class Fault Diagnosis of Photovoltaic Panels Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
Abstract: The performance of the photovoltaic (PV) systems continues to be part of the sustainable energy production, however, it is often compromised by a range of environmental and physical defects. Even though the automated monitoring methods have a significant potential, previous studies have focused on binary classification, which usually distinguishes between clean and dusty panels. The range of conditions that require special maintenance is not considered in such models. This shortcoming is addressed in the current paper by suggesting and testing a multi-class fault diagnosis system of solar panels. Two lightweight and very efficient deep-learning(DL) models, MobileNetV3Small and EfficientNet-B0, are used to classify PV-panel images into six categories which are operationally very critical, namely Clean, Dusty, Snow-Covered, Bird Droppings, Physical Damage, and Electrical Damage. These models are fine-tuned on this subtle task with the help of transfer learning and data augmentation on a publicly-available dataset. Title: Advancing Inclusive Education and Accessibility Through Regional Flexibility in TTS Systems by Indian English Accent Detection
Abstract: This study examines the application of machine learning techniques for recognizing and differentiating regional accents in Indian English, with the broader aim of improving the inclusivity and contextual suitability of speech technolo-gies in India's linguistically diverse environment. Using the Indic TTS dataset from IIT Madras, we analyzed speech samples from male and female speakers across eight states, resulting in 16 distinct accent classes. Mel-Frequency Cep-stral Coefficients (MFCC) were employed for acoustic feature extraction, and multiple classifiers-including Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and XGBoost-were trained and evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved the highest reported accuracy of 99.02 %, followed closely by Random Forest (98.86 %) and CNN-LSTM (98.70 %). These results underscore the potential of accent-aware models to enhance recognition performance and cultural adaptability in speech systems. Beyond improving general speech recognition, the system has applications in accent-specific speech synthesis, personalized voice assistants, call-center automation, and educational tools for language learning and pronunciation feedback.

Title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Speech-Based Dementia Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Dementia is a progressive neurodegenerative disease in which early diagnosis continues to be a challenge as a result of constraints of the traditional, invasive diagnosis procedures. The use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models (RNNs, CNNs, and Transformer-based architectures) to classify dementia based on speech data are systematically assessed in this review. Multimodal models with diagnostic accuracy of over 90 have been built using benchmark datasets such as Dementia Bank and ADReSS and have very efficient feature integration strategies which combine acoustic (MFCCs, jitter, shimmer) and linguistic (semantic embeddings) features. The review is quantitative in cost-benefit improvements in methodology and presents systematic issues such as the lack of diversity of datasets and lack of interpretability of the models, and research gaps in multilingual adaptation and clinical scalability. This work made a contribution in terms of a summarized analysis of the performance and a series of guidance on the overall progress of speech-based, non-invasive, and explainable dementia diagnosis to effective clinical implementation.

Title: Smart Diagnostic System for Multiple Respiratory Diseases Using Lung Sounds
Abstract: In the present world pollution is increasing rapidly, which is causing health issues in human beings. The major issue is with respect to the lung. The problem is also due to bad habits like smoking. To identify the problem in the preliminary stage we are proposing a 'Smart diagnostic system for the automated classification of multiple respiratory diseases using lung sound recordings'. Motivated by the limitations of traditional auscultation, the system employs a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model trained on Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) extracted from the ICBHI 2017 Respiratory Sound Database. The proposed architecture effectively captures both spatial and temporal features in respiratory signals, enabling accurate detection of conditions such as Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Pneumonia, Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (URTI), and Bronchiolitis. Extensive preprocessing, including noise reduction, segmentation, and data augmentation, improves model robustness against real-world acoustic variability and class imbalance. The system achieves a classification accuracy of 93.2%, with strong performance on COPD and Pneumonia classes. The findings suggest the model's potential as a lowcost, scalable tool for AI-assisted pulmonary diagnostics, particularly in resource-constrained environments.

Title: Embodied Conversational Virtual Humans in 3D Environments: Towards Scalable and Immersive AI Interactions
Abstract: We present a fully automated conversational virtual human system developed in Unity, designed for scalable and immersive human-AI interactions in 3D environments. The system integrates real-time voice activity detection for automatic turn-taking, speech-to-text transcription, text response generation, and text-to-speech synthesis with synchronized lip animation. Unlike prior systems, our approach facilitates fluid, naturalistic dialogue in customizable 3D environments. To provide initial validation, we conducted a study with 17 participants evaluating conversational experiences in both virtual reality and PC. Results indicate the system achieves low latency (mean 2.30s total response time) and is perceived positively by users regarding speed, likeability, and accuracy, while highlighting areas for improved clarity. Although conversational realism ratings were comparable or favored PC, participants preferred the VR modality, citing immersion and co-presence as key factors. These findings demonstrate the system's usability and the significant role of immersion in enhancing embodied conversational AI interactions.

Title: AS-ASR: A Lightweight Framework for Aphasia-Specific Automatic Speech Recognition
Abstract: This paper proposes AS-ASR, a lightweight aphasiaspecific speech recognition framework based on Whisper-tiny, tailored for low-resource deployment on edge devices. Our approach introduces a hybrid training strategy that systematically combines standard and aphasic speech at varying ratios, enabling robust generalization, and a GPT-4-based reference enhancement method that refines noisy aphasic transcripts, improving supervision quality. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple data mixing configurations and evaluation settings. Results show that our fine-tuned model significantly outperforms the zero-shot baseline, reducing WER on aphasic speech by over 30% while preserving performance on standard speech. The proposed framework offers a scalable, efficient solution for realworld disordered speech recognition.

Title: Voice Conversion: Transformation Through Deep Learning
Abstract: Voice conversion is a technique that converts a speaker's voice into another while retaining the original content. The main goal of this research is to enhance the quality of voice conversion system that well exhibits speaker identity while ensuring naturalness and intelligibility. To accomplish this, we introduce a three-stage pipeline using a deep learning-based approach. The Encoder draws speaker-specific features from the input speech, the Synthesizer produces mel spectrograms that maintain the linguistic and acoustic features of the target speaker, and the Vocoder synthesizes the final waveform to generate natural-sounding speech. The method is trained on varied speech datasets to achieve robustness over various speakers. Experimental outcomes confirm that the system efficiently alters speaker identity without losing speech clarity and prosody, resulting in high-fidelity voice conversions. The results highlight the capabilities of deep learning in progressing voice transformation technology. Future studies will aim at optimizing real-time performance, enhancing prosody conservation, and furthering speaker similarity, paving the way for use in personalized voice assistants, speech synthesis, and assistive technology.

Title: Air Condition Diagnosis System in Laser Directed Energy Deposition Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: In the air condition diagnosis system of laser directed energy deposition, equipment failures can lead to transient contamination, which in turn causes oxygen levels to rise by hundreds of ppm quickly, surpassing the requirement of ≤qslant 2 0 ppm for high-end components and thus degrading product performance. To address this issue, this paper constructs a fault diagnosis model based on a lightweight CNN (Convolutional Neural Network)-Transformer hybrid network to provide basic diagnostic capabilities for the system. It takes a five-dimensional atmospheric sensor sequence, including intake flow rate, exhaust flow rate, chamber pressure, and oxygen content (sensors 1 and 2), as input. It extracts local mutation features through convolution and then uses a single-layer Transformer encoder to characterize the global coupling relationships among multiple parameters. At the data level, for the difficult-to-classify category, Z-score anomaly removal, Robust Scaler independent standardization, and class weight enhancement are implemented to alleviate the problem of class imbalance. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.99%, a Macro-F1 value of 97.94%, and the F1 value for the difficult-to-classify category increases to 1.000, significantly outperforming other baseline models, such as 1D-CNN and CNN-RNN. This establishes a basis for monitoring and diagnosing laser additive manufacturing processes and other complex atmospheric systems.

Title: MERCI: A Multimodal Dataset for Personalised and Emotionally-Aware Dialogues
Abstract: The integration of conversational agents into daily life has become increasingly common. However, sustaining deeply engaging and natural interactions remains challenging due to a lack of multimodal datasets capturing personal and emotional nuances. In this paper, we introduce MERCI (Multimodal dataset for Emotionally-aware peRsonalised Conversational In-teractions), a dataset derived from user-robot dialogues involving thirty participants who completed user profile questionnaires covering ten personal topics (e.g., hobbies, music). A conver-sational system called PERCY then engaged with each partici-pant in open-domain conversations, leveraging GPT-4, real-time facial-expression and sentiment analysis to generate contextu-ally appropriate, empathetic responses. MERCI contains 1860 utterances, equating to about 12.5 hours of aligned audio, three-view video, transcripts with timestamps, emotion labels, and sentiment scores. This dataset serves as a reproducible test-bed for tasks such as emotion-aware response generation, multimodal affect recognition, and personalised policy learning. Baseline performance results have been established using advanced models such as BERT, T5, BART, and GPT-3.5/4/4o-mini across gener-ation, regression, and classification. Evaluations through human and automated methods have demonstrated strong naturalness, relevance, and consistency in responses while indicating areas for enhanced personalisation and empathic depth. We expect that MERCI will enhance the development of emotionally intelligent, user-centric conversational AI applications, potentially ranging from social robotics to mental health support.

Title: Phonetic Analysis of Real and Synthetic Speech Using HuBERT Embeddings: Perspectives for Deepfake Detection
Abstract: The growing sophistication of speech generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced new challenges in audio deepfake detection. Text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) technologies can now produce convincing synthetic speech with high quality and intelligibility. This poses a serious threat to voice biometric security systems, such as automatic speaker recognition. It also increases the risks associated to the spread of spoken disinformation, where synthetic voices can be used to disseminate malicious content. In this study, we conduct an analysis of real and synthetic speech at phonetic and word levels. For that, a parallel dataset comprising real and synthetic speech signals were developed based on a subset of the LibriSpeech ASR corpus. Synthetic speech samples were generated using two TTS and one VC systems: Coqui TTS, VITS TTS, and StarGANv2 VC. We adopted HuBERT, a self-supervised speech model, to extract speech embeddings. The motivation for using this model stems from its ability to recognize sound units corresponding to the so-called pseudo phonemes. Our analysis is based on the KL divergence (KLD) between the distributions of synthetic and real phonemes, which allowed us to rank synthetic phonemes based on their alignment with their real counterpart. We also trained several classifiers per phoneme to distinguish between real and synthetic samples. We then compute the correlations between KLD and accuracies per phoneme. Besides showing a list of phonemes that are more discriminative, our findings suggest that vowels correlate better with the classifiers' performance, suggesting that the KLD can be an indicator of the most distinguishable phonemes for deepfake detection.

Title: HAF-Net: Hierarchical Attention Fusion Network for Multimodal Image Fusion
Abstract: Fusing medical images from diverse modalities like MRI, PET, and SPECT helps improve diagnostic precision by combining their complementary features. However, existing deep learning-based fusion methods often suffer from limited detail preservation and inefficient attention modeling across spatial and channel dimensions. This study introduces an innovative framework called hierarchical attention fusion network (HAF-Net) for robust and high-quality medical image fusion. The proposed model incorporates a hierarchical feature aggregation (HFA) module to extract scale-adaptive features, and a residual attention convolution (RAC) block to enhance fine-grained details using gradient-aware spatial and frequency-domain information. Furthermore, a multispectral frequency-aware channel attention (MFCA) mechanism is introduced to capture discriminative features across multiple frequency bands, and a cross-interaction attention module (CIAM) is designed to jointly model spatial-channel relationships. An adaptive fusion weighting (AFW) strategy is employed to dynamically combine multi-scale features based on their contextual relevance. Extensive experiments on standard PET/MRI and SPECT/MRI datasets demonstrate that HAF-Net achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art fusion methods. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed modules in preserving structural integrity and enhancing detail in fused medical images.

Title: Privacy-Preserving Real-Time Conversation Summarization with Local AI on Wearable Devices
Abstract: Real-time conversation summarization is increasingly vital for professionals across domains such as healthcare, legal, and corporate communications. This paper presents a privacy-preserving wearable system that captures spoken conversations, performs on-device preprocessing using an ESP32 microcontroller, and transmits the audio to a locally hosted AI server for realtime summarization. The proposed architecture integrates Web Sockets for efficient data transfer, OpenAI Whisper for robust speech-to-text conversion, Pyannote for speaker diarization, and Ollama LLM for abstractive summarization. All processing is performed locally to eliminate external data exposure. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the system's effectiveness in achieving low latency, high transcription accuracy, and coherent summarization, establishing its applicability for secure and context-aware conversation analysis.

Abstract: Integrating with AI in the education sector is becoming crucial and impactful for students' English performance and analyzing junior high school students' perceptions of teaching effectiveness across AI, local, and native English teachers in Taiwan, there is still limited empirical evidence on how students perceive on this, without such understanding the attempt of Bilingual 2030 policy which might limited alignment with students need. Title: Enhanced Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through LightGBM and Advanced Feature Optimization
Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) refers to a complicated neurodevelopmental disorder that influences social interaction, verbal communication, and adaptability of behaviour. This is important because early diagnosis can greatly enhance the long-term. Nonetheless, conventional machine learning methods and traditional approaches to diagnosis are prone to redundancy of attributes, high dimensionality, reduced generalization, and lower diagnostic accuracy. To overcome the difficulties, the current research proposes an ASD detector in the form of Light GBM. As the primary dataset, the ASD Children Traits Dataset, which comprises Behavioral indicators and demographic information, is utilized. During the preprocessing phase, numerical variables are normalized to stabilize and accelerate convergence. The extraction of features is used to realize the underlying Behavioral patterns. Further, the feature selection procedure is applied to extract the most informative features (Sequential Feature Selection (SFS). This helps to reduce redundancy of features and to increase their interpretability. Lastly, LightGBM was used as a classifier option, including Exclusive Feature Bundling (EFB) and Gradient-based One-Side Sampling (GOSS) to easily work with structured data. The experimental assessment showed good performance with an accuracy of 0.99 %, precision of 1.0 %, recall of 0.99%, F1-score of 0.99 %, and ROC-AUC of 1.0%. These findings substantiate that LightGBM has better predictive performance and can be regarded as an advanced and highly reliable predictive instrument to detect ASD in its initial stages.

Title: Real-Time Voice Signal Classification for Identifying Emergency Scenarios using Deep Learning
Abstract: Screams are among the distinctive auditory cues that are often produced during emergencies such as violent incidents, medical crises, and public disturbances. Public safety and quick emergency response depend on the timely detection of these sounds. Manual reporting is the foundation of traditional emergency response systems, resulting in inefficiencies and delays. This study suggests a real-time voice signal classification system that analyses auditory signals to identify emergency situations to overcome this limitation. The system divides sound into emergency and non-emergency categories using deep learning techniques. To enable precise classification, melspectrogram representations of audio signals are subjected to temporal and spatial feature extraction using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. A carefully selected dataset of emergency and nonemergency sounds is used to train the model, and features are pre-processed and normalized prior to training. The proposed system is designed for real-time performance, ensuring quick detection and automated SOS alert generation.

Title: EffWhiS: A Proposed Efficient Approach for Speech-to-Text Streaming Whisper
Abstract: Whisper Streaming is an emerging approach for real-time automatic speech recognition (ASR), extending OpenAI’s Whisper model, and using local agreement to commit transcriptions. However, its reliance on fixed chunk sizes and local agreement often causes unnecessary delays or premature outputs. To address this, we propose an efficient Whisper Streaming (EffWhiS), a refined streaming algorithm that enhances Whisper’s responsiveness and accuracy through two key strategies: (1) majority-vote commit, which commits a word if it appears in at least two of the last three decoding passes; and (2) segment consistency constraint, which allows commits only when consecutive segment predictions agree. The benchmark ESIC corpus and two hours of recordings of actual Vietnamese meetings are used to evaluate our proposed EffWhiS. The findings show that, in comparison to the original Whisper Streaming, EffWhiS achieves a lower Word Error Rate and a significantly lower Average Commit Latency. Notably, EffWhiS maintains high accuracy even at a short chunk size of 0.5 seconds, confirming its robustness for practical streaming ASR deployments. These improvements are consistent across various chunk sizes in both English and Vietnamese, highlighting the generalizability of our proposed approach. With its balance between accuracy and latency, EffWhiS offers a potential path for effective and deployable streaming ASR systems.

Title: Designing Musical Instrument Identification Systems Using Lightweight Machine Learning Architectures

Title: An Improved ResNet50-based Speech Recognition System
Abstract: To address the limitation of low accuracy in traditional machine learning-based speech recognition, this paper innovatively proposes a speech recognition system based on an improved ResNet50 model. The initial ResNet50 model is enhanced by incorporating the CBAM module and the ReliefF feature selection algorithm. Experimental results show that the negative branch regularization method has minimal impact on recognition accuracy, thereby enhancing the model's anomaly detection ability without compromising its recognition performance.

Title: A Multilayer Perceptron Approach to Detecting Mental Health Conditions from Music Preferences
Abstract: Early identification of mental health disorders is essential to allow timely interventions and improve overall well-being. This study explores the potential of using Machine Learning (ML) to detect mental health conditions, specifically depression, anxiety, insomnia, and Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD), based on individual preferences of the music genre. The dataset containing anonymized music listening behavior and self-reported mental health statuses was collected and preprocessed. Four ML classifiers, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), were used and evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation and an 80:20 train-test split. The experimental results indicated that MLP produced the highest classification accuracy for depression is 58% and anxiety is 60%, while NB demonstrated superior performance in detecting OCD with 81% of accuracy and insomnia with 66% accuracy value. These results highlight the feasibility of using music preferences as noninvasive indicators for mental health screening. Future research should aim to incorporate heterogeneous data sources and conduct clinical validation to enhance the accuracy and reliability of the proposed approach.

Title: Hybrid AI-Physics Framework for Lost Circulation Zone Diagnosis: A Data-Driven Iterative Approach Integrating Drilling-Logging Big Data with Theoretical Models
Abstract: This paper develops a hybrid AI-physics framework designed to enable real-time, cost-effective diagnosis of loss zones in complex formations. The framework integrates drilling and surface logging big data with physics-based models to address two critical industry challenges: (1) the high uncertainty of manual theoretical calculations and (2) the delays and costs of post-event instrument-based measurements. By using real-time data, it rapidly determines loss zone characteristics (depth, channel type, and fracture dimensions), enhancing treatment success rates and holding the potential to reduce operational costs. A Sichuan Basin database was constructed from over 100 wells using an event-based approach, capturing time-series data around lost circulation events. Theoretical models for determining loss zone depth, identifying lost circulation channel types, and estimating fracture width were evaluated through statistical error analysis. AI optimization methods tailored to each theoretical model were selected, and corresponding AI-physics hybrid models were developed independently, followed by training and validating these models on a database randomly split with 80% allocated for training and 20% for validation. These hybrid models were embedded into the Engineering Intelligent Support Center (EISC) with real-time drilling and surface logging parameters to establish loss zone diagnostic framework. A machine learning-enhanced drilling hydraulics model was developed to calculate the loss zone depth using real-time drilling and surface logging parameters, achieving a test set mean error of 4.06%-4.87%, representing a 10%-48% reduction compared to theoretical models. A convolutional neural network-based intelligent classification model was established to identify lost circulation channel types, leveraging geometric features of loss rate vs. time and mud pit volume vs. time curves to distinguish natural fractures, induced fractures, microfractures/high-permeability pores, and medium-to-large fractures/caverns, with a test set accuracy exceeding 94%. An ensemble learning model integrating AdaBoost with solid- and liquid-phase lost circulation dynamics was constructed to invert fracture width, utilizing drilling fluid or lost circulation material slurry flow data, reducing test set mean errors to 12.07%-42.73%, an improvement of up to 73.46% over theoretical methods. Field trials across over 20 wells in the Sichuan Basin demonstrated that, following post-lost circulation events, engineers could access real-time drilling and surface logging data via the field-deployed Framework connected to the EISC, rapidly determining the loss zone depth, channel type, and fracture width to inform lost circulation control strategies. The framework achieved a field-validated diagnostic accuracy exceeding 85%, with ongoing updates to lost circulation data expected to further enhance precision. This work introduces the first EISC-integrated hybrid AI-physics framework for loss zone diagnosis. It bridges the gap between data-driven AI and physics-based models, enabling rapid, cost-effective diagnosis with acceptable accuracy and without additional downhole instrumentation. The framework offers engineers a practically validated tool for decision-making in lost circulation treatment, balancing theoretical rigor with AI adaptability.

Title: Conformer-Driven Nonnegative Matrix Factorization: A Unified Optimization Framework for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement
Abstract: A hybrid architecture integrating Conformcr encoders with multichannel Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) is proposed for speech enhancement. The model leverages the global-local feature extraction capabilities of Conformer blocks while preserving the interprctablc spcctrospatial decomposition of NMF through differentiable multiplicative update rules. This study derive a unified optimization framework based on the majorization-minimization of the multichannel Itakura-Saito divergence, enabling joint learning of spectral and spatial parameters in an end-to-end manner. The proposed approach effectively combines the strengths of deep learning and traditional probabilistic modeling: the Conformer encoder captures long-range contextual dependencies and complex acoustic patterns, while the NMF structure ensures interpretability and stability in spectro-temporal decomposition. Experimental results on the CHiME dataset demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance across multiple objective metrics, including SDR, PESQ, and STOI, validating its effectiveness in real-world multi-channel speech enhancement tasks.

Title: From Reactive to Proactive: How IoT Re-Imagines Healthcare Delivery Systems
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess how Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have revolutionized healthcare delivery, with an emphasis on resource optimisation, clinical results, and operational efficiency. In three crucial areas-hospital asset management, smart medical equipment utilization, and remote patient monitoring-the major goal is to compare healthcare organizations that have implemented IoT technologies with those that have not. In order to do this, the study examines how IoT-enabled systems are implemented in operating rooms and examines how they affect procedural efficiency and surgical safety. In order to create a responsive and integrated healthcare environment, the project also investigates the integration of IoT devices designed for patients and surgical personnel. IoT, which sits at the nexus of medicine and technology, is being studied as a tactical instrument to tackle enduring issues in healthcare, including medication shortages, medical blunders, system overloads, and disruptions caused by pandemics. The approach uses a framework for innovation that is problem-oriented and emphasises workable solutions that encourage cooperation between healthcare professionals and IoT developers. The study measures gains in operational throughput, response time, and data correctness using simulated performance datasets and Python-based predictive modelling. The results highlight how preventative treatment, allocation of resources, and overall clinical effectiveness are all greatly improved by real-time IoT integration.

Title: Fine-Tuning Wav2Vec2 for Low-Resource Kichwa Automatic Speech Recognition
Abstract: In recent years, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly accelerated the development of natural language processing and automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for high-resource languages, raising concerns about the marginalization of ancestral and underrepresented languages. In this context, this work explores the fine-tuning of the Wav2Vec 2.0 model, developed by Meta AI, for ASR in Kichwa-a low-resource language spoken in the Ecuadorian Andes. The training process utilized two datasets totaling approximately 8 hours of audio, segmented into clips ranging from 1.5 to 5 seconds, with manually aligned transcriptions created using ELAN software. Fine-tuning was performed using the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss function. After multiple experiments, a two-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test revealed no statistically significant improvement when applying SpecAugment. The best-performing model, trained without data augmentation, achieved promising results on the test set: a Word Error Rate (WER) of 0.262, a Character Error Rate (CER) of 0.120, and a Match Error Rate (MER) of 0.401. These findings d emonstrate the viability of adapting pre-trained self-supervised models to low-resource settings and underscore the potential of ASR technologies to support greater linguistic inclusivity in artificial intelligence.

Title: Speech-GAN: Black-Box Attack against Automatic Speech Recognition Systems
Abstract: Today, most Automatic Speech Recognition systems rely on Deep Learning to convert human speech to text and interpretable commands. However, such systems can be deceived by specially crafted adversarial audios, misleading them to incorrect audio transcriptions, and exposing technologies using these systems to security flaws. Hence, knowing the weaknesses of these systems is crucial if they are to be used in safety-critical and security-sensitive applications. In this work, we present Speech-GAN, a Generative Adversarial Network that aims at creating adversarial audios deceiving Deep Learning-based Automatic Speech Recognition models in a black-box setting, without drastically altering the audio quality. With a success rate of 100%, and signal-to-noise ratios averaging -9.47 dB, our black-box untargeted attack is experimentally validated on a Wav2Vec2.0 Automatic Speech Recognition model, for 1,000 audio samples spanning 10 command words.

Title: Hybrid model using both LSTM and attention mechanism along with emotion and genre embeddings for recommendation of songs
Abstract: This research models a better neural network, combining sequential data together with categorical variables like genre and emotion into a model to predict which songs will popularize. The model incorporated an attention mechanism that pays more attention to the most important segments of the input sequence, along with LSTM layers that can record temporal dependencies in song metadata. Since the embedded feature vectors of emotion and genre data could well compactly represent meaningful concepts, we can predict the composite song success score much more accurately by bringing them together. Using an extensive song dataset, we measure its effectiveness and even get documentable gains in precision and applicability over typical models. In fact, the performance metrics of Mean Squared Error, R<sup>2</sup> score, ROC curve, and Precision-Recall curve indicate how reliable the method is. Then, we proceed to success predictions specified for specific genres, revealing the versatility of the model in musical style identification. This fresh combination of LSTM, attention, and embeddings presents a powerful method to predict song popularity and also infer interesting components driving music success.

Title: Multimodal Multilingual Translation System with Text, Voice, and Visual Outputs
Abstract: As the world becomes more globalized, multilingual communication interfaces are a necessity to bridge language differences across various fields of study like education, tourism, and access. This paper introduces a multilingual translation model that can take in text and voice inputs and output the result as translated text, synthesized speech, and a visual representation thereof. The model is built using the Facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M, supporting more than 200 languages, with performance and accessibility at its core. The approach combines auto language detection from the langdetect library, text-to-speech (TTS) conversion from Google TTS, and speech-to-text (STT) functionality from Whisper tiny/base models with low-latency audio processing. For graphical representation, Stable Diffusion XL is used to produce images consistent with the translated text. To make the model efficient, quantization and FP16 precision are used, which greatly accelerates inference speed and allows hardware with low memory resources to deploy the model. A translation memory with the previous five translations and a secure login authorization system enhance usability even further. In this project, we are also developing a user-friendly interface that enables easy interaction with the system, permitting users to enter queries and obtain outputs in multiple modalities with ease. The innovation in the system is the integration of multimodal output (image, audio, text) with an optimized translation framework and user-friendly UI, providing quick, precise, and scalable results for real-world use. It is a leap ahead in accessible, human-oriented translation technology, which can be made feasible for various communication requirements all over the world.

Title: A Decoupled Biophysically-Inspired Architecture for Speech Enhancement
Abstract: The aim of biophysically-inspired speech enhancement models is to replicate the robustness of the human auditory system. However, these models often fall short due to being computationally expensive or monolithic "black box"systems. This paper introduces d-CoSE, a decoupled architecture that separates the biophysical auditory feature enhancement and waveform synthesis tasks, which are implicitly coupled within its monolithic predecessor. To demonstrate the advantages of this architectural change, the proposed system is systematically compared against the original CoSE framework. The decoupled design enables advanced training strategies, such as a hybrid loss function and a final fine-tuning stage, which are not possible in a coupled model, allowing the d-CoSE system to surpass the baseline in perceptual quality (PESQ 2.42 vs 2.33). The results validate the decoupled approach, showing the architectural separation provides inherent benefits of modularity, transparency and potential for superior performance.

Title: Benchmarking Wav2Vec and Traditional Speech Recognition in Speech Transcription
Abstract: This study presents an empirical benchmarking comparison of two distinct speech-to-text approaches under identical conditions: the Speech Recognition module, which utilizes the online Google Web Speech API, and the offline Wav2Vec model developed by Facebook AI. Both approaches facilitate the transformation of spoken language into written language, although they demonstrate unique characteristics in terms of reliance on the internet, speed, and precision. This study utilizes the LJ Speech dataset, which contains short audio segments of a single reader supplemented by their corresponding transcriptions. Both examined models acquire text from the identical dataset and subsequently assess its similarity to the texts within the dataset. Our analysis reveals that wav2vec outperforms the speech recognition model in both accuracy and performance, suggesting the use of wav2vec in speech-to-speech implementations.

Title: Automatic Code-switched Academic Tunisian Arabic Speech Recognition
Abstract: Aiming to support researchers by answering their questions, this paper presents the first module of a virtual assistant for Tunisian Arabic (TA): Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Given the specialized lexicon used, which is characterized by a high rate of Code-Switching (CS), our primary objective is to create a new dataset, Tunacad, tailored to this context. Tunacad comprises 1 2. 5 6 hours of CS spontaneous speech in the academic domain. Additionally, we experiment with our proposed CS corpus on predefined ASR models, Whisper and Wav2vec2-XLR-S. To enhance ASR performance on our corpus, we apply several techniques, such as automatic orthographic correction, normalization, and prompt-based correction. Additionally, we incorporate human evaluation to assess transcription quality beyond surface-level accuracy. Through these experiments and CS errors analysis statistics, we highlight the persistent challenges in processing TA speech.

Title: Multilingual Audio-Based Depression Detection using Audio Augmentation and Data Efficient Image Transformer
Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that speech analysis is increasingly being utilized as an objective biomarker in artificial intelligence (AI) applications designed to complement clinical assessments, improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment response monitoring, enhance healthcare quality, facilitate remote patient monitoring, and reduce the cost and time associated with the assessment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). This study employs audio augmentation techniques including pitch shifting, time shifting, and noise addition to address the issue of data imbalance between Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Healthy Control (HC) labels identified in previous research. To mitigate this imbalance, oversampling is applied to the MDD class, which contains fewer samples than the HC class. The augmented data are then used to train two variations of the DeiT model, namely deit-base-patch16-224 and deit-small-patch16-224. Both models achieved an accuracy of approximately 70 percent across the training, validation, and testing phases. Although the deit-small-patch16-224 exhibited slightly lower accuracy compared to the deit-base-patch16-224 model, this performance was attained with only half the training time required by the deit-base-patch16-224. Furthermore, the proposed framework, which incorporates audio augmentation techniques, outperforms prior related studies by achieving a 14.82 percent performance improvement.

Title: Noise-Robust Speaker Verification With Attenuated Speech Restoration and Consistency Training
Abstract: Even though the performance of speaker verification (SV) has been significantly improved with deep learning approaches, it may degrade severely in the presence of background noises. Simple approaches to relieve this issue would be multi-condition training (MCT) and adopting a speech enhancement (SE) module as a pre-processor. However, whether joint-trained with the SV module or not, the SE module may occasionally incur speech attenuation which leads to the partial loss of speaker information. To address this problem, in this paper, we propose a noise-robust SV system with the SE front-end incorporating a speech restoration module using lost information aggregation and consistency training. In the speech restoration module, the lost information obtained from the noisy and enhanced latent representations processed with different sizes of the receptive field is aggregated to produce restored speech features using a loss function penalizing speech attenuation. Moreover, to further improve the robustness to the background noises and unseen data, we adopt consistency training to make the speaker embeddings for the noisy speech similar to those for the clean speech obtained by a pre-trained SV model. Our experimental results demonstrated that the proposed system significantly improved the performance of the speaker verification for the VoxCeleb dataset mixed with environmental noises, and exhibited the generalization capability in the experiment on the CHiME-4 dataset.

Title: THE ROLE OF GENERATIVE AI CHATBOTS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A STUDENT-CENTRIC CONCEPTUAL ANALYSIS OF BENEFITS, ETHICS, AND PRIVACY CONCERNS
Abstract: Generative AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, are reshaping higher education by offering personalized tutoring, administrative support, and enhanced research capabilities, while simultaneously raising ethical and privacy concerns. This study examines their role from a student-centered perspective, focusing on benefits, risks, and institutional implications. A pilot study was carried out with 300 undergraduate students and 120 faculty members from five European universities. Participants engaged in semi-structured interviews, perception surveys, and controlled academic tasks designed to evaluate chatbot performance. Instruments included standardized student satisfaction questionnaires, expert review rubrics, and quantitative performance metrics (perplexity, response latency, context window, SWE-bench accuracy). Data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, ANOVA tests, and thematic coding of interviews. Results reveal that ChatGPT and Claude achieved the best balance between pedagogical clarity and privacy compliance, while Gemini excelled in technical capacity but showed weaker ethical safeguards. Student satisfaction was strongly associated with transparency in data policies and pedagogical usefulness rather than raw technical performance. These findings highlight the need for universities to adopt generative AI technologies under robust ethical and privacy frameworks. Future research should extend this pilot into longitudinal studies and institutional case analyses.

Title: Cross-Platform Speaker Diarization: Evaluating the Scalability and Flexibility of Maleo
Abstract: Maleo is a cutting-edge, cross-platform speaker diarization system that integrates advancements in speech processing and machine learning. This paper details Maleo's architecture and evaluates its performance. The system's purpose is to provide a flexible and scalable diarization solution deployable across diverse hardware. The methodology involves a pipeline beginning with audio processing (PCM Mono 16-bit 16kHz conversion) to standardize input. The standardized audio is then analyzed using two core models: Whisper for times-tamped speech recognition and Pyannote for neural network-based speaker segmentation. The combined model is exported into the ONNX format to ensure compatibility across CPU, GPU, and WebGPU environments. The system's performance was evaluated on 10 diverse audio files from the VoxConverse dataset. The results show an average diarization error rate (DER) of 9.217% and an average Jaccard error rate (JER) of 24.982%. This study highlights Maleo's ability to overcome diarization challenges by showcasing its efficiency, adaptability, and ability to function optimally in varied computing environments, presenting a practical solution for real-world applications.

Title: Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithms for Solving the Multi-class Classification Problem of Liver Damage Stages
Abstract: This comprehensive methodology leveraging hybrid machine learning is proposed for the processing of incomplete medical datasets and the prediction of concurrent liver fibrosis (F1-F4) and steatosis (S1-S4). The core of our contribution is a three-stage system combining hybrid imputation (KNN+MICE), PLS-neural network-based factor analysis for identifying significant biomarkers (ALT, AST, bilirubin), and an optimized Voting classifier ensemble (SVM, RF, k-NN) with automatic weight tuning, yielding an F1-score of 0.96. Experimental validation on 104 patient records confirmed a statistically significant performance advantage over isolated methods, with a 15.9% increase in accuracy (p<0.05). The practical relevance of this research is embodied in a high-precision diagnostic instrument with an interactive web interface, designed for seamless clinical deployment and forming a foundation for unified clinical decision support systems in hepatology.

Title: Detecting AI-Generated Music: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models
Abstract: The rapid evolution of deepfake music has emerged as a significant challenge for musicians and the music industry. Generative models such as Suno and Juno can produce highly realistic AI-generated music that closely mimics the style and voice of real artists, making it difficult for human listeners to distinguish between synthetic and authentic compositions. This capability raises serious legal and ethical concerns. In response, numerous studies have explored deep learning approaches for deepfake music detection. The primary objective of this study is to examine the limitations of current detection models and evaluate the performance of three deep learning architectures: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Audio Spectrogram Transformers (AST), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM). A balanced dataset comprising 10,000 AI-generated songs and 10,000 human-composed songs from YouTube was collected. These were segmented into approximately 700,000 five-second mel spectrogram segments for training and evaluation. All three models achieved strong performance, each attaining an F1-score, precision and recall of 1.0, suggesting potential dataset simplicity or overfitting. Among the models, CNN recorded the lowest final test loss (0.07%) and the highest test accuracy (99.7%), outperforming AST and BiLSTM in terms of convergence and generalization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of deep learning in detecting AI-generated music, while also emphasizing the importance of addressing potential data leakage, enhancing dataset complexity, and conducting real-world validations to ensure robust and reliable model deployment.
