Title: A Comparative Evaluation of Speech Separation Models on Multi-Speaker Child Speech Recordings
Abstract: The task of separating overlapping sounds, known as the cocktail party problem, becomes even more challenging when applied to children's voices, which have higher acoustic variability and spontaneous articulation. While deep learning-based models such as Conv-TasNet, DCCRN, DPRNN, and SepFormer have demonstrated strong performance on adult voice data, their robustness to children's voices remains rarely explored. In this study, we present a comparative evaluation of four speech separation models using a specialised dataset constructed from overlapping recordings of elementary school children speaking. These models were pre-trained using the LibriMix dataset with noise from WHAM! and then fine-tuned on synthesised child voice mixes. Evaluations were conducted using real classroom recordings involving two to five simultaneous speakers. The SI-SNRi metric was used as the primary measure, complemented by qualitative analysis using spectrograms and waveforms. Our results show that SepFormer consistently outperforms the other models, achieving up to 14.1 dB SI-SNRi with two speakers and maintaining 9.4 dB with five speakers, followed by DPRNN (13.2-8.5 dB). Conv-TasNet and DCCRN performed lower, particularly under heavy overlap. Qualitative observations confirm that the transformer-based architecture provides better harmonic reconstruction capabilities and temporal accuracy in the context of child speech. These findings emphasise the importance of long-term modelling for speech separation tasks in educational settings and real-world applications for children.

Title: Multichannel Speech Enhancement Method Using Dilated Semi-Dense Convolutional Network
Abstract: This paper proposes a dilated semi-dense convolutional network for multichannel speech enhancement using machine learning. The baseline, SpatialNet, employs a Conformer for narrowband processing but uses a simple 3-layer CNN block, limiting local information extraction. To improve performance, we replace the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) block with dilated convolution, dilated dense convolution, and the proposed dilated semi-dense convolution.

Title: AI-Based Primary Schools Teachers' Professional Competency Assessment Tool
Abstract: In the era of Industrial Revolution 5.0 and digital transformation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is known to play a crucial role in improving the effectiveness and efficiency of education, specifically in public and private elementary schools where teachers greatly influenced students' learning experiences. Therefore, the present research focused on developing an assessment tool to measure teachers' performance driven by AI. Professional competency centered on three dimensions, technical, pedagogical, and ethical. The use of a quantitative method was due to the presence of 150 elementary teachers from public and private schools in Yogyakarta, selected through cluster random sampling. Title: Development of a Lightweight Spatio-Temporal Attention Network for Visual Speech Recognition
Abstract: Visual speech recognition (VSR) aims to translate silent lip movements into spoken words. Although various approaches have been proposed to enhance accurate VSR systems, two major challenges hinder their extensive practical use. Firstly, deep learning-based VSR models often rely on complex network architectures, resulting in substantial computational and memory demands, which lead to prolong processing times. Secondly, the presence of lip-movement homophones, where distinct words exhibit similar visual lip patterns, may result in misclassifications. To address these issues, this study presents an innovative lightweight VSR model designed to balance between recognition accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed model employs a 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) for capturing short-term spatio-temporal features, followed by a sequence of lightweight residual blocks inspired by ResNet to enhance spatial representation. We incorporate stacked Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to capture the temporal dynamics of lip movements across video frames, while an attention-based aggregation mechanism selectively emphasizes the most informative temporal features. This hybrid design substantially reduces the number of parameters and inference time with competitive performance. Experiments conducted on two challenging subsets derived from the LRW dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves top accuracy scores of 84% and 74%, respectively, comparable to baseline models.

Title: Enhancing Emergency Communication with SDR Based PMR Capture and Speech Recognition
Abstract: Personal mobile radio (PMR) systems are often used in disaster relief and remote operations where other communications networks are unavailable. While reliable, these systems only support live voice communications and do not provide logging, search capabilities or automatic alerts. This paper describes a monitoring framework that combines software-defined radio technology, digital signal processing with GNU Radio, and speech recognition to transcribe and analyze all sixteen channels in the 446 MHz band. The system is implemented on an embedded Nvidia Jetson Orin platform and is capable of generating transcribed speech, speech records, and alerts when predefined keywords are detected. To evaluate performance, a dataset was created that simulated speech with static and ambient noise. From the evaluation, a keyword detection rate of 0.98 with an average delay of 1.82 seconds was obtained, demonstrating the feasibility of implementing monitoring capabilities to PMR radio systems using artificial intelligence and software defined radio technologies.

Title: CGNOS: A Deep Learning enabled Chronic Kidney Disease Detection based on Convolutional Gene Network Optimization Strategy
Abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a progressive and potentially fatal condition that necessitates early and accurate diagnosis to prevent end-stage renal failure. In this study, we propose CGNOS (Convolutional Gene Network Optimization Strategy), a novel deep learning-based framework for the automated detection of CKD. The model integrates structured clinical parameters with genomic biomarkers, forming a multi-dimensional input tensor modeled as a gene-feature interaction network. A convolutional neural network (CNN) combined with attention mechanisms is used to work with this hybrid structure to reveal prevailing patterns and correlations in patient data. An optimization module implemented using Genetic Algorithms (GNOS) is also added in order to dynamically choose the subset of informative features, maximizing the classification accuracy and computational speed. The CGNOS model is tested on CKD data set available at Kaggle, and compared with classical machine learning approaches including SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and simple CNNs. The peak accuracy of the proposed model reached 98.6% compared to the baseline models such as CNN (94.2%), Random Forest (93.1%), and SVM (91.5%). Further performance indicators that show the stability of CGNOS are the precision (98.1%), recall (99.0%), and F1-score (98.5%). Moreover, feature set size was also considerably minimized to 14 by the aid of the feature subset optimization without sacrificing the diagnostic performance that was originally 25. Such findings show that CGNOS can not only facilitate more accurate diagnoses but it can demonstrate enhanced interpretability and scalability toward real-world adoption in clinical practice. The combination of gene expression profiling and clinical characteristics provides a instrument in early screening of CKD and thus more direct and individual treatment techniques.

Title: Analysis of Pitch-Shift Effects on Self-Supervised Speech Representations
Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have led to the success of self-supervised learning (SSL) in speech processing for extracting robust representations. However, the specific acoustic information captured by different SSL models remains unclear. This paper analyzes how SSL features from HuBERT, WavLM, and ContentVec are affected by average pitch variations often caused by the difference of gender, speaker, and emotion. For the future improvement of the performance of speech synthesis applications including voice conversion and speech control, we quantitatively and visually analyze features before and after high-fidelity pitch shifting to discuss the robustness of these SSL representations to pitch variations.

Title: Integrating ASTERI-Based EEG Imaging with Deep Learning and Swarm Intelligence for Autism Diagnosis Support
Abstract: The enhancement of instruments for the early diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is of crucial importance for the efficacy of interventions. This study proposes an approach that uses Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) in the pre-processing of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals and decreasing the number of electrodes in the signal gathering to optimize the biomarkers mapping. Furthermore, deep neural networks (DNN), swarm intelligence, and signal-to-image (STI) conversion techniques are applied to enhance the classification and interpretation of EEG data. The findings have shown that Random Forest classifiers with 4000 and 500 trees achieved the best average results in the reduced and original bases, respectively. In approach 1, the performance was maintained even using only 28.8% of attributes after the particle swarm optimization (PSO). In approach 2, the accuracy was found to be 78.1% and the area under the curve (AUC) was 0.879 with all the attributes. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pre-processing and attribute reduction strategies, ensuring an efficient solution for the early diagnosis of ASD with operational excellence and lower computational cost.

Title: Convolutional Neural Network Optimization Using Particle Swarm Optimization for Hijaiyah Letter Voice Recognition with MFCC Feature Extraction
Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) for Hijaiyah letters in Arabic faces unique challenges due to phonetic complexity, subtle acoustic variations among the 28 different letters, and the need for highly accurate classification. Conventional deep learning approaches often rely on manual hyperparameter tuning, which is not only time-consuming but also risks producing suboptimal models. Additionally, feature extraction methods such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), though effective, require the appropriate network architecture to achieve optimal performance. To address these issues, this study proposes optimizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to enhance the accuracy of Hijaiyah letter speech recognition. The PSO algorithm was applied to explore 110 combinations of hyperparameters, including learning rate, number of filters, and kernel size, to find the optimal configuration. MFCC features were extracted from audio samples and used as input for the optimized CNN architecture. Experimental results show that the PSO-optimized model achieved an accuracy of 94.12%, precision of 94.39%, recall of 94.12%, and F1-score of 94.07%, representing an improvement of 0.14% in accuracy and 0.11% in F1-score compared to the baseline model (without PSO optimization). The optimal hyperparameters obtained are a learning rate of 0.008705, 128 filters, and a kernel size of 3×3. These findings prove that the integration of PSO and CNN significantly improves the performance and stability of the model in Hijaiyah letter recognition, while offering an efficient solution to the problem of deep learning architecture optimization.

Title: Dual-Feature Ensemble Deep Learning Architecture for Robust Spoofing Speech Detection
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a spoofing speech detection method using a deep learning model based on a dual-feature ensemble. The threat of spoofing speech attacks has increased with the advancements in speech synthesis and voice conversion technologies. This highlights the need for highly accurate spoofing speech detection methods. Our proposed method leverages information extracted from waveforms and mel spectrograms to enhance the robustness of spoofing speech detection. By combining a state-of-the-art spoofing detection technique with a high-performing model from sound-related tasks, we aim to develop a robust system for spoofing speech detection. Evaluation experiments using the ASVspoof 2021 dataset show that the proposed model outperforms conventional methods, including the wav2vec2.0 + AASIST baseline. Our experimental results suggest that the proposed method captures various characteristics of speech from multiple angles, thereby improving the generalization performance of the model.

Title: LLM-Based Dysarthric Communication Aid with Text and Voice Output
Abstract: Speech recognition technology still does not meet the needs of a majority of people who suffer from dysarthria. Existing systems provide transcripts that end up being broken and disjointed and grammatically flawed and unable to convey speaker intended meaning. Such systems regard transcription as the end of the conversation process rather than the beginning points for understanding. This paper comes up with a new assistive system that employs post-processing to build meaning in an intelligent way. The system's core works on FLAN-T5-Large that acts as a robust language model to reason about contextual information and semantic relations. The system works through three interdependent steps: the initial step utilizes a Whisper ASR model specifically trained on dysarthric speech to translate audio into raw text. The language model then applies this text to create meaningful fluent language that mirrors what the speaker wished to say. The last part of the system employs a Text-to-Speech synthesizer to transcribe the corrected text into natural and expressive speech output. The system converts disfluent input into comprehensible expression to enable people with dysarthria to communicate fluently.

Title: Evaluation of Noise Filtering Techniques for Speech Emotion Recognition in Educational Environment
Abstract: The growing demand for intelligent systems in education, coupled with the need to understand students' emotional states, has highlighted the importance of efficient and scalable emotion recognition solutions. Traditional approaches, such as facial expression analysis and paper-based questionnaires, are often time-consuming and prone to inaccuracies. This study presents a speech emotion recognition (SER) system that classifies emotions from speech signals, with a focus on addressing the impact of noise on classification performance. To enhance audio quality prior to classification, three filtering techniques, namely Butterworth bandpass, FIR, and adaptive LMS filtering were applied. Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) were extracted as input features for deep learning-based classifiers. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The proposed approach aims to improve the robustness of SER systems in noisy, real-world educational environments. The best performance was achieved using the CNN-BiLSTM model with Butterworth filtering, reaching an accuracy of 93.50%, which is a 0.82% improvement over the baseline accuracy of 92.68%.

Title: Music Genre Classification Using Multilayer Perceptron: A Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Music genre classification is an important task in digital library organization, and is beneficial to recommender systems. In this work, we explore the possible use of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) to solve genre classification tasks using audio features as input, such as MFCCs, chroma features, and spectral contrast, among others, and signal processing approaches such as STFT, Mel spectrograms, and spectral rolloff. The proposed model also outperformed the traditional classifiers such as KNN, SVM, and Random Forest when tested on the GTZAN dataset with a test accuracy of 92.19% and a validation accuracy of 92.22%. Experiments demonstrate that the lightweight neural models, such as MLP, can achieve comparable performance with deeper CNN/RNN architectures and have computational advantages in scenarios of real-world applications, e.g., automated genre tagging, personalized recommendations, and content curation in music streaming platforms.

Title: Evolution of Transformers in Speech Recognition
Abstract: By outperforming conventional Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in terms of accuracy and efficiency, Transformer-based architectures have completely transformed Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). Standard Transformer models, however, suffer from latency problems, memory limitations, and computational bottlenecks. The Conformer, Transformer-XL, Transformer Transducer (T-T), Multi-Channel Transformers, and Diagonal State Space (DSS) Augmented Transformers are some of the major architectural advancements in transformer-based ASR that are examined in this paper. This paper examines how these changes solve ASR issues while improving performance, scalability, and efficiency, and making real-time ASR more feasible. This paper also outlines future research directions in low-latency, energy-efficient ASR models and discusses open problems in hardware optimization, multimodal ASR, and self-supervised learning.

Title: Dynamic Temporal Cross-Modal Attention for Early Parkinson's Disease Detection using Voice and Spiral Drawing Data
Abstract: Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor and vocal impairments. This paper presents a novel multimodal deep learning framework for PD classification that integrates hand-drawn spiral analysis and voice signal processing. We introduce a Dynamic Temporal Cross-Modal Attention (DTCMA) mechanism designed to capture time-aligned degradation patterns across two heterogeneous biomedical modalities: spiral drawing images and voice recordings represented in CSV format. Voice features, including jitter, shimmer, and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), are segmented into temporal sequences using sliding windows, while spiral drawings are reconstructed into stroke-level time-series capturing tremor, velocity, and pressure dynamics. The proposed DTCMA employs bidirectional gated recurrent units (Bi-GRUs) and stage-adaptive attention weights informed by Hoehn & Yahr scale embeddings. Our approach demonstrates superior classification performance compared to traditional late-fusion and static attention models, particularly in early-stage PD detection. Additionally, we integrate Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to uncover cross-modal biomarker interactions, enhancing model transparency for clinical decision support. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to apply cross-modal temporal attention to the fusion of voice CSV features and spiral drawing image data for personalized and interpretable PD diagnosis

Title: MovieRecNet: A Multi-Source Deep Learning Model for Personalized Movie Recommendations
Abstract: This research introduces MovieRecNet: A Multi-Source Deep Learning Model for Personalized Movie Recommendations, developed to address the shortcomings of conventional recommendation systems. Traditional models often depend only on ratings or metadata, making them less effective in dynamic, real-world scenarios. MovieRecNet goes further by integrating six complementary data sources: user- item interactions, movie metadata, aspect-based user sentiments, social media discussions, contextual factors, and external signals. The key advantages of MovieRecNet lie in its ability to capture holistic user preferences and adapt to real-time trends. By including sentiment analysis, the system aligns recommendations with emotional responses such as appreciation for story, acting, or music. Social media integration ensures responsiveness to sudden shifts in public interest, while contextual modeling reflects patterns like weekend viewing or regional preferences. External signals such as awards and box office performance enhance recommendation quality by incorporating credibility and popularity factors. Together, these components provide robustness against cold-start issues for new users and movies, improve diversity by recommending beyond mainstream titles, and increase fairness through balanced coverage. Evaluations demonstrate that MovieRecNet achieves higher Precision@K, NDCG, and sentiment alignment compared to baseline systems, establishing it as a comprehensive and adaptive framework for next-generation movie recommendations.

Title: AI-Assisted Music Therapy Intervention for Alleviating Exam Anxiety in University Students: System Design, Implementation, and Efficacy Evaluation
Abstract: Exam anxiety is a prevalent concern among university students, adversely affecting their academic performance, mental health, and overall well-being. This study investigates the efficacy of an AI-assisted music therapy intervention specifically designed to alleviate anxiety during exam periods. We conducted a single-blind randomized controlled trial involving 150 participants, wherein the intervention group received personalized music playlists generated in real-time based on facial emotion recognition data. In contrast, the control group engaged in passive listening to pre-defined playlists that lacked personalization. The primary outcome was assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) scale, which participants completed both before and after the intervention. Statistical analysis revealed a significant reduction in GAD-7 scores for the intervention group (Mean: 6.0, SD: 2.4) compared to the control group (Mean: 11.5, SD: 2.2), resulting in a large effect size (Cohen's d=1.9). Participants in the intervention group also reported enhanced emotional engagement and satisfaction during their sessions. These findings suggest that AI-assisted music therapy is not only effective in reducing exam anxiety but also highlights the potential for using technology to create personalized therapeutic experiences. This innovative approach can be an important contribution to mental health strategies aimed at supporting students during critical academic periods, paving the way for future research in the field of digital therapeutics.

Title: Fairness-Aware Deep Learning Model for Covid19 Detection from Cough Audio Recordings
Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified the demand for rapid, accessible diagnostic methods. Machine learning models using cough audio recordings have shown potential for remote COVID-19 detection but often exhibit performance disparities across demographic and clinical subgroups. This study investigates fairness-aware machine learning models for COVID-19 diagnosis using crowdsourced data from the COVID-19 Sounds dataset. A Random Forest and a VGGish-based deep neural network classifier were developed. To mitigate bias, four different methods were applied and comparatively evaluated, namely correlation remover as a pre-processing approach, exponentiated gradient and adversarial debiasing as in-processing approaches, and threshold optimizer as a post-processing approach. Evaluation across sensitive attributes including gender, age, recording device's operating system, and the intersection of age and gender revealed that fairness could be substantially improved with minimal loss in predictive accuracy. The best equalized odds ratio values were 0.956,0.998, and 0.88 with respect to gender, age, and recording device's operating system, respectively. Similarly, for the combination of gender and age the corresponding metric was 0.804. These findings support the feasibility of fair and reliable audio-based diagnostic systems, emphasizing the importance of integrating fairness into clinical machine learning pipelines.

Title: Real-Time Fall Detection Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: Falls that occur among elderly adults or individuals with mobility challenges may provide certain health hazards. Due to this, effective fall detection systems need to be designed that are accurate and real-time. The classic methods of fall detection are threshold-based methods and rule-based methods that are less suited to diverse environments and generate too many false alarms. To improve on these disadvantages, this research develops a deep learning-based hybrid model employing CNN and LSTM networks to obtain increased fall detection performance. This model integrates both vision-based data and sensor-based data; it learns on benchmarks. This boosts the detection rate. The experiments prove that the suggested CNN-LSTM model is superior in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The model's accuracy reaches 96.4 % and also has substantially lower false positive and false negative rates than state-of-the-art ones. The comparison with 3D-CNN, Bi-LSTM, and Hybrid DNN models indicated that our system excels in real-time latency and robustness in various situations. The proposed system can be used for geriatric monitoring, smart health care systems, and autonomous emergency response. However, the study has several drawbacks, such as being computationally expensive and requiring big and diverse datasets to generalize properly. Future studies will work on merging several types of sensors, learning capabilities, and edge-based computers so as to shorten real-time detection. The outcomes of this research can help in the design of AI-based medical instruments that are safer for sensitive parts.

Title: MixedG2P-T5: G2P-Free Speech Synthesis for Mixed-Script Texts Using Speech Self-Supervised Learning and Language Model
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to voice synthesis that can substitute the traditional grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion by using a deep learning-based model that generates discrete tokens directly from speech. Utilizing a pretrained voice SSL model, we train a T5 encoder to produce pseudo-language labels from mixed-script texts (e.g., containing Kanji and Kana). This method eliminates the need for manual phonetic transcription, reducing costs and enhancing scalability, especially for large non-transcribed audio datasets. Our model matches the performance of conventional G2P-based text-tospeech systems and is capable of synthesizing speech that retains natural linguistic and paralinguistic features, such as accents and intonations.

Title: Dementia Prediction From Speech Signal Using Optimized Prosodic Features
Abstract: Early detection of dementia, a general term for cognitive decline, is vital for enhancing patient care and management. Conventional clinical assessments and cognitive tests require expert clinicians and are time-consuming. Therefore, developing rapid and reliable in-house detection methods is highly desirable. Prior studies have identified speech-based early markers of dementia, motivating the application of machine learning for automated detection. This study investigates the effectiveness of optimized prosodic features, with a focus on pause-related metrics, for dementia classification. Experimental evaluation of 15 selected features shows that pause and formant features are the most discriminative, achieving improved classification performance over the original 45-feature set. These findings suggest that concise, targeted feature sets can enhance automated speech-based dementia detection.

Title: Retinex-Fusion: A Novel Paradigm for Ultra-Low Light Image Enhancement
Abstract: This study presents a robust algorithm for low-light image enhancement, specifically designed to address unevenly illuminated images. The proposed method integrates several key techniques, including denoising, multi-scale Retinex, power-law (gamma) transformation, and illumination estimation and correction through color balancing. Following these stages, a multi-scale pyramidal fusion approach is employed to fuse intermediate images with their respective weight maps derived from contrast, saturation, well-exposedness, dark channel, and entropy information. The performance of the proposed framework is evaluated using the LOw-Light (LOL) dataset, which comprises extremely dark images for testing purposes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses several state-of-the-art techniques, outper-forming many machine learning-based approaches in both no-reference and full-reference image quality metrics. These findings suggest that the method holds significant promise for applications in surveillance, medical imaging, and smartphone-based imaging systems.

Title: End-To-End Multi-Channel Speaker Extraction and Binaural Speech Synthesis
Abstract: Speech clarity and spatial audio immersion are the two most critical factors in enhancing remote conferencing experiences. Existing methods are often limited: either due to the lack of spatial information when using only one microphone, or because their performance is highly dependent on the accuracy of direction-of-arrival estimation when using microphone array. To overcome this issue, we introduce an end-to-end deep learning framework that has the capacity of mapping multi-channel noisy and reverberant signals to clean and spatialized binaural speech directly. This framework unifies source extraction, noise suppression, and binaural rendering into one network. In this framework, a novel magnitude-weighted interaural level difference loss function is proposed that aims to improve the accuracy of spatial rendering. Extensive evaluations show that our method outperforms established baselines in terms of both speech quality and spatial fidelity.

Title: A Comprehensive Review of Infant Cry Audio Signal Analysis and Recognition using Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract: This paper reviews recent research on interpreting and classifying infant cry signals, focusing on data collection, machine learning methods, and signal processing techniques. Since crying is a baby's main form of communication, accurate interpretation is essential to identify needs such as hunger, discomfort, or illness. Challenges include noise, variability, and limited labeled data. The review highlights current approaches and their limitations, aiming to guide the development of reliable cry-based monitoring systems. This paper looks at how newly built Neural Network (NN) architectures are used in newborn cry research. It also looks at how preprocessing, feature extraction (e.g., Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Spectrograms), and classification using algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) are currently done. They evaluate recent advancements, highlighting both the achievements and shortcomings of data collection, tagging, and model performance. This project aims to focus future research on creating a reliable, real-time infant monitoring system to assist caretakers and healthcare providers in making urgent choices.

Title: Bidirectional ASL Communication Platform using Whisper Ai and Real-Time Gesture-to-Speech and Speech-to-Gesture Conversion
Abstract: Bridging the communication gap between hearing-impaired individuals and non-signers remains a critical challenge in inclusive technology. This paper presents a real-time, bidirectional communication platform that translates between American Sign Language (ASL) gestures and spoken English. The system integrates a gesture-to-speech module using MediaPipe and a Random Forest classifier trained on ASL alphabet data, alongside a speech-to-gesture module powered by OpenAI's Whisper AI for robust speech transcription. Recognized text is matched to corresponding ASL gestures using a predefined dictionary and displayed through an interactive interface developed with Streamlit. The platform achieves 94.7% accuracy in gesture recognition and 96% speech transcription accuracy in quiet environments, with end-to-end latency ranging from 1.3 to 1.8 seconds. Unlike traditional one-way assistive tools, this system supports real-time two-way communication, making it suitable for use in education, healthcare, and public service settings. The results demonstrate the feasibility of combining AI-driven speech and vision models in a practical, scalable solution for accessible communication.

Title: Augmented Transfer Learning for Synthetic Speech Detection
Abstract: Speech synthesis models pose significant risks, as modern text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) systems can generate highly realistic synthetic voices that can be exploited for fraud, impersonation, or disinformation. In this paper, we focus on a single, highly effective transfer learning solution: a pretrained EfficientNetV2 backbone model using augmented spectrogram inputs. We employed and evaluated a suite of spectrogram augmentation techniques (adaptive resizing, SpecAugment, and Mixup), regularization methods (dropout, stochastic depth, label smoothing, selective layer freezing), as well as a progressive resizing approach and optimization and learning rate strategies. For the Fake-or-Real (FoR) dataset, a reference benchmark in the field, comprising speech samples both genuine and generated by modern TTS/VC models, our system achieves 97.2% validation accuracy and 91.1% test accuracy, surpassing prior performance by up to 19.6%, reducing the generalization gap, and indicating that focused augmentation on a single pretrained network yields state-of-the-art performance with minimal complexity increase.

Title: CRUSE-cMGAN: a Conditional Metric GAN Framework for Real-Time Speech Enhancement Algorithms
Abstract: Denoising speech signals can be a difficult task especially if the background noise is non-stationary. Deep Neural Network (DNN) models provide an excellent performance in speech enhancement, yet they require a substantial computational effort during the inference process, as well as an enormous data basis. We propose a novel approach to optimize real-time supervised learning algorithms semi-supervised by adding a discriminator to the optimization process as well as a non-feature based objective function with phase awareness. We use a Convolutional Recurrent U-net for Speech Enhancement (CRUSE) to build up a conditional generative adversarial training framework. To reduce the computational complexity we train the generator exclusively on the magnitude spectrum and the metric discriminator returns the influence of the disturbed phase. Our findings show that CRUSE-cMGAN outperforms the existing supervised trained CRUSE based on the same architecture. Furthermore the semi-supervised learning manner allows a reduced training database for the optimization process. Experimental results are provided to prove the advantages of the conditional metric GAN framework.

Title: AI Heart Sound Denoising at the Edge
Abstract: Cardiac auscultation with a digital stethoscope is an important method for early diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), especially in resource-constrained settings. However, its utility is often impaired by unwanted noise (e.g., lung sounds, ambient speech) obscuring critical heart signals in the recordings. This paper addresses the challenge of denoising heart sounds in noisy environments and performing this processing on-device for minimal delay and improved data privacy and security. We propose a deep learning-based denoising method using U-Nets based on the Spleeter architecture, which separates heart sound signals from noise in the time-frequency domain. The models are implemented on two edge computing platforms-a Raspberry Pi 4 B and a Qualcomm RB3 Gen 2-demonstrating the feasibility of AI-driven heart sound denoising at the edge. We further optimize the models via quantization to Int8 precision to leverage the RB3 Gen 2's neural processing unit (NPU) for acceleration. Experimental results show that the denoisers achieve significant enhancement in signal quality, with each yielding an average improvement in scale-invariant signal-To-distortion ratio (SI-SDR) exceeding 10 dB. The edge deployment meets real-Time constraints, with the quantized model on the RB3 Gen 2 executing denoising substantially faster (at least 17 times faster than the Raspberry Pi implementation) and at lower power compared to the full-precision model, all without appreciable loss in denoising performance-0.06 dB being the largest drop. These results demonstrate the potential of deploying advanced AI denoising on edge devices for immediate, on-device heart sound denoising.

Title: Generalization in Audio Deepfake Detection: Evaluating ASR Encoder-Based Feature Extraction
Abstract: Audio deepfakes are artificially generated audio recordings that are used to create inauthentic imitations of a person's utterances. In the context of the increasing utilisation of artificial intelligence, the recognition of these recordings is becoming increasingly important. Thereby, the generalization of the detectors is a major challenge in audio deepfake detection (ADD). We analysed six feature representations: MFCC, LFCC, Wav2Vec2.0 and three pre-Trained encoders of automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems (Whisper, SpeechT5, Canary) for ADD. For evaluating their generalizability, we trained the models on the ASVspoof 2019 LA train set and tested on the in-The-wild (ITW) test set. Furthermore, we evaluated the training time of the models, analysed the effect of additional (newer) training data and performed a correlation analysis. The ASR encoders were outperformed by using simple MFCC features, achieving an EER of 17.96% on the ITW test set with the lowest training time (7 min. per epoch). The best results were calculated using Wav2Vec 2.0 (+MFCC) with an EER of 17.60%, but using additional training data, and a training time of 135 min. per epoch. Wav2Vec also showed the highest correlations in varying training settings, indicating the best predictability of the model's performance.

Title: EEG-based envisioned speech recognition system using spectral graph wavelet transform
Abstract: This paper presents a new framework for the recognition of envisioned speech from electroencephalogram (EEG) signal. The proposed framework consists of preprocessing for dividing the signals into blocks, spectral graph wavelet transform (SGWT), feature smoothing using the moving average filter, and classifiers (extra trees (ET), random forest (RF), and k-nearest neighbors (KNN)) for identifying three tasks such as digits, characters, and objects. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a publicly available database which consists of three classification tasks namely, digits, characters, and objects tasks. The SGWT-based method with ET classifier had the highest accuracies of 92.4%, 92.7%, and 92.3% for digits, character, and objects tasks, respectively that outperforms other SGWT-based methods using the RF and KNN. Evaluation results show that the class-wise accuracies are better than the state-of-the-art methodologies. The proposed EEG-based framework for recognition of envisioned speech can enable seamless brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for communication of people having speech impairments and can control the devices using envisioned speech in human-machine interaction (HCI) applications.

Title: Diff-DEQ: Differentiable Dynamic Equalization for Studio-Quality Speech Processing
Abstract: We present Differentiable Dynamic Equalization (Diff-DEQ), a fully differentiable deep learning framework for speech equalization and enhancement to achieve studio quality for audio post-production tasks. Unlike fixed-rule equalization methods, it adapts spectral components dynamically, responding to input signal variations to attain precise and content-aware spectral shaping. The model combines a FiLM-modulated Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) to predict per-band equalization parameters with audio feature-based conditioning for improved adaptability. We have trained the model in a self-supervised manner that eliminates the need for paired input-target data. We evaluate its performance using objective metrics on Diff-DEQ and parametric equalization (PEQ) across LibriTTS, DAPS, and VCTK datasets and non-intrusive speech quality assessment for subjective evaluation. Our results show that Diff-DEQ enhances speech intelligibility and perceived quality, making it well-suited for audio post-production.

Title: Exploiting Neural Audio Codecs for Edge-to-Gateway Speech Processing
Abstract: Neural Audio Codecs have become powerful tools for audio processing, offering learnable compression methods that balance high compression ratios with perceptual quality. This paper introduces a signal processing system that utilizes the latent space of Neural Audio Codecs for signal reconstruction and feature extraction in edge computing environments. We design a lightweight NAC encoder inspired by SoundStream, optimized for resource-constrained devices. Our evaluation on speech recognition and classification tasks highlights the system’s adaptability to Internet of Things applications. The proposed design achieves a 40× audio waveform compression with only a 3% increase in word error rate for transcription tasks and a 94.6% accuracy on end-to-end intent classification, demonstrating its practicality for real-world deployment. Additionally, the encoder operates at a real-time factor of 1.77 on an ARM Cortex-A53 using a single thread for intra/inter-operation, ensuring efficient real-time compression and 12-8 times less energy consumption compared to the original model encoder.

Title: Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
Abstract: A key element of speech processing systems, Voice Activity Detection (VAD) facilitates efficient speaker identification, efficient communication, and accurate speech recognition. Conventional methods, such as statistical and energy-based models, suffer from human interference and exhibit suboptimal performance under noisy conditions. Supplied with labeled datasets, supervised deep learning methods typically exhibit superior performance but rely heavily on labeled datasets, which are time-consuming and costly to acquire. Deep learning and unsupervised machine learning methods, therefore, have surfaced as viable alternatives to overcome these issues. This paper reviews some of the unsupervised VAD methods that are resilient to labeled data but exhibit outstanding performance, such as clustering, self-supervised learning, and autoencoder-based architectures. A comprehensive review of literature further illustrates recent trends, open research issues, and challenges such as domain adaptability, noise robustness, and real-time processing constraints. Discussion on future directions, such as incorporating transformer-based architectures and multimodal learning for more efficient VAD, is presented in the concluding part of the study.

Title: Always-on Hyperdimensional Heartbeats
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to phonocardiogram (PCG) signal classification using hyperdimensional computing (HDC) with hybrid feature extraction and Sobol-based hypervector encoding. Our method transforms heart sound signals into high-dimensional hypervectors by extracting key audio features, such as Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), zero-crossing rate (ZCR), spectral contrast, and chroma features, followed by quantization and encoding into highdimensional space. The resulting hypervectors are then classified using multi-centroid class representations, generated via k-means clustering, and evaluated through cosine similarity. Our approach achieves rapid inference, robust noise tolerance, and lower computational complexity compared to traditional machine learning methods. The hybrid feature encoding technique effectively captures both spectral and temporal characteristics of PCG signals, enhancing classification accuracy and consistency. We evaluate our model's performance using confusion matrices, inference time analysis, and energy efficiency estimation on a 3W TinyML embedded device. Our refined classifier demonstrates an overall accuracy of 83%, with an average inference time of 1.15 ms per sample, and energy consumption as low as 0.0035 Joules per classification. These results emphasize the potential of our HDC-based approach for reliable, real-time, and low-power diagnostic applications in embedded and wearable biomedical devices.

Title: Leverage Sub-Band and Cross-Band Information in Real-Time Speech Signal Improvement
Abstract: Sub-band and cross-band information have proven beneficial in improving high-resolution characteristics for speech separation and enhancement tasks. Nevertheless, the extraction of high-resolution features frequently results in significant computing complexity, which contradicts the low-complexity demands of real-Time systems. To address this difficulty, conventional methodologies often employ an autoencoder design that compresses frequency data to diminish computing demands and encapsulates global information within the bottleneck. Nonetheless, these models frequently neglect the significance of sub-band and cross-band parameters in speech signal processing. To overcome this issue, we offer a real-Time model that efficiently utilizes both sub-band and cross-band information at high resolution, while adhering to the autoencoder architecture to meet real-Time requirements. The suggested model demonstrates exceptional performance across multiple speech quality metrics, attaining a SIG score of 3.49 and an OVRL score of 3.01 on the blind test set of the ICASSP 2024 Speech Signal Improvement Challenge, with a real-Time factor (RTF) of 0.30.

Title: Deepfake Voice Detection: Countering Deepfake Audio with Deep Learning Architectures
Abstract: The active development of the Text-to-Speech (TTS) technology as well as the Voice Conversion (VC) has posed an outstanding danger to the digital security. To overcome this obstacle, this paper will compare and contrast systematically three different deep learning structures, a hybrid CNN-RNN framework that aims to conduct both spectral and temporal artifact processing, a CNN-LSTM ensemble framework exploring the distinctive capabilities of the spatial and temporal processing, and a state-of-the-art system with Wav2Vec2 as a pre-trained feature extractor and as a Light Convolutional Neural Network (LCNN) to make predictions. Although all these architectures operate on the basis of known elements, they are new in the way that they specifically aim at deepfake detection and also they are assessed and evaluated in an unprecedented way in parallel. With experiments on a wide variety of benchmark datasets, such as ASVspoof 2019, WaveFake and FoR, this paper compares the trade-offs between feature-engineered and self-supervised methods. As the results show, CNN + LSTM-based platform can deliver better results, its analysis accuracy is 99.81, because it is able to get deep, context-sensitive representations of unprocessed audio. The present study highlights the symbiosis of organizing various deep learning techniques and establishes a complete reference in future studies in resilient equipment of deepfake voice detecting.

Title: AI Driven Lip-Reading System for Assistive Communication
Abstract: The potential of new assistive communication systems has been made possible by deep learning models' enhanced performance efficiency and precise lip-reading capabilities. People who have speech impairments use traditional communication methods which operate both slowly and with limited accessibility to produce ineffective communication outcomes. The research developed a deep learning system to convert spoken lip movements into audible voice signals for speech communication with people who have speech problems. The LipNet model architecture provides processing of silent video inputs through its Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) which perform feature extraction and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for sequence prediction through Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). Natural language processing technologies facilitate the text processing modules which identify both errors along with suitable contextual terms to generate precise and understandable transcriptions. The method shows remarkable potential to transform speech conversion into a faster and more accessible system that delivers accurate contextual results.

Title: Data Augmentation Methods for Music Removal from Environmental Sounds Based on Machine Learning
Abstract: With the rapid growth of video-sharing platforms and social networking services in recent years, video posting has become increasingly active. When videos include copyrighted music, it is necessary to remove the music in accordance with copyright regulations. Traditionally, music removal has been performed using speech enhancement and signal processingbased source separation methods. However, speech enhancement tends to unintentionally remove non-Target sounds, while signal processing-based source separation requires selecting the target sound to be removed for each case. To overcome these issues, a deep learning-based music removal method has been proposed that neither eliminates speech audio nor requires manual target selection. Nevertheless, its removal accuracy remains insufficient, likely due to the limited quantity of available training music data. A promising solution is to apply data augmentation to improve performance. Although data augmentation techniques have been developed for other audio domains, no suitable method for music data has been proposed. Therefore, in this study, we propose a data augmentation approach using pitch shifting, evaluating music removal performance for each pitch scale under the twelve-Tone equal temperament, and examining appropriate pitch shifting values and applicable ranges.

Title: Towards Robust and Secure Speaker Verification Against Synthesis and Converted Speech Attacks
Abstract: The detection of spoofed audio from bonafide has become a critical task to ensure the reliability of automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems. Ensuring robustness ASV systems requires effective detection of spoofed speech generated through advanced voice conversion techniques. Spoofed data used in this work came from voice conversion (VC) and text-to-speech (TTS) techniques. This study evaluates the performance of SVM, GMM-UBM, CNN, and LSTM models on bonafide speech as well as spoofed data created using Grad-TTS and Seed-VC in both pretrained and finetuned configurations. The experimental results demonstrate that deep learning models, particularly CNN and LSTM, consistently achieve higher accuracy rates across all spoofing scenarios compared to traditional models such as SVM and GMM-UBM. While pretrained and finetuned models of Grad-TTS and Seed-VC exhibit varying degrees of spoofing effectiveness, CNN and LSTM maintain resilience with accuracies approaching 100%. This work points out the creation of spoofed data from voice conversion and speech synthesis techniques and the importance of detecting the spoofed data to build the resilient speaker verification systems.

Title: Deep Learning-Driven Audio Sentiment Analysis for Security and Threat Detection
Abstract: Online verbal abuse and offensive content present significant challenges to maintaining a safe digital environment. Automated detection and classification of harmful speech can enhance community safety by identifying abusive interactions in real-time. This study explores an AI-powered web application that detects verbal abuse in audio content, incorporating advanced language modeling approaches, such as sentiment analysis and keyword detection, to improve Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) performance. The system comprises three key components: text processing, offensive language detection, and notification mechanisms. It converts spoken content into text, analyzes words for offensive language, and automatically sends email alerts to relevant au-thorities when sensitive content is detected. This approach fosters healthier and more inclusive online inter-actions by proactively mitigating risks and reducing exposure to harmful content. Future advancements may include multilingual support, contextual awareness, and adaptive learning models to enhance detection accuracy across diverse communication platforms.

Title: Tailored Voice Activation for Enhanced Accessibility
Abstract: Speech recognition technology has revolutionized human-computer interaction by enabling seamless voice-based communication. Title: Research on the Status Monitoring Method of Nuclear Power Plant Speakers Based on Internet of Things and AI Technology
Abstract: The plant-wide broadcasting system in nuclear power plants plays a vital role in daily operations and emergency management, serving as an indispensable communication tool for issuing alerts, notifying personnel, and directing evacuations. However, the extensive distribution of loudspeakers across complex environments has long posed challenges for manual inspections, often leading to delayed fault detection that compromises information delivery and creates safety risks. Systematic speaker failures remain a key barrier to effective broadcast communication. The core objective of this research is to develop automated monitoring systems for loudspeaker operations, enabling timely identification of malfunctioning units. This ensures reliable and accurate message transmission to target audiences during routine operations, major maintenance, and emergency evacuation scenarios. This research integrates nuclear power industry information technology with acoustic monitoring expertise, leveraging rapidly evolving wireless communication technologies and the digital transformation trends in the sector. We propose an IoT and AI-based Speaker status monitoring system that constructs a distributed data collection network, designs standardized test sound sources, and employs advanced sound event detection, voiceprint similarity calculation, and Automatic Speech Recognitions to automatically assess speaker performance. The system evaluates operational status through comprehensive algorithm scoring. Analysis from wireless communication, safety redundancy, and algorithm robustness perspectives demonstrates its feasibility and effectiveness in real plant environments. Key innovations include: developing adaptive monitoring modules for high-noise, high-radiation conditions in nuclear plants; enhancing fault detection accuracy through multimodel fusion; and exploring predictive maintenance extensions via digital twin and edge computing concepts. This study not only provides engineering foundations for intelligent monitoring of nuclear power plant broadcast systems but also offers valuable references for health management of industrial acoustic equipment.

Title: Multilingual ASR for Indic Languages Using OpenAI's Whisper
Abstract: Speech-to-text technology has witnessed remarkable advancements with the advent of deep learning models such as OpenAI Whisper. However, developing speech recognition and translation systems for Indian languages poses challenges due to linguistic diversity, varying accents, and limited resources. This paper presents a web-based multilingual Speech-to-Text (STT) and translation application that operates without the need for API keys, enabling offline processing for major Indian languages. The application integrates automatic speech recognition (ASR) using the Whisper model and provides seamless translation between languages such as Telugu, Hindi, and English. We discuss system architecture, language model optimization, preprocessing techniques, and interface design to ensure accurate and efficient transcription and translation. This solution improves accessibility and usability, particularly in low-resource settings, empowering users to perform speech-to-text and translation tasks effectively.

Title: Explainable AI for Cardiorenal Insights: Linking ECG Features to Kidney Function Decline in a Heart Failure Cohort
Abstract: The pathological pathways involved in the cardiorenal syndrome remains unknown and more research is needed to uncover this relationship. Here, we investigate the correlation of electrocardiogram (ECG) features in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients with renal function measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) We used the Sudden Cardiac Death in Chronic Heart Failure (MUSIC) data from Physionet database, to classify CHF patients into two classes (eGFR < 66 and eGFR > 66). Different machine learning (ML) models were employed, among which, the logistic regression (LR) model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an accuracy of 69.35%, a sensitivity of 70.71%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.752. Furthermore, explainable ML analysis revealed that Minimum RR Interval (RRI), QRS Duration, RR Range, and corrected (QTc) were identified as significant predictors of eGFR classes. These results pave the way for understanding the cardiorenal syndrome.

Title: Heart Failure Hospitalization Risk Models Predict Mortality Among Heart Failure Patients and Other Groups at Risk
Abstract: Machine learning based early risk assessment and prognosis prediction of Heart Failure (HF) are beneficial for disease management, but challenging due to the limited availability of large survival datasets. In this paper, we study whether models originally trained to predict the risk of HF hospitalization can be repurposed to estimate mortality. We hypothesize a relationship between hospitalization and mortality risks based on the progressive nature of HF that could be leveraged to unlock data limitations. Using our previously developed models based on 30-second lead I ECG and basic patient information, we evaluate their performance in predicting mortality in multiple cohorts: HF patients in the MUSIC dataset with additional insights into the cause of death and left ventricular ejection fraction, as well as other risk groups in the SaMi-Trop and CODE-15% datasets. Our results demonstrate that our HF hospitalization models are capable of effectively stratifying mortality risk among different populations.

Title: Ensemble Machine Learning-Based Approach to Predict Human Mental States with Optimized Feature Selection and Data Balancing
Abstract: The quality of life is greatly impacted by mental health illnesses worldwide, making sophisticated diagnostic instruments that strike a compromise between precision and interpretability necessary. This paper uses the DASS-42 dataset (n = 39,775) to predict stress, anxiety, and depression using a unique machine learning architecture that uses a stacking ensemble of k-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, and Multi-Layer Perceptron. In order to solve class imbalance and guarantee robust feature scaling, the model incorporates Yeo-Johnson transformations, Min-Max normalization, and NRS Boundary-SMOTE for data balancing. Grid Search and Nested Cross-Validation are used to maximize hyperparameter tuning, resulting in 99.94% (depression), 99.92% (anxiety), and 99.92% (stress) accuracy. The framework bridges the gap between predictive capacity and transparency, making it a dependable tool for clinical mental health evaluations due to its high accuracy and interpretability. This method offers a scalable, reliable solution for mental health diagnostics and advances AI-driven psychological treatments, opening the door for early diagnosis and individualized therapy.

Title: An Artificial Intelligence and Genetic Algorithm Optimized Biosensor System for Real-Time Detection of Environmental Toxins and Their Biomedical Impact: A Natural Science Driven Approach to Sustainable Public Health Monitoring
Abstract: The environmental pollution is turning environment-unfriendly, and food safety, and human health are endangered threateningly, and most of the established monitoring systems are not sensitive, adaptive, and capable of real-time analysis to offer such level of protection to the people. This paper describes a biosensor based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based optimization to monitor major environmental poisons in real time and evaluate their possible biomedical effects. An electrochemical and optical transduction-based multimodal biosensing platform was developed to detect heavy metals (Pb2+, Cd2+), organophosphate pesticides and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). With the aim of increasing analytical accuracy, a hybrid AI system, which includes convolutional neural networks (CNNs), along with feature extraction, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which retrieve temporal prediction of toxins, was trained on 8,450 datasets of biosensor signals. The optimization of the model hyperparameters, calibration curves and receptor-analyte affinity thresholds was refined using GA. The optimized system was able to accomplish a 97.8 percent toxin classification efficiency, 94.6 percent prediction accuracy and 21 percent better sensitivity sight as compared with conventional biosensor systems. Simultaneously, a biomedical impact module was created that calculated the biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokine probabilities and toxin toxicity pathways. The field tests showed strong real-time functionality with less than 1.6 Second latency, which proved field-testing with the example that permits continuous monitoring coverage of the environment. On the whole, the findings indicate that the hybrid of AI analytics and GA optimization can be used to boost the performance of biosensors to a considerable extent and allow observing environmental toxins on a large scale and in the long-run. The suggested system will present an effective instrument of environmental risks preventive, food quality, and timely anticipation of health effects, toxins.

Title: MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORKS FOR AI-INTEGRATED CREATIVE INDUSTRIES
Abstract: Implementing Artificial Intelligence (AI) into creative sectors is a radical change of how art, media, and design systems work. This study suggests an overall management system that integrates AI-based innovation with conventional creative processes. The paper starts with an account of the history of management paradigms in the field of creativity, with a particular focus on the digital transformation and computational creativity as the factors that transformed the way of how organizations are run. The analysis of literature provides a solid understanding of the models of AI integration that are available to date, and there are gaps in governance, ethical implementation, and interdisciplinary cooperation. The study applies the mixed-method design, i.e., the qualitative data offered by industry participants and quantitative evaluation of the performance of the AI-based workflow, to meet the requirements of the empirical rigor and the reliability of the framework. The framework suggested has two structural levels: strategic levels, which cover governance, innovation and collaboration, and operational levels, which cover automation, co-creation and content optimization. These aspects are created to accommodate adaptability management practices that promote creativity without sacrificing humanism. The case studies of implementation in the areas of media, advertising, design, and music industry already reveal the levels of variable AI maturity, providing a comparative insight into the area of scalability and efficiency.

Title: Adaptive Slimming for Scalable and Efficient Speech Enhancement
Abstract: Speech enhancement (SE) enables robust speech recognition, real-time communication, hearing aids, and other applications where speech quality is crucial. However, deploying such systems on resource-constrained devices involves choosing a static trade-off between performance and computational efficiency. In this paper, we introduce dynamic slimming to DEMUCS, a popular SE architecture, making it scalable and input-adaptive. Slimming lets the model operate at different utilization factors (UF), each corresponding to a different performance/efficiency trade-off, effectively mimicking multiple model sizes without the extra storage costs. In addition, a router subnet, trained end-to-end with the backbone, determines the optimal UF for the current input. Thus, the system saves resources by adaptively selecting smaller UFs when additional complexity is unnecessary. We show that our solution is Pareto-optimal against individual UFs, confirming the benefits of dynamic routing. When training the proposed dynamically-slimmable model to use 10 % of its capacity on average, we obtain the same or better speech quality as the equivalent static 25 % utilization while reducing MACs by 29 %.<sup>1</sup>

Title: Leveraging Linguistic Sciences and Artificial Intelligence to Correct Qur’anic Recitation: The Al-Fatihah application for Indonesians as a model
Abstract: The world is witnessing rapid advancements in artificial intelligence technologies, while non-Arabic speakers continue to face substantial difficulties in pronouncing Arabic phonemes and reciting the Qur’an accurately. This paper explores a technological approach and a practical model that addresses these challenges by integrating linguistic sciences with artificial intelligence. The study examines an Al-Fātiḥah correction application developed specifically for Indonesian learners by the Saudi educational company Bajdah, which serves as the case study for this research. The paper aims to examine the integration of artificial intelligence and the operational mechanisms underlying this technology. The system functions by having the user record their voice, converting the audio input into digital data, and comparing it to an ideal model recitation. It subsequently provides feedback on pronunciation errors, enabling the learner to adjust and refine their recitation. The paper outlines the advantages of this learning approach, including its self-paced accessibility at any time and from any location, immediate evaluation that helps learners identify both strengths and weaknesses, the ability to re-record and undergo repeated assessment, and the issuance of a certificate of proficiency in Al-Fātiḥah. The study reveals that this application constitutes a pioneering initiative that brings together linguistic sciences and artificial intelligence tools to support Qur’anic instruction for non-Arabic speakers. It demonstrates that artificial intelligence is not merely a technological instrument but rather a comprehensive epistemic framework, one that enables the application to continuously learn and improve its performance through natural language processing and automatic speech recognition technologies.

Title: Utilising generative AI to assist in the creation and production of Chinese popular music
Abstract: Background: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has had a significant impact on the music industry, particularly Chinese popular music (C-pop), which presents unique difficulties due to its distinctive melodic structures and emotional depth. While AI can boost efficiency and inspire composers, current models are ineffective in feature selection and prediction accuracy, leading to compositions without stylistic integrity and commercial viability. Problem Statement: Current AI-generated melodies often lack the stylistic depth of human compositions and fail to predict market success accurately. These challenges highlight the need for a more effective AI framework capable of generating high-quality melodies. Objectives: This study introduces the GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm. This generative AI-driven technique uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to create melodies inspired by Chinese pop songs and forecasts their success. The main goals are to build an AI pipeline for music preprocessing, improve feature selection, train a deep learning model for stylistically consistent melodies, and compare its effectiveness to other methods. Methodology: The methodology utilises a GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm, which contains data preprocessing techniques such as mode and mean imputation, label encoding, and Min-Max scaling. Feature selection is improved using the Hybrid Filter-Wrapper Ensemble (HFWE) method, which combines Mutual Information, Chi-Square Test, ANOVA F-Test, and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), with the final subset determined by majority voting. The selected features, like melody structure, key signature, tempo, rhythm complexity, instrumentation, and emotion, are used as inputs for an LSTM-based deep learning model that comprises multiple LSTM layers, dropout layers to prevent overfitting, and a dense output layer to create melodies and forecast their commercial success. Results: Performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1- score, and Matthew’s correlation coefficient (MCC) provides better results with the GenAI Melody-LSTM algorithm, with 89.7% accuracy, 87.5% precision, 88.2% recall, an F1-score of 87.8%, and an MCC of 0.82. Conclusion: This research demonstrates that integrating generative AI, optimal feature selection, and deep learning significantly enhances Chinese pop music compositions. The LSTM-based model generates melodies and predicts their commercial viability, enabling composers to fine-tune AI-generated music for improved quality and market appeal.

Title: Evaluating the Impact of Strategic Alignment on Performance Components of Iranian Pharmaceutical Companies Using Machine Learning Techniques
Abstract: Background: Sustainable performance in the pharmaceutical industry hinges on the strategic alignment of human resources (HR), marketing, and information technology (IT). Prior studies often examined these domains separately; evidence on their joint influence in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector remains limited. Objectives: To assess how HR, marketing, and IT strategic alignment relate to profitability, liquidity, and revenue growth using machine-learning methods, and to document model generalization and measurement validity. Methods: This applied, cross-sectional study surveyed 323 managers in Tehran Stock Exchange (TSE)-listed pharmaceutical firms (May to Nov, 2024). A validated questionnaire [CVI/CVR; EFA/ confirmatory factor analysis (CFA); reliability reported] was used only to construct composite indices of HR, marketing, and IT alignment; organizational performance outcomes, profitability, liquidity, and revenue growth (year-over-year) were computed from audited financial statements and then z-standardized. Inputs were min-max scaled to [0, 1]. Title: MACHINE LEARNING AND NLP IN ASSESSING TERRITORIAL DIFFERENCES IN SOCIAL WELL-BEING: A COMBINED ANALYSIS OF SURVEY DATA AND VKONTAK TE DIGITAL TR ACES
Abstract: This article uses a combined analysis of survey data and VKontakte digital traces to examine territorial differences in the social well-being of St. Petersburg residents. Employing the sociology of emotions as its analytical framework, the study uses machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) methods as its core instruments. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was used to identify key domains of urban everyday life, and an ensemble of sentiment-analysis models classified over half a million comments into five basic emotional categories. The survey data captured subjective evaluations of the urban environment and residents’ emotional reactions, while the digital traces revealed situational and collective forms of emotional expression. The findings show that differences in social well-being consistently emerge at the intersection of district-specific infrastructure, housing quality, demographic structure and everyday mobility patterns. Social media data refine and extend insights from surveys by revealing localised points of tension, such as infrastructure failures, 'growing pains' in rapidly developing districts, and chronic everyday inconveniences characteristic of older neighbourhoods. The study demonstrates that combining survey methods with AI-based text analysis enables social well-being to be viewed as a dynamic process sensitive to changes in the urban environment, rather than a static indicator. The results have practical implications for urban social policy and for diagnosing territorial inequalities.

Title: Mobile Cloud Computing and AI Use in Education
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Cloud Computing stand as the most mentionable advancements in technology which has profoundly impacted healthcare. The advantages include but are not limited to, rapid expansion, effective resource distribution, low operational costs, and invaluable data processing services. This study examines the effect of the combination of the cloud computing technology and AI on education with the advent of smartphones. As mobile technologies become more predominant in daily activities, they have transformed into necessary teaching instruments that facilitate learning by providing uninterrupted access to educational materials. Many mobile applications in education now rely on cloud platforms, such as Google Cloud and Apple iCloud, to deliver real-time services. In parallel, AI is leveraged to personalize learning experiences, automate administrative tasks, support intelligent tutoring systems, and enable data-driven decision making in educational institutions. Implementing AI algorithms has ensured improved student participation and performance by using advanced analytics on enormous sets of educational datasets capabilities to change content to suit users' unique preferences. The widespread use of mobile devices combined with AI and cloud capabilities has led to the creation of mobile cloud computing (MCC), a new paradigm that improves educational delivery systems. The MCC empowers institutions to manage academic data efficiently while enabling students and educators to interact with learning materials anytime and anywhere. This study investigated how cloud computing and AI jointly reshape the educational environment, driving the evolution of smarter and more adaptive digital learning systems.

Title: Sequence-to-Sequence Voice Conversion With Weighted Guided Attention
Abstract: Voice conversion (VC) using non-autoregressive sequence-to-sequence (S2S) models has gained attention in recent years. Compared with conventional framewise VC models, these S2S VC models can control features, such as prosody and speech speed, and enable high-quality and fast conversion. In S2S VC, the accuracy of alignment between source and target speakers strongly affects conversion performance. In this paper, we propose EdenVC and WSAS-VC using attention-based alignment. EdenVC simply introduces a diagonal-guided weighting initially proposed in EdenTTS, while WSAS-VC integrates the attention weights and those based on the alignment path obtained from the monotonic alignment search. We evaluate the conventional MAS-VC, EdenVC, and WSAS-VC using two types of speaker conversion conditions, from native to native speech and from non-native to native speech. Experimental results show that WSAS-VC achieves more stable training than EdenVC and better conversion accuracy than MAS-VC.

Title: Rating the Experiencing Scale with generative AI: examining the accuracy, reliability, and feasibility of ChatGPT
Abstract: In recent years, psychotherapy research has seen increasing interest in the application of generative AI, accompanied by advances in natural language understanding. The Experiencing Scale (EXP Scale) is a valuable instrument for evaluating psychotherapeutic processes and outcomes, but ratings require specialized training and time, posing challenges for large-scale analysis. Generative AI may offer a solution. This study examined the accuracy, reliability, and feasibility of EXP Scale ratings using ChatGPT (GPT-4o and OpenAI o1). Both seven-stage ratings and a simplified three-stage version (Low, Middle, High) were evaluated against expert ratings (primarily based on Klein et al., 1970). As a result, high agreement was observed in the three-stage ratings, suggesting potential utility as a screening tool for identifying Stage 4 and above, a critical turning point in psychotherapy. Although the seven-stage ratings often misclassified Stages 1 and 6 and lacked sufficient accuracy, they generally aligned with expert ratings. Therefore, improvements in prompts and models may enhance rating precision. Additionally, a supplemental evaluation of Japanese segments demonstrated performance comparable to or exceeding that of the English segments. Despite its limitations, generative AI’s ability to rate much faster than humans suggests its potential as a valuable adjunct to psychotherapy research and clinical practice.

Title: A Transducer-adaptive Denoising Model for Medical Ultrasound Imaging
Abstract: Ultrasound imaging is a pivotal diagnostic tool in medical practice due to its non-invasive nature, low cost, and real-time imaging capabilities. However, the images are often affected by various types of noise, significantly degrading image quality and hindering accurate diagnosis. Traditional filtering methods struggle to preserve fine image details, while machine learning and deep learning-based models often lack adaptability to different ultrasound instruments and transducer configurations. To address these challenges, we propose a novel deep learning-based ultrasound image denoising model. Our model uses a multi-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) structure to configure metadata based on sensor configuration Center Frequency, Element Kerf, Element Width, and Imaging Depth adaptively adjusts the noise level and denoising intensity, effectively suppressing speckle noise and preserving texture details in images from different ultrasound instruments. It is trained and evaluated primarily on ultrasound images synthesized using Coherent Plane Wave Compounding (CPWC), chosen for its standardized and reproducible framework. Despite being trained on CPWC data, our model demonstrates competitive denoising performance for non-CPWC-based ultrasound images, attributing to the shared physical factors influencing speckle generation. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing denoising methods, with average SSIM, PSNR and EI values increased by 1.67%, 1.28% and 1.04%, respectively. Additionally, when applied to real breast ultrasound images, our denoising method achieves state-of-the-art results in downstream image classification tasks, significantly improving both accuracy and AUC values. This study holds practical significance in enhancing the quality of ultrasound images for improved clinical diagnosis.
